jobs.title: AI Software Developer (m/f/d)
jobs.description:
Hey, we’re Sunlab—nice for you to drop by.
Are you a passionate developer who no longer writes a line of code by hand? Do you know how to integrate AI tools sensibly into workflows, solve complex problems and turn ideas into working applications?
Perfect. That is what we are looking for!
At Sunlab, we combine performance marketing with technology. Our in-house development develops individual tools, intelligent automations and technical solutions that optimize processes and make everyday work easier.
Artificial intelligence merges with our DNA. Whether in the terminal or OpenCode, Visual Studio Code, etc., our stack is currently based on Claude, OpenAI and a local LLM (Nvidia Spark).
To further our mission, we look for you as
AI Software Developer (m/f/d).
Your area of responsibility
- Agentic Coding: You use LLMs to efficiently develop high-quality code, extend existing applications and implement new features without writing code by hand.
- From prompt to product: You turn requirements and ideas into working applications. You use AI specifically for architecture, implementation, debugging, refactoring and testing.
- Intelligent Automation: Identify processes that can be automated with AI and code and develop pragmatic, scalable solutions.
- AI integration: You integrate LLMs and matching APIs into existing systems and develop intelligent assistants, data-driven tools or automated workflows, for example.
- Quality instead of blind trust: You check AI-generated code, detect vulnerabilities and make sure your solutions are performant, maintainable and secure.
- Think tech stack further: You test new AI tools and development approaches, evaluate their practical benefits and bring the best solutions into our everyday work.
- Share know-how: Together with our tech team, you will develop new standards for AI-enabled software development and help make the entire team more efficient.
Your background
- You have completed studies in computer science, business informatics, software engineering or a comparable discipline with a sound IT and AI focus and can independently write clean, functioning code – regardless of whether you use AI or develop classically.
- You already actively use AI coding tools and know how to use them for more complex development tasks.
- You are familiar with at least one relevant programming language, such as .NET/C#, Rust, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, PHP or a similar language.
- APIs, databases, Git and basic software architecture are not foreign words for you.
- You understand that AI-generated code is not automatically good code and can critically review, test and improve results.
- You want to try out new technologies, quickly learn about unknown topics and independently advance solutions.
- You think pragmatically, work in a structured way and have a high demand on your work.
- You have reliable knowledge of German and English in writing and in both languages and can safely exchange information on technical topics and explain complex issues in an understandable way.
Your benefits
- Hybrid working with flexible office days
- All-round supply in the top modern headquarters on the Bavarian submain, fitness room, gaming room on over 1,600 sqm and more.
- Flat hierarchies & short decision paths
- Strong onboarding, regular training and conferences
So, apply today and work alongside us to get our customers into pole position. We look forward to meeting you soon.
Julia and the Sunlab team
PS: You can also simply call us at 06021 4228997.

jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, AI Platform
jobs.description:
We are looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to join the AI Platform Team at Smartly! Our team works on helping marketers make the most of their ad creatives (images, video, text) and campaigns (product and performance data). We build and experiment with AI-based solutions across the media and creative workflows.You will have the opportunity to take ownership of and work on high impact projects.
Join us in building high impact ML-based solutions to help our customers to build better and more effective advertising experiences for their consumers. If you’re a growth minded individual who has a passion for ML and the marketing space, this team is for you!
As a Senior Machine Learning Engineer, you’ll:
- Build ML-based software systems that enable our users to craft great advertising experiences and campaigns
- Work with a large span of datasets from image to video to audio to text to structured performance data.
- Contribute to and strengthen Smartly’s MLOps + data platform. You’ll work alongside our stellar senior machine learning engineers, data scientists, and software engineers to enable us to productionize AI/ML applications more robustly and efficiently.
- Be a core contributor of our team and our ways of working to build high impact products. You’ll actively be involved in work planning, retrospectives, and overall team improvement.
- Impact the daily life of the staff of the hundreds of advertisers using Smartly
- Work with our stakeholders - be them product, engineering, infrastructure - to ensure we meet customers where they are. As with most ML-related roles, being able to translate business/product needs to viable solutions is a must.
- Apply and enhance your soft skills through working closely with your colleagues and our customers. Doing knowledge shares, running productive meetings, and pair programming/debugging are just some ways we grow our soft skills.
- Keep up to date with the latest ML innovations, especially in areas such as generative AI, computer vision, natural language processing and explainability.
What we are looking for:
- 5+ years of experience developing and deploying production-quality software
- 2+ years of experience delivering software services powered by machine learning
- 2+ years of experience working with cloud infrastructure such as AWS or GCP
- Fluent in Python; experience with C++ or Java is a plus
- Hands-on experience with modern ML frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow)
- Knowledge of MLOps concepts and tools (e.g., MLflow, Kubeflow)
- Experience in feature engineering, model evaluation, diagnostics, and monitoring
- Strong foundation in linear algebra, statistics, and calculus
- Experience building scalable data pipelines for ML-based data processing
- Experience developing and maintaining services under SLA
- Analytical mindset with a problem-solving approach
- Passion for solving customer challenges quickly while making thoughtful architectural decisions
- Adaptability and resilience when facing new or ambiguous challenges
- Strong written and verbal communication skills in English
- M.Sc. in a relevant field is preferred
- Ability and willingness to work in a hybrid capacity from our office 3 days a week
What We Offer You
At Smartly, we offer a place where you can advance your career. Here, you'll find:
An Inclusive Global Culture: Join a team of over 750 Smartlies, representing more than 60 nationalities across 24 locations in 13 countries. We cultivate a culture built on trust, transparency, and open feedback, where diverse perspectives are valued and encouraged.
Global Impact: Contribute to a company making a global impact, directly influencing our customers' success and business growth.
Focus on Wellbeing: We prioritize your health with healthcare packages, mental health services, and a commitment to work-life balance through paid holidays and family leave.
Comprehensive Rewards: Benefit from equity options, performance-based rewards, competitive compensation, and career development opportunities.
Flexible Hybrid Workplace: Experience a hybrid work model, balancing office collaboration with remote work, and the option to work abroad for up to 30 days annually.
Apply Now and Build Your Future with Smartly!
Curious what it’s like to work at Smartly? Visit our Careers page to see how we grow, collaborate, and make impact together
About Smartly
Smartly is the AI-powered advertising technology company transforming ad experiences for brands and their consumers. Our comprehensive advertising platform seamlessly integrates the capabilities of media, creative, and intelligence to power more than 800 billion impressions and generate more than 300 billion creatives annually, delivering tangible business outcomes for brands and advertisers.
Smartly is the only company in the industry recognized as a Leader in The Forrester Wave: Creative Advertising Technologies with PwC validating the results it delivers for brands. We manage creative and media for 700+ brands worldwide and $6B in ad spend across the largest media platforms, including Facebook, Google, Instagram, Pinterest, Snap, and TikTok. Our end-to-end technology, unmatched access to media platforms and exceptional customer service help Fortune 500 brands to reach and engage consumers and learn what performs best.Smartly is a multinational and diverse team of 750+ Smartlies from 60+ nationalities, working in 13 countries. Visit Smartly to learn more.

jobs.description:

Hello there! We’re Appinio, a global market research company that combines an AI-powered insights platform with expert consultancy. On a mission to make the world a little more fact-based, we help companies understand how consumers think and make smarter decisions.
We started out in Hamburg back in 2014, but we’re now humbled to call the world our playground, with over 260 employees spread across 13 countries (we’re remote-first), 2600+ international clients, delivering research from +190 markets, globally.
Want to be a part of the Appinio movement? 🚀
Here at Appinio, we value transparency in our recruitment process, and we've created a blog to share what to expect during each step of our journey together: here
Your mission as a (Senior) Product Designer
We’re looking for a (Senior) Product Designer (m/f/d) to help shape the core experiences of our B2B research platform and B2C panel app. You'll work alongside a team of product designers, product managers and engineers to identify problems, explore solutions and ship great products.

- Find problems worth solving. Proactively identify opportunities through your own exploration and research, user conversations and feedback from research experts and product managers.

- You are autonomous and proactive. You don’t need every problem fully specified before you can get started. You take initiative and own features end to end.

jobs.description:
About the Team
OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. We work with customer executives, product and engineering teams, security leaders, and transformation teams to identify valuable opportunities, accelerate technical implementation, and scale what works.
Production-ready deployments are defined by complexity rather than any one industry: existing architectures, diverse data environments, security and governance requirements, multiple stakeholder groups, and organization-wide change. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products and reusable patterns for customers everywhere.
About the Role
As an Applied AI Engineer you will partner directly with leading organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that deliver measurable business outcomes. You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from use-case selection and architecture through prototyping, evaluation, production launch, and scale.
You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions involving model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. Success is measured by production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful customer impact—not simply activity or successful demonstrations.
This is a rare opportunity to work on consequential real-world deployments at the frontier of AI while directly influencing how OpenAI’s products evolve.
This role is based in Munich/Berlin. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees
In this role, you will:
- Partner directly with enterprise and digital native customers to identify high-value opportunities and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and measurable success criteria.

- Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive blockers toward resolution.
- Help customers progress from promising prototypes to reliable production systems, sustained adoption, and scaled impact.
- Partner closely with customer engineering teams and OpenAI Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and go-to-market teams, translating deployment experience into high-signal product feedback.
- Create reusable architectures, tooling, playbooks, and technical guidance that accelerate future enterprise deployments.
You’ll thrive in this role if you:
- Have a demonstrated track record of 5+ years of designing, building, and delivering AI or machine-learning systems in enterprise environments, including taking systems from prototype to production. Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, customer engineering, solutions architecture, product engineering or technical consulting.
- Are fluent in both German and English

- Understand how to evaluate AI systems systematically using representative data, graders, production signals, and human judgment.
- Have navigated enterprise production requirements such as integrations, reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, performance, and cost.

- Communicate with clarity and credibility across hands-on engineers, technical leaders, security teams, product leaders, and executives.

Miaplaza is dedicated to making education engaging and accessible through innovative online learning platforms. We develop personalized learning experiences for students, helping them grow in a supportive and interactive environment. Our vision is to elevate online learning by applying the most successful approaches in virtual education to create an accessible and inclusive education curriculum platform where all students can be successful!
As an engineering manager at Miaplaza, your team will build technology with a direct impact on the lives of hundreds of thousands of students. Every step of the way, you will have the opportunity to influence our direction. Through our platforms, we create engaging, safe, and thoughtfully designed learning experiences that help children grow academically, creatively, and personally. Every feature we ship, every system we scale, and every improvement we make contributes to shaping how the next generation learns and discovers their potential. If our platform is down, a child might not go to school that day. We’re looking for leaders who want their work to matter in classrooms and homes, who care about access to quality education, and who are excited to craft technology that makes a difference in young people’s lives. Here, your impact doesn’t just power a product; it shapes future generations!
What you’ll work on:
We’re moving everything towards GCP and Kubernetes. We’re growing towards a scale that no longer matches our legacy architecture and actively investing in modernization. We’re migrating on-premise workloads to GKE, strengthening security and business continuity best practices, and moving toward platform self-service for our development teams. A core goal is to consolidate and shrink the stack, and every migration decision is measured against whether it lowers the daily burden on the team. You’ll need to work with your team balancing both platform initiatives and the operational needs of the engineering teams you serve. You’ll report to our head of engineering and be expected to split your time roughly 50/50 between people management and hands-on development. Prioritization always goes to leading and supporting your engineers. Your team will consist of four engineers.
What’s unique about management at Miaplaza:
Miaplaza is a US-based education company, which means we probably are doing things differently than you’ve done in your past experience. Here are a few differences you may notice:
- You will first onboard within your team as a senior engineer for 2 months. You will start to onboard as a manager during month two and will take over the team roughly at 10 weeks. This is non-negotiable as both periods of time are equally important.
- We expect our EMs to spend approximately 50% of their time hands-on, even after they’ve completed onboarding as a senior engineer.
- We emphasize the importance of pedagogical principles. A responsibility is to grow your engineers and those around you.
- One of such pedagogical principles is that we expect you to have full oversight into your direct reports' work; you can’t properly teach if you don’t see the process behind the output.
- Feedback is the norm. You’ll be expected to give meaningful, specific reinforcement and constructive feedback whenever you notice something. You should also expect to receive feedback. Ultimately, everything we do is optimizing ourselves, our teams, our processes, and our company to best support our students.
- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.
- 2+ years of experience being a mentor/leader, of which:
- 1+ years leading a team, formally or as a tech lead
- 7+ years of experience in DevOps, SRE, or Infrastructure Engineering, of which:
- 3+ years running production workloads on Kubernetes (GKE preferred)
- 3+ years of experience with a major cloud provider and Infrastructure as Code. GCP is our primary cloud and we expect senior-level knowledge of IAM, networking, KMS, GKE, CloudSQL and Secret Manager
- 3+ years of experience operating at a Senior, Staff, or Principal Engineer level.
- Experience with CI/CD pipeline design and operations
- Experience with GitOps (FluxCD or ArgoCD)
- Experience working directly with engineering teams and other managers as your customers on scoping and prioritization
- Experience leading incident response, including running postmortems
What makes you stand out:
Experience leading a team through a significant architectural migration
Experience with consumer platforms at scale
Experience building in regulated environments
Experience operating self-hosted observability stacks (Prometheus, Thanos, Loki, Grafana, Tempo, OpenTelemetry)
Experience building internal developer platforms or self-service tooling
Experience supporting .NET/C# application deployments
Experience with database operations (PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, RabbitMQ)
Experience with Istio or other service meshes
Responsibilities
- Work with your team to design, build, and operate the infrastructure the rest of engineering depends on: clusters, pipelines, databases, edge, and observability
- Your customers are the other engineering teams. Work with the other Engineering Managers and product development leadership to scope and prioritize platform work
- Set the quality bar for your team. Lead by example.
- Manage, lead, and mentor your team while working side by side with them in code quality, clean infrastructure-as-code, soft skills, best practices, etc

jobs.title: Lead Software Engineer, Integrations (TypeScript)
jobs.description:
Our team shared’s mission is deploy AI agents to transform how patients and doctors connect
We believe healthcare shouldn’t be defined by missed calls, endless waiting lines, and overwhelmed staff. Patients and professionals deserve better.
Vocca builds AI voice agents that answer every call instantly, schedule and reschedule appointments, and free up staff to focus on what matters most: care.
Already trusted by 15 000+ providers, we’re transforming the patient–provider relationship, one call at a time.
Want to shape the future of healthcare?
Join us !
- Discover our company culture and values
- Here is a product teaser
- Eliott's interview for Welcome to the jungle
- Eliott's quick interview for Speedinvest
- Articles on our A round (techfundingnews, Maddyness, les echos, our blog)
Vocca in a few words
Vocca is an AI voice agent that answers 100% of the calls of medical centres. The patient calls, the AI books the appointment or answers the question, and the medical secretaries keep their time for the cases where a human is really needed.
- $20M raised, with the founders of Alan and Datadog as investors
- Close to 1 million calls a month going through the platform
- Opening the US market
The problem
Every medical practice runs on software that holds its calendar and its patients. There are dozens of different ones. Most were built twenty years ago and some have no API at all. To book an appointment during a call, our AI agent has to read and write in that software in real time, while the patient waits on the line. On several of these systems, Vocca is the only integrator in the world.
This is the work with the most direct impact on the business. A clinic whose software is connected to our agent does not switch. Retention, pricing power, our lead over competitors: it all depends on these integrations. Every software we cannot connect is a clinic we cannot sign.
The next step is writing back. Today the agent reads and books. Tomorrow it updates records in EHR, PMS and RIS systems, which raises the reliability bar a lot. In the US, we are opening the dental software ecosystem, with the compliance work that comes with it (HIPAA, SOC2).
There is no product manager on this scope. You would be the one deciding.
What you will own
- The architecture of our booking layer. Today it is code written provider by provider, under pressure, partly in Python. It is becoming one unified layer in TypeScript that handles the rules of each medical centre, where adding a new software takes days, not weeks.
- Speed and reliability at close to 1M calls a month. A call to a clinic software can take several seconds, and the patient cannot wait. You decide how we detect a booking failure in a clinic within 24 hours and what a healthy integration looks like.
- The roadmap of your scope. You decide which software we connect first, with the sales, ops and support teams and the clinics themselves, and you prove it worked with a number: bookings that go through, failures caught, clinics signed.
- The relationship with the software vendors, in France and in the US. The hard integrations are the ones nobody else wants to do. They are what makes Vocca hard to replace.
- The team. You define how this scope works (reviews, documentation, technical decisions), you take part in hiring the next engineers and you help them ship in their first week.
How we build
- Experimental, not R&D. You test, you prove with data, you ship. Challenging a decision means coming back with a result, not a debate.
- Ship, then fix the last 1%. We ship the version that works, then fix the last 1% when it shows up. With AI, this trade off is much cheaper than before. The judgment about what not to touch is yours.
- AI, seriously. Agents in every workflow, Claude Max provided. A migration estimated at 3 months was done in 2 weeks.
- Close to the field. You talk every day with the ops team that deploys clinics, the support team that hears when something breaks and, when it matters, the clinics and the software vendors themselves.
Stack
TypeScript everywhere (Node, monorepo), PostgreSQL, REST and SOAP APIs from software vendors. We are migrating our last Python services to TypeScript over the coming months.
Who does well here
- 6 to 10 years building products in production, mostly in startups that were growing fast, with at least one place where you stayed long enough to see your system live in the long run.
- You have built something that mattered: an early engineer at a startup that took off, a system you launched that real users depended on. You can tell us who it was for, what problem it solved and which number moved.
- You have integrated systems you did not control and you know the difference between a clean API and the real world.
- Strong in TypeScript and Node, comfortable across the stack.
- You think about the product and the business as much as the code. You can say no, reduce the scope and explain a technical decision to a founder in two minutes.
- You are at ease with clients and partners, in French and in English.
Probably not for you if you want to manage without coding, or if you need a stable, fully specified environment before you move.
What we expect from you
- First week. Onboarded on the stack, your first fix on a live integration is in production.
- First month. You own one integration end to end, from the software vendor to production, and show what it changed. You write down how our booking layer should evolve.
- First 3 months. The unified booking layer in TypeScript is the standard. Adding a new software takes days, not weeks. We detect a booking failure in any clinic within 24 hours.
- 6 to 12 months. Our first US integrations run in production. You have hired at least one engineer and they ship on their own.
Process: 4 steps, fast
- 45 min with Nans (Talent).
- 45 min with Pierrick, Head of Engineering.
- 2h in our office with the engineering team: coding without AI and a real conversation about architecture.
- 30 min with Hugo, CTO.
Then references and an offer. When the match is obvious, we have made an offer in 24 hours. You get feedback at every step.
Practical
- Paris, rue d'Alexandrie (Sentier), new offices.
- Hybrid, 3 days at the office.
- BSPCE.
- Claude Max provided.
We aim to keep the process within 30 days. You’ll receive continuous feedback throughout.
Why should you join Vocca?
- An entrepreneurial adventure, with a supportive, high-energy, execution-focused team
- A product already live, with delighted customers in a fast-growing market (healthcare automation, voice AI)
- A true scaling phase, with everything still to build
- Real responsibilities from day one
We hire people, not roles.
If you're excited about our opportunities but don't check every box, we'd love to hear from you. Everyone, no matter how underrepresented, should feel free to apply as it can only bring learnings or success. If you identify yourself as a woman: Did you know that research shows women often apply only when meeting 100% of requirements?
We'll be thrilled to receive your application!

jobs.title: Product Frontend Engineer
jobs.description:
quinn is becoming the way people employ, across the globe, through one app.
quinn is an app-based, managed payroll and employment-administration service. We run it for private households employing a cleaner, nanny, or caretaker, and for businesses that manage employment relationships at scale. The customer stays the legal employer: quinn registers the employment, runs payroll, and handles social insurance, taxes, and filings on their behalf, automated end to end.
Where everyone else sells software, quinn sells the outcome. We don't sell payroll software. We run payroll.
The purpose behind it is simple: Fair employment. For all. Correct and fair employment, made simple and accessible for any employer and any employee, in any market quinn enters.
Where this is going
Think about what Revolut did to banking. All of the complexity (the regulation, the clearing, the compliance) handled invisibly in the background, and one simple experience at the front. Nobody using Revolut thinks about what happens behind the screen when they open a new account, swap currencies or send money abroad. It just works, in a couple of taps. Nobody should have to think about it in order to employ someone either.
That is what quinn is building, and it is further along than most people assume: a profitable core business, running today in Switzerland, Germany and the UK, expanding into new markets both by launching and by acquiring. By 2030 quinn intends to be the destination brand for fair employment across six countries and more, on one platform, with one experience.
One platform means one frontend. One experience means it looks and behaves like quinn whether you are in Zurich or in London, a household or a company. In this strategy that is not a nice-to-have. It is the strategy.
Which is why the surface matters more than anything else. Everything quinn does is designed to disappear. The interface is the only part the customer ever sees, and it is the whole proof that the complexity behind it is really handled.
Why this role exists
Today, quinn runs on several separate web apps: one per product and market, each with its own frontend, grown over the years as the company grew. Our backend engineers built them alongside everything else, plus an internal admin tool that grew the same way. They all work: thousands of employers run payroll through them every month. But nobody was ever tasked with owning the frontend development, so each one got built the way frontend is built by Backend Developers, seen as a hassle rather than the main aspect users interactive with.
What comes next is one frontend that replaces all of them, built from scratch: one quinn app for employers, employees and our own support team, in the browser first, then in the App Store and Google Play from the same work. Alongside it, the frontend of Maestro, the internal tool that replaces the old admin for batch processes. The phone app is the surface that matters most, so everything is built for it from the first screen rather than adapted to it afterwards.
That is the opening.
How we work
We are AI-native, and we mean it operationally rather than as a slogan. AI is how the work gets done here. It is why a small team ships like a large one, and it is a large part of how one person will be able to hold the standard we are describing.
We expect you to be at the front of that. Not to have heard of the tools, to live in them, and to build your own leverage with them: scaffolding, visual regression checks, design-token pipelines, whatever takes manual work out of the way.
And we expect the judgement that has to come with it. AI writes code that looks right and is subtly wrong: structure that doesn't scale, patterns that fall apart three screens later, components that work once and never again. You take the speed and throw away the rest. AI never lowers the bar here. It is the reason the bar can be this high.
Tasks
What you will own
Everything on the screen:
- The frontend of the quinn app and the web app. App first. One app for everyone who uses quinn: the employer, the employee, and our own support team working inside the customer's account.
- The frontend of Maestro, our internal batch tool. Desktop and dense: queues, runs, tables, filters, multi-select, keyboard shortcuts. A different discipline from the app, built on the same components.
- The component library across quinn Home and quinn Business: one frontend, one experience, every market and every device.
- Whether the app feels native: response, scrolling, gestures, transitions, biometric login, push. Nothing that gives away it isn't native.
- The quality of what you ship. Nothing leaves your hands half-finished.
Where design ends, engineering begins.
We have a design team, and they own how quinn looks and behaves: the flows, the visual design, the tokens, the component specs. You don't design. You own everything from there: how it is built, and everything a design file cannot reasonably specify, such as gestures, keyboard, safe areas, what happens between the drawn breakpoints, the loading, offline, pending and failed states, what a three-line German label does to a layout that was designed for English. You are in the room before design starts, saying what already exists in the library and what a new pattern costs. Not at the end, receiving a handover. When you and design disagree, they decide how it looks and behaves and you decide how it is built. Nothing enters the component library without both of you.
Requirements
Who we are looking for
You care about interfaces more than anyone else in the room. You see the two-pixel misalignment without being told, and it bothers you until it is fixed.
You build and maintain UI components and design systems, not one-off screens. You can build a mobile app that feels like one. And you can also build a desktop tool full of tables, filters and keyboard shortcuts, because Maestro is one. You understand UX and how people actually behave, not only how a screen looks. And you write code other people can take over: scalable, structured, documented. Not something that only works while you are in the building.
You are independent and decisive. Nobody will spec every detail for you and nobody will review your pixels.
You are fluent in English, no other language is required. And if you have a portfolio, a live product, or anything you have shipped that you are proud of, show it to us. Not a requirement, but it tells us more than a CV does.
Most importantly: you want this one. Not a frontend role at a company where the frontend is a chore. This one, the app nobody has built yet, the standard nobody has set yet, and a company where getting it right actually decides whether the strategy works.
The Team
We are a small, fast, direct team. We do not have a lot of process or a lot of hierarchy. We do have a clear strategy, an ambitious plan, and five values we actually mean: Be open, Own it, Speak up, Keep it simple, Bias for action.
This is one of the most important hires we will make this year. We are not rushing it and we are not filling a seat. We are looking for the person who reads this and thinks: finally.

jobs.title: Chief Information Security Officer
jobs.description:
Who We Are
Catalyst Capital is a profitable, bootstrapped holding company building a diversified financial services group: education, publishing, software, wealth and tax planning tools, investment products and proprietary trading technology. Funded entirely from its own operating cash. We have never taken outside capital.
The cash engine is Decentralized Masters, a DeFi education business that went from zero to 150+ people, 4,500+ paying members and roughly $48.6M of FY26 revenue at ~25% earnings before tax in four years. That engine funds everything else on this page.
Role summary
Catalyst Capital is hiring its first Chief Information Security Officer to own security across every brand in the group. You will set the strategy, build the program, and personally run the response when something goes wrong.
The job is two halves. Half is the core of a CISO's role: incident response, identity and access, vendor risk, phishing defense, policy and audit readiness, and the judgment calls only a person can own. The other half is making security AI-driven: mapping our full surface and building agentic systems that test, monitor and audit it with near-total coverage, so security keeps pace as more of the company runs on AI. This is a player-coach role: about half hands-on, leading a small team of engineers.
You report to Group leadership, brief the leadership team monthly, and are the person they trust to explain risk in plain language and make the call under pressure.
What you will own
Core security leadership (about half)
- Security strategy and program. Own the security strategy, roadmap and budget across Decentralized Masters, Legacy, Inflection Club, Sentinelis and future brands. Report posture, top risks and trends to leadership every month, with a risk register leadership can act on.
- Incident response. Own IR end to end: detection, triage, containment, eradication, recovery and the postmortem. Lead the room during a live incident and coordinate with legal counsel, forensics firms, insurers and regulators. Keep runbooks current and run tabletop exercises.
- Cloud and identity security. Own identity and access across the group: SSO, MFA, least-privilege roles, admin redundancy and short-lived credentials. Set the AWS security baseline.
- Third-party and vendor risk. Assess the security of every vendor and data provider we depend on, including their audits and attestations, and set the bar a vendor must clear before connecting to our systems or data.
- Platform and customer account security. Set the standards for login protection and account-takeover defense on our platforms, and work with the engineering teams that own each platform to build them in.
- Phishing and impersonation defense. Own email security, staff training and phishing simulations. Run brand protection: find and take down fake domains and accounts impersonating our brands and leaders.
- Policy, compliance and trust. Write and enforce policies people actually follow. Prepare the company for SOC 2 or ISO 27001 with Legal & Compliance. Own the public security and trust story, including the trust page on our products.
- Team leadership. Manage and develop our security engineers, decide what we build in-house versus outsource, and grow the team only where automation cannot do the job.
- Member scam awareness. Supply the security content behind scam-awareness messaging to members, working with Community, Support and Marketing. Legal approves the wording.
AI-driven security (about half)
- Full attack-surface map. Build and maintain a living inventory of everything we run: internal apps, cloud, code repos, and every SaaS tool and integration (CRM, telephony, community, payments, data providers). Know what connects to what, who has access, and what is logged.
- Agentic security harness. Design and run AI-driven systems that approach 100% coverage: automated code and dependency review, continuous configuration and access audits, and vendor documentation review. Humans set direction and make the judgment calls; agents do the exhaustive work.
- AI-driven detection and logging. Own the security stack (SIEM, Rapid7; endpoint protection; email security; identity and device management), make sure every critical system sends usable logs, and use AI to triage alerts and hunt across them.
- Secure AI and vibe-coding standards. Set the rules for how teams build with AI: what can ship, what data AI tools may touch, and the review path before anything with customer data goes live.
- AI agent security. As more of the company runs on agents and automations, secure them: scoped credentials and tool permissions, prompt-injection defense, data exposure, and monitoring and guardrails for agents in production. Review high-risk agents before launch, including our own security agents.
Scope
This role protects our company, our platforms, our data and our brands. For members' personal wallets and accounts outside our platforms, our role is education: helping members recognize and avoid scams.
Requirements
What you will bring
Must have
- 10+ years in security, including 3+ years leading a security function as CISO, Head of Security or equivalent at a company of 100+ people.
- Has led live-incident response, not just tabletop exercises, including briefing executives during the incident.
- Has built or rebuilt a security program from an early stage: strategy, policy, tooling, training and incident response.
- AI-native operator. Uses AI agents daily to do the work: writing detections, reviewing code and configs, reading vendor documentation, drafting policy. Can show us the harnesses, workflows or automations you have built, and knows where AI stops and human judgment has to take over.
- Deep, current knowledge of AI-specific risks: prompt injection, over-scoped agent permissions, credential and data exposure through AI tools, and insecure AI-generated code.
- Hands-on with cloud security (AWS preferred), identity and access management, SIEM, endpoint protection and email security.
- Writes code: scripts, tooling and automation, not only vendor UIs.
- Experience in crypto, fintech or another high-fraud industry, and deep knowledge of phishing, social engineering and impersonation attacks.
- Can read the fine print: thorough with documentation, contracts and vendor security terms, and documents everything so nothing slips through.
- Briefs executives in plain language, trains non-technical staff, and writes policy people follow.
- Player-coach: comfortable spending about half your time hands-on while leading a small, fully remote team across many time zones.
Nice to have
- Has prepared a company for SOC 2 or ISO 27001.
- Has secured or evaluated AI agents and LLM-based tools in production.
- Has run a third-party risk program covering financial data aggregators or similar providers.
- Has run a brand protection or takedown program.
- Experience with customer-facing security features such as account-takeover defense.
- Experience with risk quantification (FAIR or similar) and presenting to a board.
- Certifications such as CISSP, CISM, GCIH or OSCP.
Benefits
What We Offer
- Competitive compensation package
- Independent Contractor opportunity
- Fully remote, globally distributed team
- Team offsites (Dubai, Costa Rica, etc.)
- Collaborative, forward-thinking culture that values innovation and results

jobs.description:
Who are we?
Smarkets: Predicting the Future of Betting
Smarkets runs one of the world’s most sophisticated prediction markets, handling over £29 billion in volume since 2010 and engaging 200,000+ traders globally. We’re a technology company that happens to revolutionise betting - from sports to political markets, to delivering the sharpest prices and the fairest odds.
Our stack is designed for scale, reliability, and speed: Linux, Kafka, Postgres, Kubernetes, with Python 3, C++, Rust and React powering our platform. We build infrastructure that institutions trust while keeping trading accessible to everyone. Our edge? We’ve thrived through every market cycle, competitor, and industry revolution.
At the heart of our success are our people. We create a high-performance environment where exceptional talent can thrive, blending deep business experience with a commercial mindset to drive strategic growth.
If you’re ready to help shape the future of prediction markets with cutting-edge technology and a customer-first philosophy, Smarkets is where you belong.
The Team
The Data Team is responsible for taking the wealth of data that Smarkets generates and using it to drive insights which improve the business. Since Smarkets produces a huge amount of data - including sports event data, payments information, order flow and user analytics - there are many opportunities for the team to add real business value.
The team’s responsibilities currently span across three different areas:
- Data Engineering: development and maintenance of ETL pipelines, services and APIs, and data-related infrastructure like Redshift or BigQuery;
- Data Science and Machine Learning: data exploration, ML models training and ML Ops to extract new insights from data;
- Analytics and Reporting: creation of data models and dashboards as well as automation of reporting pipelines for different teams, stakeholders and third-parties.
In a typical week, a data engineer in the Data team would:
- Add a new python ETL pipeline that segments users interested in specific sports through analysing behaviour which streamlines and tailors marketing communications to those users;
- Develop a new endpoint to a Flask API, add unit tests, and deploy the new version of the API into our production Kubernetes cluster;
- Train and evaluate an ML model to identify certain user patterns and provide it as service to other engineering teams in a Flask API;
Team Tech Stack
Our current technology stack primarily includes Linux, Docker, Kubernetes, Jenkins, Kafka, Python, Flask/FastAPI, Postgres, AWS Redshift, dbt, Google Bigquery, Prometheus, Grafana, Elastic Search, Kibana, Lightdash.
About the Role:
You will work very closely with the Data team lead and the other team members who will be assisting you whenever needed, making your integration in the company as smooth as possible.
The Data team works in an organised way using Agile methodologies and tools such as Jira and regular standups. You will find an environment where you have a clear engineering direction, can focus on your work and hone your skills as a data engineer through exciting projects. You will always be able to count on the support of many engineers across the company.
What you will do:
As a member of the data team, your responsibilities will include contributions to:
- Developing and maintaining our Data ETL pipelines, some of which are real-time. The pipelines are fundamental to helping teams and stakeholders understand and drive business direction. Data components can also be user facing e.g. sending notifications to users;
- Ensuring our data lake is kept in a healthy state, particularly our data warehouses: Redshift and Bigquery;
- Developing and maintaining Flask services and Postgres databases within the Data team to provide access to data or manage certain business entities relevant to Data.
- Assisting the different teams in the company with reporting, especially when it comes to automated reporting pipelines.
- Doing data exploration and training & deploying ML models used to perform different kinds of user segmentation, detect operational anomalies or estimate important business quantities. In particular maintain and improve our existing recommender service that provides users with suggestions on new sport competitions.
Role Requirements:
What we are looking for in you:
- 3+ years of experience
- You have an understanding of developing ETL pipelines using Python frameworks such as luigi or airflow;
- You have experience with the development of Python-based REST APIs / services and their integration with databases (e.g. Postgres);
- You are familiar with the key tools of the Python data science stack, e.g. Pandas, Numpy and scikit-learn;
- Some experience with training and deploying ML models;
- You enjoy writing elegant, well-tested and maintainable code;
- You are a team player that enjoys contributing to the success of the team in a proactive and friendly environment;
- You have a bachelor’s in Computer Science, Math or equivalent field, or possess relevant experience.

Our values are at the heart of everything we do - guiding how we work, collaborate, and innovate. They reflect what we expect of ourselves and each other to deliver the best results, while fostering a positive, high-performing environment:

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer - OpenCRQ
jobs.description:
🌀 The Company
Founded in 2022, Filigran is a global cybersecurity company on a mission to empower defense teams to be proactive through open-source solutions that uncover threats and drive action.
Filigran stands out in the cybersecurity ecosystem through its open-source, AI-powered and threat-informed approach to Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM). Our eXtended Threat Management (XTM) platform brings together threat intelligence, exposure validation and cyber risk reduction, enabling organizations to better understand their threat landscape and take action.
At the heart of Filigran is our open-source approach. Our vision is to unite defenders into a global community to make security more open, resilient and collaborative.
As Filigran continues to scale globally, we are building the organization, infrastructure and capabilities needed for our next stage of growth. How we scale matters just as much as how fast we scale: our CORE values: Cohesion, Openness, Responsibility and Equity shape how we work together, make decisions and build for the future.
🎯 The Role
We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer who is curious about the modeling problem underneath cyber risk and wants to help shape a young product.
You will join OpenCRQ as its fourth engineer and work across the data model, backend and product surface. Many foundations are still being defined, giving you meaningful influence beyond the features you directly own.
You will shape these decisions with the squad and experienced engineering and product leaders across Filigran. We value constructive disagreement, clear reasoning and shared outcomes, and we expect everyone to ask for context, challenge assumptions and learn from one another.
🧩 The problem you would be working on
Ask a CISO what a cyber risk could cost, and the answer often still begins with a color: red, amber or green, often produced by a spreadsheet disconnected from current evidence.
OpenCRQ replaces that color with a financial estimate and a traceable chain of evidence: which threat actors are active, which assets they can reach, which controls have proven effective and what the remaining exposure could cost.
Every step is computed from live data and must withstand a simple question from a board: “Where does that figure come from?” That is what makes this an engineering problem rather than a reporting one.
OpenCRQ is Filigran’s cyber risk quantification product. It combines threat intelligence from OpenCTI, exposure and control validation from OpenAEV, and agentic workflows through XTM One. As these products become more connected, the squad will define what agents can ask of the risk model, which evidence they can use and how their answers remain safe and explainable.
🛠️ What you would work on
- End-to-end product ownership. Take product problems from early ideation and technical design through implementation, end-to-end testing and validation with users. You will have the autonomy to drive the work, while using the squad to challenge assumptions and improve the outcome.
- The quantification engine. Turn threat frequency, control effectiveness and asset value into probabilistic loss distributions. Build general-purpose quantitative models that can evolve as assumptions and available evidence change, without losing reproducibility or explainability.
- The correlation layer. Model complex relationships across OpenCRQ, OpenCTI, OpenAEV and customer systems. Map threat intelligence, including intrusion sets, techniques, campaigns and observations, to assets, vulnerabilities, exposures and control coverage. This includes adapting OpenCRQ to open standards and schemas such as STIX and OCSF, without coupling the product to a single representation.
- Reliable ingestion at scale. Process hundreds of thousands of findings per tenant through delta syncs, long-running backfills and feeds with imperfect timestamps. You will help design observable, recoverable pipelines while extending tenant isolation as the domain grows.
- The agentic surface. Design the contracts used by XTM One agents and the plain-language explanations behind risk figures. Together, the squad will define what models can safely do in a product whose outputs inform board-level decisions.
🏆 What success could look like
Priorities will evolve with the product, but within your first 6 to 12 months you could have:
- Taken a meaningful product problem from early ideation through implementation, end-to-end testing and validation with users.
- Shaped a core part of OpenCRQ’s interconnected data model or quantification engine and documented the trade-offs behind it.
- Made a major ingestion or calculation path more observable, recoverable and reproducible.
- Defined or implemented a durable contract between OpenCRQ and another Filigran product or an open standard, without making the internal model brittle.
- Helped ship risk results that users can trace back to the evidence that produced them.
- Contributed to the open-source release and to engineering practices the growing squad can build on.
🌐 Open source, like the rest of Filigran
OpenCRQ is about to become Open source, alongside OpenCTI and OpenAEV. You will contribute visibly to a product whose risk calculations can be inspected, challenged and improved by the organizations running it.
👥 The squad
You will join two senior engineers and a staff engineer, reporting to OpenCRQ’s Engineering Manager. The squad is small enough for you to influence its direction, without working in isolation.
You will collaborate with the VP of Technology, CTO and Principal Engineers on technical standards, and with the OpenCTI, OpenAEV and XTM One teams on cross-product contracts and integrations. These relationships bring domain knowledge and broader technical context into the squad’s decisions as it grows.
✨ What will help you succeed
We do not expect you to arrive with expertise in cyber risk or every standard named below. We are looking for a strong software engineer who can learn quickly, work autonomously and use the squad to challenge and improve decisions.
- A track record of taking complex product problems from an ambiguous idea to a validated outcome: framing the problem, making technical decisions, implementing the solution, testing it end to end and checking that it solves the user’s need.
- Strong experience with a modern TypeScript stack and practical knowledge of PostgreSQL beyond the ORM. You treat failure modes and observability as part of the design.
- The ability to reason about complex relationships across systems and design interconnected data models that remain coherent as concepts and integrations evolve.
- Comfort turning quantitative concepts into maintainable software. Formal training in statistics is not required, but you should be willing to work with probability distributions, orders of magnitude and models whose assumptions evolve over time.
- Thoughtful use of coding agents: you know where they accelerate engineering and where their output needs careful verification.
- Fluent English is required.
💡 Useful, but not required
Any of the following would help, but none is expected:
- Experience in cybersecurity, GRC or risk quantification.
- Familiarity with STIX/TAXII, OCSF, MITRE ATT&CK or other open cybersecurity standards and frameworks.
- Experience shipping features involving LLM agents, RAG or MCP.

TypeScript end to end: React, Vite and TanStack Router on the frontend; Node.js, Fastify and tRPC on the backend; PostgreSQL with a code-first schema and Drizzle, all in one monorepo.

You lead by example: engineers follow your direction because they see it work in your code. Your impact will also come through the engineers and teams you work with.
Your mission is to build the best agentic runtime for audit: one that completes audit tasks faster, more accurately, more reliably and at lower cost, while scaling to meet the needs of our largest customers.

The hardest AI problems aren't about getting an answer fast. They're about getting one people can trust.
We believe trust is essential to how society works. Every day, we rely on information that's been independently verified, from financial statements to the products we buy, to the sustainability claims companies make. Behind that trust are audit and finance professionals who examine evidence, verify information and hold organizations accountable.
At DataSnipper, we build AI solutions that empower those professionals. By making evidence easier to trace and verify, we help them focus on the judgment and expertise that make their work so important.
For our product and engineering team, this is where things get exciting. In audit, a plausible answer isn't good enough. Every output has to be explainable and traceable back to its source. We've just launched a brand new agentic platform, Alwin by DataSnipper. Backed by a $100 million Series B led by Index Ventures, at a $1 billion valuation, and as proud members of 1% for the Planet, we care about how we grow, not just how fast.

Everything we build is a node: from small embedded devices to full compute systems and ground infrastructure. Together they operate as one network, in the field and over denied, degraded and intermittent links. You design how this works end to end: how nodes find and connect to each other, how trust propagates, how they communicate, and how every node exposes what the application stack needs. And you build it: the network itself, the node agent that runs on every node, the node API and the SDK.
Your roadmap to make an impact
- System design: Own the end-to-end design of how our systems connect and communicate: topology, links, transports, delivery semantics and failure behaviour. - The network: Build it: addressing plans, routing, segmentation and multi-homing across tactical radio, cellular, satcom and wired links, with dynamic routing and link selection for nodes that move and links that fail
- Secure links: IPsec/IKEv2 or WireGuard overlays with certificate authentication from hardware-backed keys, including rekeying, NAT traversal and behaviour on link loss
- Trust: Design how trust propagates from production to the field: device identity, certificate lifecycle, mutual authentication, authorisation tiers, revocation and signed commands that keep working without backend connectivity
- Node agent: Design and build the agent that runs on every node and exposes identity, health, software state, connectivity and updates through one API, served locally, over the network and in compact form over constrained links. Devices too small to run it are represented through their parent node
- Node API and SDK: One resource model for every node type, versioned and backward compatible across a fleet that never updates all at once, with SDKs generated from the contract for the languages our teams use
- Discovery and directory: How nodes find each other with and without infrastructure, and a directory that survives restarts and shows what should exist versus what is present, at fleet scale without polling every node
- Communication: Build on proven middleware and transports instead of reinventing them, define delivery semantics per traffic class, and engineer QoS so command and control traffic survives congestion on constrained links

Founding Full-Stack Engineer
Build the software systems around planqor.ai: the real-time decision layer that steers discrete manufacturing when production plans get disrupted. Born on the shop floor, co-founded by senior production experts, and with direct access to high-impact industry problems. Work directly with our CTO and shape a greenfield product spanning Python backend, data, visualization, frontend, infrastructure, and integration with our optimization core. Backed by investors who have built and scaled successful companies. Remote-first or from our office in Munich, competitive pay + VSOP, no puzzle interviews.
The opportunity
Factories have invested billions in automation, yet production is still steered largely by people. Every night, a plan is computed for the next day, and the first disruption makes it obsolete. From then on, planners and shift leads juggle dependencies by hand. That is expensive, rarely optimal, and wastes much of what these factories were built for.
We are building the layer that takes over when the plan gets disrupted. It connects to factory data, models production, detects disruptions and bottlenecks as they emerge, simulates responses and recommends the best one.
About us
planqor.ai was born on the shop floor. Our founding team brings deep production expertise, strong industry networks. We have the runway to build deliberately and the experience of people who have built and scaled successful companies before. On the technical side, we combine deep algorithmic and software-engineering competence with modern optimization methods, GenAI-assisted development and fast, pragmatic iteration. We are in stealth and very early, which means you can shape much of what comes next.
What you'll own
- The product layer: Turn complex optimization systems into software planners can actually use.
- Backend and data: Build Python services, APIs, data models, and pipelines around our optimization engine.
- Interfaces and visualization: Make schedules, bottlenecks, dependencies, and alternative decisions understandable and interactive.
- Integration: Connect native C++ components, factory data, and product workflows into one coherent system.
- Infrastructure: Own CI/CD, containers, deployment, observability, and the supporting services we need.
- The team: Grow into leading software engineering at planqor.ai as we scale: hiring, mentoring, and setting direction.
You set your own priorities and structure your work toward clear goals. No ticket queue, no micromanagement.
How we build
Our product sits at the boundary between algorithms, software systems, and real industrial operations.
We care about building systems that are easy to integrate, responsive, understandable, and maintainable as both the product and the underlying algorithms evolve.
We use GenAI extensively to prototype, implement, and explore alternatives. But generating code is not the hard part. The value lies in designing the right system, choosing good abstractions, validating behavior, and knowing what is worth building.
There are no points for cleverness. The simplest system that reliably solves the real problem wins.
What you'll bring
- Strong Python and backend engineering. You are comfortable designing APIs, services, libraries, and maintainable system boundaries.
- Full-stack product skills. You can work with TypeScript, React, or similar technologies and build interfaces that make complex systems understandable.
- Data and integration. You can design data models and pipelines, work with databases, and connect messy external systems to clean internal interfaces.
- Systems thinking. You think beyond individual services or screens: how data, algorithms, product, and infrastructure fit together.
- Infrastructure fundamentals. You are comfortable with Docker, CI/CD, deployment, observability, and operating services.
- Independence. You can turn an underspecified operational problem into working software without waiting for a detailed spec.
- Fluent English. German and experience in manufacturing or industrial planning are useful but not required.
Bonus: C++ and native Python bindings such as pybind11 or nanobind; data visualization; optimization, scheduling, simulation, or other algorithmic systems; enterprise integrations such as ERP / SAP.

- A clear growth path into leading the software engineering team.

- Talk with our CTO about your work and how you approach hard problems.

jobs.title: Staff Platform Engineer
jobs.description:
About hyperexponential (hx)
At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a £7 trillion industry, which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.
Until now, insurance has been making billion-pound decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.
Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.
What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.
What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.
If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.
About the Platform team
Platform at hx builds the foundation that enables engineering teams to ship secure, scalable applications at velocity. We're evolving towards an AI-first platform where self-service infrastructure, intelligent automation, and reusable components compound developer productivity and operational excellence. This isn't about maintaining the status quo; we're reimagining how modern software delivery works.
As the Staff Platform Engineer, you will own the technical direction of this evolution. You will define the architecture and engineering standards that others build to, drive coherence across teams, and ensure the platform strategy is aligned to long-term business outcomes. You will shape how AI-first, self-service infrastructure is done at scale, not just by delivering capabilities yourself, but by creating the conditions for engineering teams across the organisation to move faster, more safely, and more autonomously.
Check out our Engineering Candidate Hub for a behind the scenes look at the team you would be joining!
What you'll be doing
- Establish a coherent 12–18 month technical direction for the platform, with clearly articulated trade-offs, milestones, and alignment across engineering leadership. The roadmap is understood, trusted, and actively referenced by stakeholders.
- Platform capabilities are adopted broadly across engineering, not because teams are told to use them, but because they are well-designed, well-documented, and genuinely reduce friction. Measurable reduction in Platform as a bottleneck for common provisioning and deployment tasks.
- Define the architectural patterns and standards that enable autonomous and AI-augmented workflows across the organisation. Other engineers can build AI-native capabilities without requiring Platform's direct involvement in every initiative.
- Platform defined standards for security, reliability, and operational excellence are embedded into how all teams build not enforced through gatekeeping, but adopted because they are the path of least resistance. Measurable reduction in misconfiguration, security exceptions, and operational incidents across the estate.
- Senior engineers are visibly stronger for having worked alongside you. The team develops better instincts for architecture, trade-offs, and platform thinking. You are sought out as a technical authority.
What you'll need to have done
- Defined the architecture, standards, and patterns for the platform domain over a multi-quarter horizon. Makes high-judgement calls on foundational trade-offs such as build vs buy, depth vs breadth, short-term pragmatism vs long-term coherence and brings the organisation along on those decisions.aa
- Navigating disagreement across senior engineers, architects, and stakeholders to reach durable technical decisions. Comfortable holding a position under pressure, updating it when presented with better evidence, and ensuring decisions stick once made.a
- Accountability for outcomes that span multiple teams and that they do not personally deliver. Designs systems, standards, and enablement approaches that multiply the effectiveness of the engineers araound them, rather than being the primary hands-on contributor to every initiative.
- Defined how AI and automation are embedded into the platform at an architectural level not just experimenting with tools, but establishing patterns that make AI-augmented workflows the default for engineering teams across the organisation.
- Understanding of the adoption dynamics, internal customer needs, and the systemic barriers to self-service. Shapes the platform roadmap based on feedback, usage data, and a clear-eyed view of where friction exists and ensures the platform earns its adoption rather than mandating it.
- Identified architectural, security, and operational risks before they become incidents. Influences how the broader engineering organisation thinks about reliability, security posture, and cost efficiency not just within Platform's direct remit.
- Connecting platform decisions to business outcomes clearly and credibly. Can represent the platform strategy to senior leadership, translate engineering constraints into business language, and use commercial context to sharpen technical priorities.aa
- Actively developing senior engineers through technical challenge, honest feedback, and deliberate exposure to harder problems. Recognised as someone who raises the capability of the team, not just the quality of the code. Models the engineering culture the organisation is trying to build.
You're unlikely to thrive here if
- You prefer executing predefined tasks over taking ownership of ambiguous problems that require exploration, experimentation, and iteration to solve
- You view platform engineering as building infrastructure in isolation rather than treating it as a product with internal customers whose adoption and satisfaction drive success
- You're uncomfortable with rapid change and continuous improvement, preferring stability and established patterns over evolving practices based on data and feedback
If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you'll do your best work. We're building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.
Compensation
At hx, we're committed to salary transparency. You'll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we're working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally.
Because we're building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don't always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that's competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make.
Benefits
- £5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development.
- 25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total).
- Company pension scheme via Penfold.
- Mental health support and therapy via Spectrum.life.
- Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno.
- Private healthcare insurance through AXA.
- Income protection and Life Insurance.
- Cycle to Work Scheme.
Additional perks
- Top-spec equipment (laptop, screens, adjustable desks, etc.).
- Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and game nights.
- Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry.
- Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together.
Interview process
- Initial call with our Talent team
- Hiring Manager Interview
- Technical Assessment & follow-up interview
- Values Interview
- Meet the CEO
- We offer!
Our commitment to Diversity
hxers are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive.
Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure.
If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team.
Next steps
If this opportunity resonates with you, we encourage you to apply or share it with your connections! Our dedicated talent team reviews all applications, and we promise to provide feedback regardless of the outcome.
For more information about applying and to view other opportunities, you can visit our careers page.

jobs.title: Senior Security Engineer
jobs.description:
About Kestra
Kestra is the universal orchestration platform: open source, declarative, and designed to orchestrate data pipelines, IT automation, business workflows, and AI/agentic systems.
Trusted by over 10,000 organizations worldwide, including JPMorgan Chase, Bloomberg, FILA, and Crédit Agricole, Kestra orchestrates mission-critical workloads at scale. The open-source project has close to 30,000 GitHub stars, hundreds of contributors, and a fast-growing global community.
About the role
Kestra runs arbitrary, user-defined code at scale. Our users write workflows that execute scripts, containers, and queries against their own production systems, through hundreds of community-built plugins, on a platform whose entire source code is public. That is an unusually rich attack surface, and securing it is a genuinely hard engineering problem rather than a checklist exercise.
You would be our first dedicated security hire. We're looking for a Senior Security Engineer to own and elevate the end-to-end security posture of our platform, infrastructure, and open-source ecosystem.
This is a unique, hybrid role for someone who excels at both sides of security: actively breaking systems to find vulnerabilities (hands-on penetration testing) and actively fixing them (opening PRs, patching infrastructure, and managing supply chain risks). If you want to build a world-class security foundation for a fast-growing open-source and SaaS platform, this role is for you.
This is a hands-on engineering role, not a GRC or compliance one.
What you would do
Your first six months would focus on the first three points below. The rest is where the role grows.
- Conduct hands-on penetration testing and threat modeling across our web application, APIs, control plane, and cloud environments.
- Manage end-to-end vulnerability tracking across our codebases, software dependencies (SCA), container images, and cloud infrastructure.
- Proactively fix security flaws by writing patches, submitting Pull Requests (PRs), or collaborating directly with product teams to guide remediation.
- Audit and harden our cloud infrastructure (GCP, Kubernetes clusters, and networking configurations) against external and internal threats.
- Automate security tooling into our CI/CD pipelines (SAST, DAST, dependency scanners) to catch CVEs before code reaches production.
- Perform security code reviews and evaluate third-party dependencies, open-source integrations, and supply-chain risks.
- Lead incident response efforts and establish continuous monitoring, detection, and mitigation strategies.
- Own our public security posture as an open-source project: vulnerability disclosure process, CVE handling, security advisories, and the trust model of our plugin ecosystem.
Our Tech Stack
