jobs.title: Principal Security Engineer
jobs.description:
Streaming TV is no longer just a brand awareness channel. It’s becoming a core part of the performance marketing mix, alongside search and social. Vibe.co is building the platform that makes TV work like the rest of the acquisition stack: targeted, measurable, and optimized for results.
Vibe.co is an Audience First Streaming TV Advertising platform that gives marketers the tools to reach the right audiences, optimize campaigns in real time, and understand what’s actually driving business outcomes. With hyper-targeted segmentation, AI-powered recommendations, real-time optimization, and incrementality measurement, Vibe brings the precision and accountability of digital advertising to the biggest screen in the house.
Today, more than 12,000 brands use Vibe.co to reach 120 million+ households. And in August 2026, Vibe.co became a Walmart company, opening up a new chapter for the business and the industry. With Walmart’s first-party data and purchase signals now part of the Vibe platform, advertisers can connect TV advertising to real-world transactions and measure the impact of CTV with a level of precision previously associated with platforms like Google and Meta.
This is a unique moment to join Vibe. With Walmart’s scale, data, and reach behind us, we’re building the next generation of TV advertising and creating a more measurable, performance-driven future for the channel.
About the Role
You'll be Vibe's founding security hire. Security has been part of how we build since day one and we're already SOC 2 Type 2 compliant, but nobody has owned it full-time. Ad spend and headcount have both roughly doubled every year since 2022, enterprise partnerships keep expanding, and the more visible Vibe becomes, the more scrutiny comes with it. Now it needs an owner.
You'll define the risk model, set the roadmap, decide what we harden and what we accept, and turn policies into running procedures in code on the paths engineers and AI already use. That work happens in a cloud native ecosystem across AWS and GCP, with most of our services running on Kubernetes, everything as code and a GitOps deployment model.
Reporting to our, Head of Infrastructure, and joining a lean six-person Infrastructure and IT team. You won't do it alone, but you'll be the main contributor, and the person every team turns to on security. Since we joined forces with Walmart, you'll also coordinate directly with their cloud security teams.
What You'll Do
Risk & Governance
- Map Vibe's risk model across every major system.
- Set the security roadmap with clear priorities.
Security Engineering
- Pave the road with guardrails and secure defaults enforced across the engineering tool set.
- Ship the golden paths so the safe way is the easy one.
- Harden security across our cloud native ecosystem (AWS and GCP) and third-party providers.
- Own access management from onboarding to offboarding, and get it to the point where it runs without you.
Detection & Response
- Prioritize vulnerability findings by real exposure, assign them to the team that owns the code, and follow remediation through to closure.
- Own security incident response from detection through resolution.
- Turn manual processes into pipelines that run on their own.
- Launch and run Vibe's private bug bounty program.
Trust & Compliance
- Own SOC 2 compliance end to end and maintain current certification.
- Drive Vibe's future compliance initiatives and requirements.
- Define Vibe's security posture and make it self-serve so enterprise deals clear security without routing through you.
Security Culture
- Set clear, practical rules for safe AI use, built into the tools themselves, covering both the AI we ship in our products and the AI our teams work with every day.
- Run security awareness training and measure behavior changes so the whole company raises its bar.
What You Need
- Built a security function as a company's first security hire.
- Write code comfortably and bring deep cloud-native security experience.
- Managed a compliance framework at scale, such as SOC 2, ISO 27001 or HIPAA.
- Managed AI security risk hands on, both in what a company ships with AI and in how its employees use it day to day.
Nice to Haves
- Ran a private bug bounty program.
- Ad tech security background, including exposure to US privacy law (CCPA/CPRA, VPPA) in a data-heavy environment.
- Navigated security through a company acquisition.
Our Values
At Vibe, we run on three values: Impact, Ambition, and Urgency. We tie every goal to a real business outcome, think 10x rather than settling for good enough, and move daily rather than waiting for perfect conditions.
You'll thrive here if you own outcomes without needing direction, default to action, and hold yourself to results, not effort.
This is a high-performance environment with high-performance rewards: you'll work alongside people who push you, with real ownership over hard problems in a market that's moving fast.
If that sounds like the best version of your career, we want to meet you.
What We Offer
The pay range for this role is €127,000-€171,000. We will support relocation to Paris for great candidates.
At Vibe, we want you to build something, own something, and grow fast. Here's how we back that up:
- Variable pay — Based on real Vibe business goals.
- Hybrid flexibility — We're in the Heart of Paris and our team is in 3x a week!
- Health insurance — Full coverage via Alan.
- Meal vouchers — Via Swile.
- Annual offsite — The whole team, once a year, somewhere worth the trip.
- Tech Syncs — Engineering and Product meet in person at least quarterly, worldwide.
Our Interview Process
We respect your time. Here's exactly what to expect, no surprises, no ghosting.
- Recruiter Screen — 30 minutes. We’ll share more context on the role and team, and learn more about your background and what you’re looking for.
- Hiring Manager Interview — 45 minutes. Meet with the person you’d work with directly and dive deeper into your experience, technical background, and approach to the role.
- Technical Assessment — 90 minutes. A deeper technical conversation covering core engineering skills, problem-solving, and a technical use case relevant to the role.
- Bar Raiser Interview — 30 minutes. Meet with a senior leader at Vibe for a final conversation and an opportunity to ask any remaining questions.
- Offer — We move quickly once we’ve made a decision. We don’t let good decisions sit.
Equal Opportunity
Vibe is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.
We believe the best ideas come from teams with different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences. If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or interview process, please let us know.
Referral Instructions
Being referred? Ask your contact to submit your application directly on your behalf.

We are doing it with a small, senior, very fast AI development team working shoulder to shoulder with our business leads. Now we are opening a handful of seats for young builders who want to grow faster than any graduate scheme, bootcamp, or big-tech ladder could ever let them.

For this role, we will only consider candidates who are currently based in the Netherlands.
About SkinVision
Skin cancer is highly treatable when caught early, but limited access to specialist care and long wait times delay diagnosis, increasing the risk of late-stage cases and driving up treatment costs. SkinVision, founded in Amsterdam in 2012, exists to close that gap. Our proprietary AI — certified as a Class IIa medical device under EU regulation, with over 90% sensitivity and 89% specificity — has already helped nearly 3 million people worldwide detect early signs of skin cancer. Today, SkinVision has a database of more than 6 million skin spot assessments and can reach 20 million people through insurer partnerships. High-risk cases are reviewed by a team of dermatologists, who support users in taking the right next step — from urgent care to a specialist referral. We are extending this further, connecting users faster to the specialist care they need. We're a focused, international team, active globally, united by one goal: making early detection accessible to everyone, everywhere. If you join us, you're not just building a product — you're helping close the gap between a person noticing something and getting the care they need.
DevOps at SkinVision
As a DevOps Engineer at SkinVision, you will play a key role in building, scaling, and securing the infrastructure that powers our AI-driven health platform. You’ll design and maintain our cloud-based systems in AWS, implement CI/CD pipelines, enhance observability using Datadog, and drive operational excellence through automation and monitoring.
Your work will directly impact the reliability and scalability of a medical-grade system that serves users globally. You’ll collaborate closely with backend, ML, and product teams to ensure smooth delivery, rapid deployments, and resilient operations — ultimately enabling us to deliver life-saving technology with confidence.
Beyond hands-on expertise with AWS and modern DevOps tooling, we’re looking for someone who thinks architecturally. You’ll get to know our current setup, form your own view of how it should evolve, and help define a target vision for our infrastructure, then drive its implementation. Day-to-day operational work is part of the role, but we value someone who thinks before building and takes ownership of where our infrastructure goes next.
What you will do
Cloud Infrastructure & Automation
- Design, build, and manage AWS-based infrastructure, ensuring high availability, scalability, and cost efficiency.
- Implement and manage infrastructure as code (IaC) using tools like Terraform or CloudFormation.
- Automate environment provisioning, configuration, and deployments using CI/CD pipelines.
- Ensure system resilience, security, and performance through automated monitoring and alerting.
CI/CD & Deployment
- Design and optimize CI/CD pipelines to support rapid, reliable, and safe deployments across environments.
- Manage deployment workflows using Argo CD and Kubernetes.
- Collaborate with developers and ML engineers to streamline build, test, and release processes.
- Integrate automated testing, rollback strategies, and version control into the deployment lifecycle.
Observability & Monitoring
- Build a comprehensive observability stack using Datadog for metrics, logs, traces, and alerts.
- Define service-level objectives (SLOs), service-level indicators (SLIs), and dashboards for system performance.
- Proactively detect and resolve performance bottlenecks, capacity issues, and reliability risks.
- Create automated health checks and ensure visibility across production systems.
Security & Compliance
- Implement security best practices for AWS, containers, and CI/CD pipelines.
- Manage identity, access, and secret handling (IAM, Secrets Manager, Parameter Store).
- Ensure compliance with medical device standards and data privacy regulations (GDPR, HIPAA).
- Partner with the Information Security Officer to embed security controls across infrastructure and deployments.
Reliability & Incident Management
- Lead incident response and root cause analysis for infrastructure or deployment-related issues.
- Establish SLAs and operational runbooks for production environments.
- Continuously improve system reliability through chaos testing, redundancy, and fault tolerance.
- Mentor engineers on DevOps principles, observability practices, and infrastructure automation.
Infrastructure Strategy & Architecture
- Assess the current infrastructure and deployment setup, and form a well-reasoned view of how it should evolve.
- Define and maintain a target architecture for our cloud platform, balancing reliability, scalability, security, and cost.
- Translate the target vision into a practical roadmap and drive its implementation incrementally, alongside day-to-day operations.
- Document and communicate architectural decisions, aligning with engineering and leadership on technical direction.
Essential skills
- Minimum of 6 years of experience in DevOps, Site Reliability Engineering, or Cloud Infrastructure roles.
- Strong expertise with AWS services (EC2, ECS/EKS, S3, RDS, CloudWatch, Lambda, etc.).
- Expert in Kubernetes and Argo CD, deploying and managing production-grade custom Helm charts with secure, automated GitOps workflows in EKS
- Advanced knowledge of CI/CD systems (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, or similar).
- Proficiency in Datadog for observability, monitoring, and alerting.
- Strong scripting and automation skills in Python, Bash, or Go.
- Experience managing infrastructure with Terraform, CloudFormation, or Ansible.
- Familiarity with networking fundamentals, load balancing, and API gateway configuration.
- Excellent problem-solving and incident management skills.
Desirable skills
- Experience in regulated industries such as healthcare, MedTech, or FinTech.
- Familiarity with multi-environment architecture (staging, pre-prod, production) and blue-green deployments.
- Exposure to event-driven systems, message queues, and data streaming (Kafka, SNS/SQS).
- Understanding of Zero Trust networking and cloud security best practices.
- Experience in cost optimization and performance tuning in AWS.
Qualifications
- A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
- Certifications such as AWS Certified DevOps Engineer, Kubernetes Administrator (CKA), or Terraform Associate are a plus.

The Growth Mega Alliance (GMA) builds the platforms that power how HelloFresh acquires, converts, and retains customers across 18 markets and multiple brands, across five pillars: AdTech, Conversions, Payments, Communications, and Customer Value Optimization (CVO).
As Principal Engineer, you are the technical visionary for these platforms. You define architectural direction across all five pillars, lead the most consequential cross-cutting initiatives, and raise the technical bar for the entire organization. This is a hands-on leadership role - you code, review, and design alongside the senior and staff engineers who look to you as the technical lead.
What You'll Do
GenAI & Agentic Engineering Leadership
- Own GMA's GenAI strategy: identify the highest-leverage opportunities across all five pillars where AI/ML unlocks step-change outcomes, for both engineering productivity and customer-facing capabilities.
- Establish agentic development workflows — where specs drive AI-assisted code generation — and scale them from early adopters to standard practice. Build the guardrails and reference architectures that enable squads to work AI-natively.
- Develop and articulate a clear point of view on how engineering teams need to evolve in skills, process, and culture to realize the gains that agentic tools make possible.
Growth Platform Architecture
- Own the long-term technical architecture across GMA's five pillars: real-time personalization, experimentation at scale, AI/ML-driven automation, and cross-pillar data integrity.
- Lead the most complex architectural decisions (shared identity schemas, experiment assignment, AdTech-to-Conversions signal loops, payment authorization flows) and drive migrations with large impact.
- Ensure GMA platforms integrate cleanly with internal infrastructure and meet reliability, latency, and observability requirements at a global scale.
Experimentation & Personalization
- Define GMA's experimentation strategy and execution framework to optimize experimentation-based decision-making at scale.
- Own the data path from customer event to business decision: instrumentation standards, identity resolution, attribution windows, and signal quality.
Technical Strategy & Cross-Alliance Collaboration
- Define GMA's multi-year technical vision and communicate it with the precision engineers need and the clarity executives can act on. Represent GMA in company-wide programs.
- Partner with Intelligent Platforms, Consumer, and Operations Mega Alliances to drive shared architectural standards and prevent fragmentation.
Mentorship & Engineering Culture
- Coach and grow Staff and Senior Engineers across all five pillars. Foster engineering excellence through rigorous design review, strong observability practice, and honest post-incident learning.
- Champion AI-native development workflows, TDD, DDD, and DevSecOps. Set the written communication standard through your design docs and architectural decision records.
What You'll Bring
GenAI & Agentic Engineering
- Practical, hands-on experience with AI coding agents (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode) in production or near-production environments — not just experimentation.
- Experience integrating GenAI into customer-facing products or internal business processes at scale, with a clear point of view on the team and cultural changes required to realize the productivity gains.
Growth Domain Expertise
- Deep familiarity with at least two of: AdTech / paid media infrastructure, funnel optimization, payment orchestration, CRM and lifecycle communications, or pricing and incentive optimization.
- Fluent in growth domain constraints: PSP behavior, consent and privacy requirements across markets, deliverability limits, attribution windows, and incrementality measurement. Experience in a multi-market subscription or e-commerce business preferred.
Technical Depth
- ~10+ years in software engineering, with ~5+ years at principal level in a high-growth, cloud-native environment.
- Expert in distributed systems, microservices, and event-driven patterns (Kafka). Deep AWS experience. Strong proficiency in Go, Kotlin, Python, or TypeScript.
- Track record of designing and operating large-scale, multi-region systems. Comfortable doing hands-on architectural reviews and solving critical bottlenecks directly.
- Working knowledge of experimentation design and analysis; able to work directly with data (SQL, BI tooling) and trace the full signal chain from instrumentation to business metric.
Ways of Working
- Exceptional written communication — your documents make complexity smaller, not larger.
- Able to influence without authority; direct, low-ego, and comfortable disagreeing with senior stakeholders while keeping the relationship intact.
- Fluent English. German is a bonus.
What Success Looks Like
3 months — You have mapped GMA's critical architectural dependencies and GenAI opportunities, conducted design reviews across multiple pillars, and established a point of view on the highest-leverage technical bets for the year.
6 months — Your architectural direction is reflected in roadmaps. GMA's first AI-native workflows are in production. At least one cross-pillar initiative is running under your technical ownership with clear instrumentation.
12 months — GMA's platforms are measurably more scalable, observable, and AI-capable. Engineering standards are set and followed. You are the person leaders across HelloTech bring their hardest growth-engineering problems to.
Why Work With Us
- Make an Impact: GMA's platforms touch every customer HelloFresh acquires and every euro it collects. Your decisions move top-line numbers at a company that has changed the way millions of people eat.
- Real Scope: You own technical direction, make consequential architectural calls, and ship things that matter — at a scale that makes the problems genuinely hard.
- AI at the Frontier: You will have the mandate, resources, and organizational support to lead AI-native engineering transformation — not advocate for it from the sidelines.
- Direct Access: You work daily with engineering, product, and business leadership, with the visibility and accountability that implies.
- Learn & Grow: Annual learning budget, HelloFresh Academy, and internal mobility across a large, technically ambitious engineering organization.

jobs.title: Platform Engineer
jobs.description:
Why Faculty?
We established Faculty in 2014 because we thought that AI would be the most important technology of our time. Since then, we’ve worked with over 350 global customers to transform their performance through human-centric AI. You can read about our real-world impact here.
We don’t chase hype cycles. We innovate, build and deploy responsible AI which moves the needle - and we know a thing or two about doing it well. We bring an unparalleled depth of technical, product and delivery expertise to our clients who span government, finance, retail, energy, life sciences and defence.
Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology.
AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen.
About the team
Bringing medicine to patients is complex, expensive and high-risk. Faculty’s Life Science’s team is concentrated on building AI solutions which optimise the research and commercialisation of life-changing therapies.
We partner with major pharma firms, academic research centres and MedTech start-ups to design and deliver solutions which address critical healthcare challenges, and help to democratise health for all.
About the role
We're looking for a Platform Engineer to build the backbone of applied artificial intelligence for our customers. You will design, build, and deploy robust, secure, and scalable cloud infrastructure that powers cutting-edge data and machine learning workflows. Working in a cross-functional team, you'll solve complex challenges and empower our data scientists and ML engineers to deploy their work effectively, shaping the future of AI solutions.
What you'll be doing:
- Building robust, secure, and scalable cloud infrastructure for AI and ML workflows.
- Partnering with technical and non-technical stakeholders, from initial idea generation through to implementation and shipping.
- Enabling Machine Learning Engineers and Data Scientists by contributing to internal best practices, standards, and reusable code repos.
- Proactively identifying and recommending new ways customers can leverage cloud infrastructure to solve their key challenges.
- Creating and maintaining reusable, company-wide libraries and infrastructure-as-code.
- Researching and integrating the best open-source technologies to enhance Faculty's infrastructure capabilities.
Who we're looking for:
- You are pragmatic and outcome-focused, balancing the big picture with the details to execute complex projects in the real world.
- You think scientifically, always testing assumptions, seeking evidence, and looking for opportunities to improve how things are done.
- You have a drive to learn, constantly exploring new technologies and novel applications for existing tools.
- You possess deep experience with both Azure and AWS as well as Infrastructure as Code, especially Terraform.
- You are experienced in building and deploying containerized solutions using Docker and Kubernetes, supported by strong CI/CD and GitOps practices.
- You possess proficient knowledge of Networking and Cloud Security
- You excel at working directly with clients and stakeholders, confidently handling requirements gathering, technical planning, and scoping.
The Interview Process
- Talent Team Screen (30 minutes)
- Pair Programming Interview (90 minutes)
- System Design Interview (90 minutes)
- Commercial Interview (60 minutes)
Our Recruitment Ethos
We aim to grow the best team - not the most similar one. We know that diversity of individuals fosters diversity of thought, and that strengthens our principle of seeking truth. And we know from experience that diverse teams deliver better work, relevant to the world in which we live. We’re united by a deep intellectual curiosity and desire to use our abilities for measurable positive impact. We strongly encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, ethnicities, genders, religions and sexual orientations.
If you don’t feel you meet all the requirements, but are excited by the role and know you bring some key strengths, please don't hesitate in applying as you might be right for this role, or other roles. We are open to conversations about part-time hours.
A note on AI: we're happy for you to use it for research and interview prep, but please don't use it to generate answers during live interviews. We also use an AI note-taker (Metaview) in interviews so interviewers can stay present (which you can opt out of just let us know,) and every application is reviewed by a human, never decided by AI.

jobs.title: Senior AI Engineer - Legal AI
jobs.description:
About 9fin
9fin is the AI platform powering global debt markets — the world’s largest asset class at over $145 trillion.
Debt markets are vast, global, and mission-critical, yet still run on fragmented data, PDFs, and manual workflows. 9fin replaces this broken infrastructure with a single platform that centralises proprietary credit data, deep analysis, and high-value workflows across global markets.
Today, 9fin powers teams at 300+ blue-chip institutions worldwide, including global banks, asset managers, private equity firms, law firms, and advisors. The business is scaling at exceptional speed, with rapid expansion in the US and best-in-class retention driven by deep workflow adoption.
We’re at a defining inflection point. With proven product-market fit and strong, global market pull, 9fin is accelerating toward becoming the category-defining platform for debt markets worldwide.
The Opportunity
The Data Science team is growing at 9fin! We are doing world-class work with groundbreaking technologies to build data-driven products using machine learning, computer vision, natural language processing, speech and audio, and knowledge/data mining. We are looking for a Senior AI Engineer to accelerate our application of AI across teams and products. Come and join us, you will get to build large-scale AI powered systems, learn and apply the latest techniques, and work alongside other great researchers and engineers!
Every day is different, but here's an example of the kind of things you'll work on:
- Design and build generative AI applications tailored to complex financial and legal workflows, leveraging state-of-the-art models to deliver innovative, practical solutions that streamline decision-making and unlock new efficiencies.
- Drive end to end model development lifecycle, leading the team in best practices, ensuring reproducible research and well managed model delivery/deployment.
- Collaborate cross functionally to share diverse ideas, understand business problems, and elevate/mentor your teammates.
- Translate complex problems into well-defined scoped bets in an internal startup style environment, dynamic and fast-paced.
- Learn and apply ground-breaking research and approaches in advanced topics, iterating improvements with a fail fast mentality.
- Be a proactive sharer of compelling ideas/work to the rest of the team and organisation. We want you to help lead/push the adoption of AI throughout 9fin.
What Makes This Role Different
This role is focused on converting complex financial and legal documents into structured, reliable data. While experience with chatbots, retrieval systems, and general-purpose AI applications is valuable, the core challenge is building systems that can accurately understand legal documentation and extract the information that powers financial analysis and workflow automation.
About You
This role will be a great fit if you:
- Legal Document Intelligence: Deep experience working with complex legal and financial documents, including bond offering memoranda, credit agreements, indentures, court filings, and related transaction documentation.
- Information Extraction: Expertise in extracting structured data from long, complex documents, including financial terms, covenant provisions, definitions, parties, dates, thresholds, baskets, ratios, and transaction mechanics.
- Document Understanding & NLP: Strong understanding of document structure, section hierarchy, cross-references, defined terms, tables, exhibits, and other patterns common in legal and financial documentation.
- LLMs for Structured Extraction: Experience applying LLMs to high-precision extraction tasks, including schema-driven extraction, citation grounding, validation, and confidence scoring.
- Data Quality & Validation Systems: Ability to design review, verification, and reconciliation workflows that ensure extracted data is accurate, consistent, and auditable.
- Training Data & Annotation: Experience building labelled datasets, annotation frameworks, synthetic data generation, and evaluation sets for document extraction tasks.
- Retrieval & Context Engineering: Strong understanding of chunking, document segmentation, retrieval, and context construction for long-document reasoning and extraction workflows.
- Financial & Legal Domain Knowledge: Familiarity with leveraged finance, debt capital markets, credit agreements, covenant packages, bond documentation, restructuring processes, and related legal concepts.
- Production ML Engineering: Ability to build and operate extraction pipelines, evaluation systems, model-serving infrastructure, and monitoring for production AI workflows.
- Strong proficiency in Python for production ready delivery.
- Experience working in the full model lifecycle (including experimentation, training, testing, monitoring, and deployment). We are data centric and love our evals!
- You have a strong product focus with a desire to understand the end-to-end impact of your solutions for our end users.
- Good knowledge of AWS’s AI infrastructure.
Benefits
We’re a scaling start up, and we enjoy sharing our success, when the company succeeds, we always reinvest that in our people. We also offer huge amounts of responsibility, an abundance of opportunity for growth and a platform to truly excel.
Financial & Insurance
- Competitive Salary (our salary bands are benchmarked at the top end of the market)
- Equity
- Pension (your minimum contributions are 4% with 9fin matching up to 7%)
- Private Medical Insurance
- Paid sick leave with Income Protection for long periods of illness
- Group Life Assurance
- Season Ticket Loan & Cycle to Work schemes
Time off
- 25 holiday days per year
- Local public holidays (with the ability to exchange them for alternative days)
- Work abroad for up to 3 months a year
- 1 month paid sabbatical after 5 years of service
- Enhanced parental leave & flexible working arrangements available
Training & Culture
- Professional learning and development budget
- AI experimentation budget of £800 (UK) per employee to trial AI tools
- Quarterly team socials
- Summer and Winter company social events
Hybrid Policy
9fin is a hybrid company, and the office is a regular part of how we work. From January 2027, all employees will work from their designated 9fin office on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. Some teams may be asked to be in the office more often, where the nature of their work calls for it. For the rest of the week, you may work from wherever works best for you and your team. Your Talent Partner will share hybrid working details for this role.
9fin is an equal opportunities employer
At 9fin we are dedicated to building and promoting a fair and inclusive workplace where everyone can reach their full potential and truly belong. We recognize that building diverse teams enables a more creative and productive environment. If you’re excited about this role but your experience doesn’t perfectly align with the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You might just be who we’re looking for — either for this role, or perhaps another.

jobs.title: Platform Engineer
jobs.description:
About us
We love pets - which is why we're on a mission to make the world a better place for pets and their parents. We offer pet insurance policies with generous pet health benefits that are designed with their needs in mind. We've helped half a million pets stay happy and healthy since 2017 - and many more customers throughout the world are joining us every day. Our company is respectful, fun-loving and passionate about pets and their wellbeing. Throughout our business you'll meet people who think differently, aim for impact, and love to try new things. Want to join our pack? Join us. Love every moment. Love ManyPets.
A day in the life
As a Platform Engineer, you will initially join our platform squad. We build and maintain the AWS infrastructure, deployment pipelines, tooling and engineering standards that every other squad at ManyPets depends on.
This role has a strong security focus, and it will become more security focused over time. Much of the work is compliance and assurance: building and running the tooling that checks our cloud estate against our security standards, writing the scripts that turn a manual check into a scheduled one, gathering the evidence we need for ISO 27001 and our other obligations, and supporting the audits that depend on it. Alongside that you will help us tighten access controls across our cloud estate, and take on ownership of the edge and network security tooling that protects our services.
Over time this role moves across to work directly with our Head of Security as we build out a dedicated security function at ManyPets. You will help shape what that function does and how it works, rather than inheriting something already built.
Our environment is fast-paced and highly collaborative. You will work closely with your teammates using pair or mob programming, participating in regular workshops and planning sessions, primarily over Zoom, with occasional in-person collaboration.
We embrace modern development practices:
· All our services are cloud-hosted on AWS, using serverless and event-driven architectures for scalability and resilience.
· We use a fully automated deployment pipeline, allowing you to release to production within minutes, multiple times per day.
· We define our infrastructure as code, and we emphasise observability, testing and secure-by-design principles from the start.
As a squad we own our work end-to-end, including development, maintenance and support. You will play a key role in ensuring the reliability and quality of what we provide to the rest of engineering, and contribute to a culture of rapid learning and continuous improvement.
Your responsibilities
ü Build and maintain secure platform foundations
o Design, build and maintain the shared cloud infrastructure, tooling and deployment pipelines that other squads rely on.
o Define infrastructure as code so our environments are consistent, repeatable and reviewable.
o Make secure configuration the default, so squads get it without having to ask for it.
o Maintain the edge and network security tooling that protects our services.
o Share in the day-to-day operational ownership of the platform, responding to requests and issues raised by other squads.
Make our security posture measurable
o Automate the gathering of evidence for ISO 27001 and our other compliance obligations, so that an audit means pulling a report rather than running a manual exercise.
o Write the scripts and small services that turn a manual security check into a scheduled, repeatable one.
o Triage findings from our scanning and posture tooling such as Aikido and Ascidian, work out which ones actually matter, and either fix them or get them in front of the team that can.
o Work with our Head of Security to turn written policy into controls that are enforced by tooling.
Strengthen access and identity controls
o Review and tighten access across our cloud accounts, working towards least privilege.
o Improve how we manage secrets, credentials and machine identities.
o Make access changes auditable, and straightforward for engineers to request and for us to review.
Extend our platform standards beyond AWS
o Help us apply the standards, tooling and controls we have built in AWS to our Google Cloud estate.
o Work with the teams who use Google Cloud to understand their needs and where the gaps are.
Team collaboration
o Work closely with other squad members and stakeholders to align on goals and solutions.
o Support engineers across other squads who use our platform, and take their feedback seriously.
o Proactively build shared understanding across the team through pairing, discussions, and reviews.
o Document your work clearly to support knowledge sharing and future maintenance.
Self development
o Take ownership of your learning journey and technical development plan.
o Approach challenges with curiosity and a growth mindset.
o Learn from your peers and actively seek feedback and mentorship.
Your skills and experience
We are looking for someone with:
· Commercial experience building and maintaining cloud infrastructure on a major cloud provider (AWS, Google Cloud or Azure).
· Hands-on experience defining infrastructure as code.
· Experience building and maintaining continuous integration and deployment pipelines.
· A good working understanding of cloud security fundamentals.
· Proficiency in at least one scripting language, ideally Python.
· Comfort working in a regulated environment. We are FCA regulated and take our ISO 27001 commitments seriously.
You will also need at least one current associate-level cloud certification:
· AWS: Solutions Architect Associate, Developer Associate or SysOps Administrator Associate. We would also be interested in the AWS Certified Security Speciality.
· Google Cloud: Associate Cloud Engineer.
· Microsoft Azure: Administrator Associate (AZ-104) or Security Engineer Associate (AZ-500).
Entry-level certifications such as AWS Cloud Practitioner, Google Cloud Digital Leader and Azure Fundamentals do not meet this on their own. Please include the certification name and your credential ID or badge link with your application.
We would also like to see at least one of the following. You do not need both, and we will support you to build the other:
· A security specialism, where you can tell us about security or compliance tooling you have built and what it caught.
· Experience across more than one cloud provider, ideally both AWS and Google Cloud.
The interview process
This position has a four-stage interview process, which will be held via Zoom.
· Stage 1 - an initial conversation with a member of our Talent team.
· Stage 2 - an informal meeting with the hiring manager for about 45 minutes. We will explain more about the role and explore how your experience matches up with what we need.
· Stage 3 - a longer interview, up to an hour, with the hiring manager and two engineers from the team. We will ask some competency questions and work through a technical scenario together. There is no take-home exercise.
· Stage 4 - an informal conversation with our Head of Security.
About the team
The EPD ("Engineering, Product and Design") team operates with a squad system and Agile ways of working within quarterly terms - and we really enjoy working collaboratively. We hold regular 'Hack Weeks' to look at products and address problems relating to the business, and we get the chance to highlight and work on things we're interested in and feel passionately about.
Our tech stack
We are on a mission to become the best we can be, constantly challenging ourselves to achieve and learn. You will be supported to learn new technology – both in breadth and depth - and encouraged to challenge our ways of thinking with new and innovative ideas.
Our "north star" is to become an elite performer as defined by the 4 key DORA metrics. To drive towards elite status, we apply and continually inspect and adapt the best Agile frameworks and practices inspired by DevOps, SRE, Scrum, XP and Lean. We are a highly collaborative environment and regularly practice Mob and Pair based programming which we believe improve our quality of delivery and share understanding.
We take our operational performance, security, and reliability as seriously as our quality and development practices. We are cloud hosted and highly automated, primarily on AWS with some critical services running on Google Cloud.
Some specific technologies we use include: AWS | Google Cloud | Python | MongoDB | Aikido | Ascidian | Cloudflare
Salary range:
£55,000—£65,000 GBP
Ways of working
On a typical day you'll be working from a laptop with a screen, mouse, keyboard, and headset. jobs.title: Front End Design Engineer
jobs.description:
About Seamflow
Every plane, medical device, lift, battery and building has to be tested, inspected and certified before it reaches the world. It's the invisible layer that keeps the physical economy safe, and it still runs on Word documents, PDFs, spreadsheets and email. Seamflow is the software layer for that industry. We build AI-powered workflows for certification bodies, notified bodies and inspection companies: scheduling and resource planning, technical review, conformity assessment, field inspection, and document intelligence over messy real-world files.
Where we are:
- Live in production inside some of the largest enterprises in the industry
- $4.5M seed, 14x oversubscribed, co-led by Northzone and Initialized Capital, the funds behind Spotify, Klarna, Coinbase and Reddit. Angels include Charlie Songhurst and Mario Götze.
- Demand is outstripping what we can build. That's the reason this role exists.
The team
Most of our engineers were olympiad medallists in maths, physics or informatics before they were engineers. The team has come to us from Google, Amazon, X, Yandex, McKinsey and Bain, and from founding-engineer seats at startups that went on to multi-billion-dollar valuations. We hire against a very high bar, and this role exists to raise it further.
The role
A Front End Design Engineer thinks in finished interfaces, not mockups or components in isolation. A technical reviewer at a notified body spends their day inside a 400-page technical file, cross-referencing clauses, checking test reports against standards, and deciding whether a medical device is safe to sell. Today they do that in Word, Acrobat and a spreadsheet someone built in 2011. The interface they use decides how fast they work and whether they trust the AI sitting next to them.
You own that interface. Layout, typography, interaction, motion, the design system underneath it, and the React that ships it. You decide how a reviewer sees a finding, how they correct a model that got it wrong, and how a hundred fields of dense regulatory data become something a person can actually read. You sketch it, build it, ship it, then sit next to someone using it and find out what you got wrong. You'll ship to production in your first week.
What we're looking for
We care far more about taste and engineering strength than about matching a list of tools. If you're excellent, we'll hire you whether you've spent the last three years in React, Svelte, Vue or something we haven't heard of. Our stack is learnable in a fortnight. Judgement, craft and speed are not.
What we're actually screening for:
- You've designed and built an interface that real people used every day. Not a Dribbble shot, not a component library nobody adopted. Something that shipped, got used, and got better.
- You have taste, and you can defend it. Typography, spacing, motion, hierarchy. You notice when something is a few pixels off and you can explain why it matters.
- You build the whole thing. Design, frontend, the state and data it sits on. You don't hand the code to someone else once the Figma is done, and you don't hand the design to someone else once the code is.
- You can design for density. Expert users, complex workflows, hundreds of fields on a screen. Making that clear is much harder than making a landing page beautiful.
- You go to the source. You'll watch a technical reviewer work through a real file, and you'll design for what they actually do rather than what the process diagram says.
Signals we like, none of them required:
design engineering or front-end roles at somewhere like Linear, Vercel, Notion or Figma, a design system you built and maintained, work on interfaces where people review or correct AI output, founder or ex-founder, founding team experience, EF / YC / Antler, early or stealth-stage startup.
This is probably not for you if
- You want a strict boundary between work and life. We run one of the most ambitious startup cultures in Europe: fast paced, extremely high ownership, and in person in Shoreditch.
- You want a well-defined ticket handed to you each morning.
- You want to specialise narrowly and stay in your lane.
What you get
- Real equity, and compensation that reflects a high bar
- Genuine ownership of product surface area from day one, with the founders in the room
- Relocation support and visa sponsorship, handled properly
- Lunch and dinner covered, 24/7 gym access, and any tool that makes you faster
- A small team with high standards, high trust, and no politics
If this sounds like your kind of problem, apply. A short note on the hardest thing you've built goes further with us than a polished CV.

You'll join the team that owns iwoca's partner integrations — the Lending API and embedded flows that let third-party platforms, from major banks to fintechs, offer iwoca loans inside their own customer journeys. You'll own projects, collaborate with stakeholders, and design robust systems to deliver important functionality and measurably improve the experience for our partners and customers.
The company
Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don't wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that's as flexible and responsive as they are.

We've already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.
The team
iwoca partners with a variety of third-party platforms, ranging from large banks and comparison sites to small fintechs that serve SME customers. These partners use iwoca’s Lending API to embed iwoca loans into their own customer journey. Partnerships are an important and fast-growing source of customers for iwoca.
The Partner Flow team builds new features and optimises existing flows to provide the best possible experience for iwoca's partners and the customers they refer to us. The team’s responsibilities include:
- Continually improving our Lending API and other developer tools, so that partners can integrate with iwoca quickly and easily.
- Adding new functionality to facilitate deeper integrations and ensure iwoca is the best embedded finance provider on the market.
- Improving the conversion rate of customers who come to us through partners - streamlining the journey, running RCTs (randomised control trials) and building models alongside our embedded data scientist to find what works.
The team is made up of three engineers, a data scientist plus a team lead, working closely with an internal team of commercial stakeholders. This role is one of two new engineering hires as we grow the team to meet our ambition.
Partner Flow is remote/hybrid-friendly, meeting up for team days in the office once or twice a month, but not on a fixed schedule. They work in an Agile fashion with two-week sprints and a daily standup.
The role
You’ll work on challenging projects all over iwoca’s codebase - anywhere there are improvements to be made for partners and partner-referred customers. You’ll be encouraged to bring your own ideas and take responsibility for areas of functionality.
Autonomy:
- Own features and projects from scoping and design through to production.
- Collaborate with other engineers to meet the team’s goals, whilst being trusted to define your own solutions and work independently on your part of the problem.
- Design and maintain robust, flexible, and maintainable systems to ensure scalability and fast-paced development.
Impact:
- Deliver new functionality critical to onboarding important new partners.
- Run experiments (RCTs) and optimise the funnel to measurably improve how partner-referred customers convert.
- Leave code, docs, and processes in better shape than you found them.
Purpose and product thinking:
- Work on systems that genuinely help businesses get the funding they need.
- Collaborate with our partners and internal stakeholders to design effective solutions.
- Use data to make decisions, uncover insights, and refine strategies.
AI:
- We're pushing hard on AI-assisted development. Engineers here write clear technical specs, let skills and agents implement boiler-plate, and hold a high bar on code review — the person, not the model, is accountable for what merges. We expect AI output to be validated for correctness, performance and security like any other change.
- We give the team unlimited tokens across all models and expect people to experiment.
The requirements
Essential:
- Experience designing and building scalable back-end systems, ideally in Python.
- Experience working with relational databases, ideally PostgreSQL, with an understanding of performance and maintainability considerations.
- Experience building and maintaining APIs that are easy to use, reliable, and well-documented.
- Experience managing projects end to end, from understanding business problems to designing and delivering technical solutions.
- Pragmatism in balancing delivery speed with long-term system health.
- Clear, concise written and verbal communication, focusing on outcomes and impact.
- A genuine team player: you support your teammates, share knowledge, and care about the team's success as much as your own.
- AI fluency. Experience using AI coding tools to accelerate real delivery, and a genuine interest in getting better at it - with a pragmatic sense of where it adds value and where it doesn't.
Bonus:
- Front-end development experience, particularly with React and Typescript.
- Experience with DevOps practices, including containerisation and CI/CD pipelines.
- Experience with experimentation (e.g. A/B tests or RCTs) or using data to drive product decisions.
- Working knowledge of modern data tooling - ideally Snowflake and dbt - used to build analytical or reporting pipelines.
The salary
We expect to pay from £60,000—£85,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.
The culture
At iwoca, we prioritise a culture of learning, growth, and support, and invest in the development of our team members. We value thought and skill diversity, and encourage people to explore new areas of interest, adopt better tools – including AI – and apply sound judgement so our products and decisions improve over time.
The offices
We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:
- Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.
- Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.
The benefits

- A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:
- A learning and development budget for everyone.

jobs.description:
About Agicap
Created in Lyon in 2016 by three French entrepreneurs, Agicap is one of the fastest growing scale-ups in Europe, with over 8,000 customers, 600 employees and a rapid growth in turnover (multiplyed by 7 between 2021 and 2024). Agicap is part of French Tech 120, which rewards the most promising startups in France.
Agicap enables the financial branches of mid-size companies to effectively manage and forecast their cash flow, pay their suppliers and get paid. By combining a cash management system with accounts payable and accounts receivable management solutions on a single platform, Agicap aims to become the new benchmark for cash management for mid-size companies.
We have raised €145 million since our inception from prestigious venture capital funds such as AVP, Greenoaks, Partech and BlackFin, with a final round in November 2024.
These additional resources further fuel our product innovation, allowing us to grow significantly and accelerate our international expansion around the world.
We are convinced that our success lies in our passionate and dedicated teams committed to building a company where everyone can evolve and build their careers. We are constantly looking for new talent, aiming for excellence and ready to join our ambitious adventure!
Agicap is becoming an AI-first company. We train all of our employees to work with AI and automate some of their tasks themselves. Some projects are too long, too transversal or too technical to be carried by a business team alone.
This is the role of the AI Lab.
It is the pivotal team that builds the internal tools that change the way Agicap works daily. Our compass: quick operational impact, short iterations, 360° work with all teams (Sales, CS, Finance, Product, Marketing, Data, C-level).
It is a job creation: the acceleration of AI changes our processes and how we work. Senior reinforcement is needed to support this transition and to integrate it into long-term practices.
The team you're about to join:
- 4 people, you included: a junior AI engineer, a half-time Lead Tech (who will be your manager), a Product Manager.
- Your role: to bring the technical setback that is lacking in the team today (infra, architecture, maintenance, scalability) — to build quickly, but without digging debt for tomorrow.
- You're in direct contact with all Agicap's business teams: it's a very transverse, highly exposed position.

You alternate between quick framing, build and iteration:
- Understand the need for a live business team, frame what really has impact vs. which is comfort, prioritize.
- Build the internal tools from end to end: framing → dev → running → iteration with users.
- Evolving the common AI platform: MCP servers, integrations, transverse tools made available to the entire company.
- Make the technical decisions that structure the Lab: infra, choice of stack, architecture. There's no heavy existance to conform to, you build to scaler.
- Raise the technical level of the team: mentoring of the junior AI Engineer, transmission of good practices, useful code review.
- Proactively identify processes where AI brings real gain — and build the solution.
Examples of projects in your first 6 months:
- Feedback loop product: build a system that digests all customer feedback logs (calls, RFP, CS climbs) and produces prioritized recommendations for Product Managers. Today the data exists but it is not digested.
- Building infra MCP: providing Agicap employees with MCP servers connected to their everyday tools, on a scale.
How we work:
- Total autonomy: team of 3, you decide, you assume your choices.
- Ship rate high: we deliver daily, we measure, we iterate.
- IA daily in delivery: we use Claude, OpenAI, Mistral daily to build — we don't observe wave IA, we're in.
- English required: many employees are English-speaking. Your relationship is francophone.
The profile sought:
We aim for a senior profile with experience of Tech Lead — someone who has already made impacting decisions, pushed demanding technical topics, and actively explored the IA field:
- ~4-5 years of minimum experience in dev, on projects actually put into production.
- Experience of Tech Lead or equivalent: you have already driven decisions of architecture and infra, you know how to arbitrate between speed and debt.
- Practical and recent practice of LLMs: you have tried things, pushed experiments, tested Claude / OpenAI / Mistral. You're a motor on these subjects, not a follower.
- Python and TypeScript in your toolbox. Language counts less than your ability to choose the right tool for the right problem.
- Solid technical bases: you master and understand what you are delivering.
- Ability to deliver quickly and prioritize what really has impact — Doer mode, not powerpoint mode.
- Proactivity and curiosity: you identify opportunities that no one has formulated, you will seek.
- Common professional English.
- Autonomy assumed: in a team of 3, you cannot hide.
• Stack and tooling
- LLMs: Claude (Anthropic), OpenAI, Mistral — the team is not mono-provider, you choose the right model for the right use.
- Languages: mostly Python and TypeScript.
- Infra: it's up to you to build it, with a real right of decision—no heavy existence.
- Internal AI tools: MCP servers, common AI platform, agents connected to business tools.
- Cycle: Continuous Delivery, daily production, direct user feedback.
What We Offer
- A direct and visible impact position in an AI-first company of 600 people.
- A highly responsible framework: autonomy, ownership, technical decisions at your level.
- Remuneration : 55K€ - 70K€ according to expertise + vacation bonus SYNTEC.
- CDI, package in hours, 39 hours including 4 hours extra paid.

Recruitment process:

- Two technical interviews with the AI Lab team (formats and topics communicated upstream).
Feedback within 24-48 hours at each stage. Fast, transparent process.

jobs.title: Applied ML Engineer/Data Scientist
jobs.description:
🍇 About grape:
Our entrepreneurial spirit drives us in what we do and what we are passionate about. Our mission is to become the premier health partner in the insurance business. Recognising the need for innovation in the traditional employee insurance model we are set to revolutionize the employee insurance industry. We help companies support people before and after they get sick and to make more of their time. Our insurance solutions reduce monotonous and manual work for employees, doctors, HR & payroll managers. As we strive to lead a technology-driven transformation, we put employees first.
At grape we pride ourselves on our people and our culture. We continue to grow fast and that’s where you come in. Our team is dynamic, diverse and full of creative ideas. Want to join? We can’t wait to get to know you!
Your role
Our data and tech give us an edge in risk assessment, pricing and premium calculation. This role turns that into accurate models that support our carrier partners and our growth, builds tuned models where they beat rules and off-the-shelf LLMs in claims (triage, intervention, return-to-work, fraud), and responsibly explores how data can help employees stay healthy through grape Care.
We’re looking for an applied ML engineer / data scientist to build predictive models from the ground up on real, regulated insurance data. You’ll own problems end to end, from effective-dated records to production, in a domain where correctness and responsible use genuinely matter.
Starting points include pricing and risk, portfolio monitoring, claims and payment patterns, triage and return-to-work, absence, and fraud detection. grape sits on a rich dataset, though, and you’ll help find the next high-value use cases. You’re candid about what the data can support, and you propose simpler approaches when they’re the right answer.
This is not an LLM role. LLM and agent workflows and document extraction sit with our engineering teams, and you’ll use their outputs as features.
What you'll do:
Build and validate models
- Own the full model lifecycle: feature engineering, training, evaluation, explainability, deployment, and drift monitoring.
- Backtest on the historical book and run models in shadow mode alongside human decision-makers, reporting where and why they disagree.
- Produce audit-ready validation and governance documentation that actuarial, compliance, and carrier partners can review.
Platform and MLOps
- Deploy models on grape’s cloud platform within strict security and data-residency requirements for health data.
- Set up experiment tracking, model versioning, and production monitoring, partnering with engineering on integration.
Shape the problem space
- Identify and prioritize high-value use cases as you explore the dataset, rather than waiting to be handed problems.
- Turn ambiguous business questions into well-defined, measurable modelling.
Responsible & explainable by design
- Build privacy, fairness, and explainability into every model that touches personal or health data, working with compliance and legal on nDSG/GDPR boundaries.
- Models support decisions; accountable owners make them. Pricing, reserving, and claims work requires licensed-actuary sign-off, and any automation requires governance approval first.
Collaborate
- Explain model behavior and limits to underwriting, claims, actuarial, and compliance teams.
What you'll need:
- Strong applied ML and statistics: supervised and unsupervised learning, anomaly detection, time-series, and survival/duration modeling.
- Proven experience building models on real-world, relational, effective-dated data, including imbalanced outcomes.
- Fluent Python (pandas, scikit-learn, a modern ML stack) and strong SQL.
- Solid grasp of validation, calibration, and explainability (e.g. SHAP).
- Production MLOps: experiment tracking, versioning, and drift monitoring.
- Sound judgment on data privacy and modelling.
- Fluent English.
- Bias for action, ownership, and clear cross-functional communication.
Big plus:
- Insurance, actuarial, or risk modeling (pricing, reserving, loss ratios).
- Health, disability, or absence data, especially Swiss insurance (KTG, UVG); fraud detection in claims.
- Regulated special-category data under nDSG/GDPR, or model risk management.
- Google Cloud, including security-restricted deployments.
- German language skills.
🤝 What we offer in return:
🌱 Empowering workplace: Join a passionate team and an empowering workplace where you are given the ownership, tools, and support to make decisions and take initiative. Together we grow and build innovative solutions.
💻 Hybrid setup: Enjoy the flexibility of our hybrid work schedule, with the freedom to work remotely or from our office in Zurich. On Thursdays, our team day, we meet together in our Zurich office.
🪑 Home office stipend: To enable our hybrid setup, we allocate a one-off CHF 200.- home office budget to help you set up your dream workspace in the comfort of your own home.
🌐 Internet allowance: We give you a monthly internet allowance to help cover your internet costs at home and enable you to work seamlessly from your home office.
⏳ Flexible working time: You can distribute your working hours the way you want to.
🧠 Learning budget: We support you in improving your skills, acquiring new knowledge and advancing your career. We also allocate a CHF 1'500.- budget annually
❤️‍🩹 Well-being: Work-life balance is important to us and we foster a supportive work environment. We support you with mental health sessions with our partner Aepsy.
🎫 Team events: Every month we gather for fun and engaging events where we can connect and bond with our colleagues and our teams.
✈️ Team retreats: Once a year we travel somewhere nice to bond with our colleagues.
🚂 Travel and commute: We will cover your SBB half fare card, so we can spend some time together in the office.
🌴 Paid vacation: You get 5 weeks (25 days) of paid vacation every year and 2 additional days of paid vacation to compensate for canton-related holidays, religious holidays, birthdays, etc. The total amount of paid vacation days per year is 27 days.
🧖‍♀️ Wellness budget: Health and well-being looks different for everyone. You can optimize your wellness budget to best fit your needs.
👨‍👨‍👦‍👦 Parental and adoptive leave: We offer additional time off to support employees who are balancing family and work time in the most crucial stages of family life.
✈️ Digital nomad: For every 3 years of employment, you can work for an extended period of time from anywhere in the world (location subject to review).
🏁 Our recruitment process
We place particular emphasis on four areas when making our selection decision: professional and technical skills, mindset & values. We evaluate these through the following steps:
Step 1 - Your motivation
To get to know you better, we invite you to a 30-minute motivational interview with our Talent Acquisition Team.
Step 2 - Role fit
In the first interview, we assess how well your qualifications and skills align with the role requirements. This discussion will take place with your Hiring Manager.

For roles with higher technical demands, we will invite you to complete a case study or technical assessment. This allows us to better evaluate your specific skills and problem-solving abilities.
Step 4 - Our culture connect
Throughout the interview process, you'll gain insight into our company culture, and we'll explore how your values and mindset align with our ways of working. The final interview will offer a deeper look into this connection, along with broader discussions about the role and our vision.
Our diverse experiences, perspectives, and voices make us the company we are, and we would love to learn more about you!

With well-being at the core, we foster an environment where ideas and people thrive. Your growth matters as much as our mission. Whether it’s supporting your self-care, developing new solutions, or redefining how health and insurance connect, we grow together.
Our values guide us every step of the way: keeping Health at Heart, Inventing Together, and always striving to Embrace Clarity.

jobs.title: Senior Backend & AI Engineer (Remote)
jobs.description:
This role is open only to candidates living in the EU or EEA. We can't consider applications from other locations.
If you've built something before, start here
The hardest part of a startup usually isn't the code. It's finding customers who really need what you build and getting them to change how they work. At Scalera, that part is done: manufacturers, suppliers and contractors across Switzerland, Austria and Germany already run their tenders through us every day.
What we need now are people who can take the next unsolved problem and turn it into a product customers can't do without. If you've founded a company (whether it worked out or not), been the first engineer somewhere, or built something people paid for, this role was written for you.
About Scalera
Scalera is an ETH Zurich spin-off building AI for the €200B+ European construction industry. Large manufacturers and suppliers still run their most document-heavy processes by hand, from reading 300-page tenders to retyping purchase orders into their ERP. We automate them one by one. Our product matching already handles 1,400 tender positions in 16 minutes at 98% precision, work that used to take a sales rep most of a day.
What you'll do
You'll be part product manager, part engineer. You'll spend real time with customers and help shape what we build. Sometimes you'll spot the next problem yourself, and sometimes we'll hand you a clear priority to run with.
- Spend real time with customers. Join calls and site visits, sit with the people who do the work, and understand why they do it the way they do. You'll know their problems firsthand, not from a ticket.
- Shape what to build. Turn what you hear into a clear problem, a scope and a plan, and push back when the obvious request isn't the real need. When we bring you a priority, you'll own how it gets solved.
- Build it. Design and build backend services in Go and Python that turn messy tenders, catalogs and purchase orders into data customers can rely on.
- Ship, then check. Get it in front of customers fast, watch how they actually use it, and iterate.
- Own it in production. When something breaks at a customer, it's yours to understand and fix.
- Build with AI. Use AI heavily in how you work, and design systems that agents can use as well as people.
What success looks like after 3 months
- There's a part of the product people now think of as yours, and you're the one deciding what happens to it next
- You've spotted a problem nobody asked you to solve, made the case for it, and shipped a first version
- You've shipped features from both sources: priorities we set and ideas from your own customer conversations
- At least once, you've talked us out of building something customers didn't really need
- You've left a part of the platform simpler than you found it
You'll probably thrive here if
- You've taken something from zero to one: a company, a product line, or a side project with paying users
- You've built and run backend systems in production that other people depend on. We care more about your judgment than your language; you're strong in Go or Python and happy to work in both
- You're solid on data modeling, API design and messy real-world data
- You'd rather talk to a customer than wait for a spec
- You're comfortable with ambiguity. You can make progress while the problem is still half-defined, which at a startup it usually is
- You want a large scope of responsibility and are happy to own things well beyond your job title
- Rapidly changing requirements don't throw you. When customers or priorities shift, you adapt and keep going
- You enjoy direct customer contact and want to be on customer calls
- You make things simpler over time, not more clever
- You write clearly in English. German is a plus, not a requirement
You probably won't enjoy it if
- You just want to code and go home
- You don't like talking to customers, whether on calls or on the occasional site visit
- Ambiguity and chaos bother you
- You want a well-defined backlog handed to you
- Your main goal is managing people soon. Here, scope grows with what you own, not with headcount
Our stack
Go and Python (FastAPI), PostgreSQL, GCP, and LLMs throughout the document pipeline. You don't need to know all of it on day one.
How we hire
- Screening call (30 min) with our VP Engineering. It's two-way: ask us anything, including the hard questions.
- Technical deep-dive call: walk us through something you built from scratch, the decisions you made and what went wrong.
- Meet Scalera Day: join us remotely to work on a real problem with real (anonymized) construction documents, and meet the team.
- Offer: if it's a fit on both sides, we'll move quickly to an offer.
Working at Scalera
- Remote within the EU or EEA
- Small team, no bureaucracy. You'll work directly with the CEO, CTO, VP Engineering and Customer Success
- Competitive compensation
Founders and former founders: if you're unsure whether you fit, send a few lines about what you built and why you moved on. We read every one.

Most ML jobs hand you a benchmark. This one hands you a business problem with paying customers and their real data. Construction tenders are long, messy and full of trade jargon, and every decision a customer makes on our platform becomes a labeled example you can train on.
We need someone who can turn that data into models that customers notice: from the first experiment to the model serving production traffic, and back again when a customer says it got something wrong. If you've founded a company (whether it worked out or not), been the first ML engineer somewhere, or shipped a model people paid for, this role was written for you.

Scalera is an ETH Zurich spin-off building AI for the €200B+ European construction industry. We automate that work one process at a time, and ML sits at the center of every one of them.

You'll own the ML behind our products, end to end. In practice that means:
- Training and fine-tuning: embedding models, rerankers, classifiers and LLMs, trained on our own data.

- Evaluation: offline benchmarks, per-customer evals and gates that keep a new model from shipping if it makes things worse.

- Retraining runs automatically, and nothing reaches customers without passing an eval you designed.
- You've cut LLM cost or latency by replacing an expensive step with a smaller model of your own.

About The Role
About the role
We are looking for a Senior Data Analyst, Lifecycle to own measurement and experimentation for how new customers activate and existing ones stay.The metrics are yours whatever the lever: CRM campaigns, promos and incentives, onboarding changes in the product, and a next best action layer that decides what each customer should see next. You decide what we test, how we test it and what we do with the answer. You also bring your own hypotheses on where the next win is.
What You'll Do
What you'll do
Join activation and retention initiatives before anything is built, whether they come from CRM, growth or product. Define the primary metric, check against historical data whether the effect is detectable at our volumes, and turn solution-shaped requests into problem-shaped ones.
Design and analyse experiments end to end: hypothesis, guardrails, audience split, MDE and power, stopping rule, and a readout that ends in ship, iterate or kill.
Correct for channel and engagement bias (not everyone opens email, and open and click populations are self-selected). When a clean A/B is impossible, use causal inference: diff-in-diff, matching, synthetic control or geo designs.
Bring hypotheses of your own. Launch a few new experiments across onboarding and the customer lifecycle, and turn one-off wins into recurring segmented flows.
Build deliberately simple models: segmentation, propensity, churn and dormancy scoring. They feed audiences, personalisation and incentive targeting. Over time these come together into next best action: for a given customer, which offer, feature nudge or message to send next, through which channel, and whether to send anything at all. You own the logic and the measurement of whether it beats the current rules.
Automate your own recurring work: audience refresh jobs, readout templates, dashboards for Activation, Onboarding and Retention. Ship models the Databricks way (scheduled jobs write tables, tables map into downstream tools such as Braze) and bring engagement data back into the warehouse to close the loop.

Predictive modelling with honest validation. Uplift modelling is a plus.

Braze or a comparable CRM platform: audiences, canvases, native split testing, channel mechanics and their biases.

We work closely with the OpenTelemetry SIGs to make OpenTelemetry SDKs and instrumentation libraries a success. Members of this team are experts in at least one programming language and have a broad knowledge of various other programming languages.
In this role, you will focus on a language-specific implementation of OpenTelemetry in Python, with an emphasis on OpenTelemetry for Generative AI. You will get to work in an upstream-first approach, helping accelerate the OpenTelemetry project while bringing the innovations to Grafana labs products and offerings.

What You’ll Be Doing:
You will bring your software engineering expertise to develop improvements to the OpenTelemetry Python SDK and instrumentation libraries, with a strong focus on AI applications and agent workflows. This is a hands-on role for someone with deep Python expertise and an interest in AI.
- Collaborate in open-source communities. You will develop and maintain the OpenTelemetry Python SDK and instrumentation libraries, working with maintainers and other vendors on specifications, APIs, and implementation decisions.
- Build Python instrumentation for AI agents. Build instrumentation that connects agent runs, model calls, and tool execution, including across asynchronous code. Contribute to evolving OpenTelemetry conventions for generative AI, with care for sensitive data and metric cardinality.
- Improve Python SDK performance. Use profiling and benchmarks to evaluate implementation approaches with the upstream community. Make sound tradeoffs around runtime overhead, compatibility, and maintainability.
- Be visible as an OpenTelemetry expert. Teach others, promote best practices around OpenTelemetry, semantic conventions, and various technologies and frameworks. Both within Grafana Labs and in the broader OpenTelemetry community.
- Support the technical direction and vision of the team, and contribute to business conversations on the OpenTelemetry strategy at Grafana Labs. Own projects from an ambiguous problem through design, implementation, testing, documentation, and release.
- Partner in an open and respectful way. Lend your knowledge and skills to our GTM, Product and Support teams. Join customer conversations, investigate instrumentation issues, and turn what you learn into fixes and practical guidance.
As we are remote-first and our engineering organization is largely remote, we provide guidance and meet regularly using video calls, so high agency and good communication skills are a must.
What Makes You a Great Fit:
At Grafana Labs, Staff Engineers are defined by the impact they have and the people they enable. You take ownership of complex problems, set technical direction, and help others deliver improvements that matter to customers and the OpenTelemetry community.
- 8+ years of experience in software development, with strong proficiency in Python and experience debugging production software, language internals, libraries, and asynchronous code.
- An interest in AI applications and agent systems, and curiosity about how to instrument and troubleshoot them. Prior experience building AI systems is helpful, but not required.
- Experience working in open-source communities. You are eager to become an active member of the OpenTelemetry community, collaborate with maintainers and users, and keep learning across languages, frameworks, and the wider observability ecosystem.
- Familiarity with observability tooling such as Grafana, Prometheus, and OpenTelemetry, alongside experience with cloud-based software or systems engineering. You understand production environments and can assess operational risks.
Bonus Points For:
- You have experience working on open source observability projects, ideally in OpenTelemetry or Prometheus.
- Experience in Python instrumentation techniques, profiling, runtime diagnostics, or asynchronous context propagation
- Experience in a hands-on technical leadership role, setting technical direction and leading project teams
- Experience instrumenting AI frameworks or agent workflows, or working with OpenTelemetry semantic conventions for generative AI
- Experience contributing to or maintaining Open Source projects, with evidence of successful pull requests and community collaboration
- Rust experience is a plus for exploring potential Python SDK performance improvements, including Rust-backed implementations.
Compensation & Rewards:

All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success.
