jobs.description:
Our Mission:
Omnea is the agentic operating system for procurement.
Procurement touches every pound a business spends, yet requests still stall for weeks and approvals get lost in inboxes. Our AI-first platform changes that: our agents capture requests, route approvals, onboard suppliers, flag risk and track every renewal, while anyone in the business can ask a question and get an answer grounded in their own company’s data. Buying becomes painless for everyone, procurement gets a seat at the table, and our customers have saved more than 100,000 hours of manual work so far.
Companies like Spotify, PayPal, T. Rowe Price, JustEat, Adyen and S&P Global run procurement on Omnea. We’re backed by $75M from Khosla Ventures, Insight Partners and Accel, and we’ve been named the UK’s number one startup in the Startups 100, ranked 11th on Sifted’s 2026 list of Europe’s fastest-growing companies, and recognised as one of Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies.
Talent density matters more to us than almost anything else. We keep the bar high in every team, so everyone here has real ownership and real impact. Our team is full of former founders and operators who’ve scaled unicorns, and we’re looking for people who want to do the best work of their careers alongside them.
Find out more about the team and life at Omnea here.
Why We Need a Platform Security Engineer Now
Omnea takes security seriously. In an era where exploits and supply chain attacks are being discovered and conducted faster than ever before, it’s vital that we stay on the cutting edge of keeping our systems and our customers’ data safe.
Hardening our systems is only part of the solution. As we scale out to more industries with their diverse security requirements, we want another individual who can help us attain and maintain higher levels of compliance certification.
What We're Looking For
We're hiring at both Level 3 (Senior) and Level 4 (Staff). For calibration, candidates typically bring 5+ years of platform engineering experience in high-growth, cloud-native SaaS environments, but we care more about impact than years. We’re looking for that “T”-shaped skillset where the candidate’s depth is in Cloud Security.
Furthermore, the ideal candidate will have a product engineering background but caught the bug for security and cares deeply about enabling people to work fast, safely. Finally, we’re looking for someone who sees security as an enabler and force-multiplier and answers questions with a “Yes, here’s how we do it securely” attitude as opposed to the flat “No” security teams are too often renowned for.
What You'll Do
- Implement and take ownership of our Security roadmap. Working with the Platform Lead, a successful candidate will steadily take ownership over the Platform Security Roadmap, leading implementations and experiments to level up Omnea’s security posture.
- Own Security Tooling. From safe-chain plugins to SAST/DAST tooling, we want someone who’s keen to get stuck in, onboard, and evolve our tooling to ensure our posture stays at the bleeding edge.
- Deliver Compliance Programs. Omnea plans to tackle multiple additional compliance certifications to enable the business to serve some of the most regulated industries on the planet. You’ll have a massive hand in making sure we’re up to those standards.
- Collaborate with our DevX streams. Omnea ships fast, and we want to ship even faster. Making sure we can enable that safely and securely will become your wheelhouse.
- Implement hardening patterns. See an area where code security could be improved? Let’s do it, and do it in a way that can be scaled out across the entire codebase and easily implemented by the rest of the engineering staff.
What Can You Expect?
- A strong team. You'll join a platform team of senior and staff engineers who set a high bar and will push you to do your best work.
- Modern, cloud-native stack. Everything serverless and IaC-driven (AWS, Pulumi, TypeScript end-to-end).
- Continuous delivery. We deploy multiple times a day. Your work determines how fast and safely the whole engineering org ships.
- Scalability challenges. As we 10x revenue, you'll be a part of evolving our infrastructure to defend against new security threats and keep us one step ahead.
- Customer impact. Delivering on our compliance goals and successfully handling audits.
- Massive ownership. You own problems end-to-end, from brainstorming through to production.
- Collaboration & autonomy. Plenty of heads-down technical work, but also close partnership with product engineers and engineering leadership.
About You
- Platform engineer & builder. You design reliable infrastructure and write clean production code (TypeScript or similar). You've built and maintained CI/CD pipelines, IaC, and security gates at scale.
- Cloud-native. Deep knowledge of AWS (Lambda, DynamoDB, EventBridge, IAM, networking), or equivalent cloud-native experience. You understand serverless and its trade-offs.
- Security as an enabler. You think about engineers and business as your customers. You automate toil, improve feedback loops, and care deeply about making other people productive.
- Commercially minded. You understand that infrastructure & security exist to serve the product and the business. You make trade-offs with that in mind.
- Bias for action. You iterate quickly, ship pragmatically, and automate everything.
- Culture carrier. You coach teammates, share knowledge freely, and keep calm when things break.
Nice-to-haves
- Experience with Pulumi or similar IaC frameworks.
- ISC2 (any level) certification.
- Experience running SaaS compliance programs (ISO:27001, SOC 2 Type II).
- Open-source contributions to security, infrastructure, or developer tooling projects.

jobs.description:
At Stark, we forge the future of European and national security through cutting-edge, AI-driven technology and unmatched engineering precision. As a premier defence technology company, our mission is clear: to equip NATO Allies and their partners with next-generation autonomous defence platforms and advanced AI-driven software built to perform in the world’s most demanding environments.

ABOUT THE TEAM
Our Production Quality team in Thessaloniki is the technical shield protecting the integrity of STARK’s next-generation autonomous systems. Operating directly on the production floor, we partner with assembly leads, technicians, and engineering teams to stand up resilient, high-yield manufacturing processes. We bridge precise structural mechanical builds with complex, high-reliability aerospace-grade electronics. We value absolute technical precision, structured problem-solving, and the proactive ownership required to safeguard zero-defect manufacturing standards.
YOUR MISSION
As our Quality Assurance Inspector, you will be the final gatekeeper of production standards on our assembly floor. Utilizing your combined knowledge of mechanical and electronics engineering, you will continuously review active assembly lines, verify build documentation, and ensure all mandatory inline steps are executed flawlessly. You will take end-to-end ownership of on-floor quality checks—collaborating closely with Manufacturing Engineers to identify assembly gaps, block defective parts, and update localized Control Plans so our processes are continuously improved.

- Define, update, and maintain dynamic Control Plans (CPs) for inline assemblies and final products based on real-time assembly data.
- Block defective products immediately, physically isolating and managing quarantined materials on the floor.
- Initiate and coordinate technical reworks, providing on-floor guidance to technicians and verifying that repaired systems meet original engineering standards before re-release.
- Perform final quality checks and outgoing document reviews before delivery, recording deviations in the QMS and creating precise Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs).
WHAT YOU BRING TO THE MISSION
- Education: Vocational diploma or technical degree in mechatronics, electronics, mechanical assembly, or a related field.
- Experience: 3+ years as a Quality Inspector, QA Specialist, or Lead Assembler in aerospace, automotive, or defense.
- Technical Skills: Strong practical understanding of both electronics (wiring, connectors) and mechanics (tolerances, fasteners, blueprints).
- Process Review & Control Plans: Proven ability to spot floor assembly gaps, collaborate with Manufacturing Engineers, and execute dynamic Control Plans (CPs).
- NCR Ownership & Languages: Experience managing non-conformances in QMS/ERP with professional working proficiency in English and Greek.
NICE TO HAVE
- Active certifications in IPC-A-610 and IPC/WHMA-A-620 standards.
- Familiarity with flight-critical avionics systems (flight controllers, power distribution boards, telemetry) or military-grade hardware, tactical defense systems, and UAS.
- Familiarity with ERP/QMS platforms (SAP QM, JIRA, CAQ) and basic training in Lean manufacturing, Kaizen, or Six Sigma.

jobs.title: Principal Penetration Tester
jobs.description:
At Dragos, the mission is personal. The systems we protect deliver the water you drink, power your home, and keep the hospitals your community depends on running. Those critical infrastructure systems that power our civilization around the world are under attack every day by adversaries. When those systems fail, people are immediately at risk. We are the global leader in xOT cybersecurity, combining technology, threat intelligence, and expert services. The people here chose this work because they understand what is at stake. Here, you will find a remote-first mission-driven team across North America, Europe, the Middle East, and APAC built on authenticity, transparency, and trust. If safeguarding the systems that protect your family, friends, and community is the kind of work that matters to you, you are in the right place.
About the Role:
Our Professional Services Team is seeking Associate Principal OT Penetration Tester who will provide technical leadership across vulnerability assessments, penetration testing, and adversary emulation activities supporting customer services engagements. You will shape engagement strategy and uncover real‑world attack paths across ICS/OT networks through hands‑on exploitation and deep technical analysis, working closely with customers across critical infrastructure sectors such as oil and gas, electric, water treatment, and manufacturing. You will also translate findings into clear, actionable remediation guidance, influencing detection and platform development. You will mentor team members and be an advisor and representative of Dragos within the broader OT security community.
Responsibilities:
- Serve as primary technical lead and trusted advisor for Dragos’s most complex, high-impact industrial penetration testing, purple teaming, and vulnerability assessment engagements, shaping engagement direction and aligning deep technical execution with client business goals.
- Set the technical bar for OT penetration testing excellence by defining methodologies, assessment frameworks, and red team tactics informed by threat intelligence and adversary emulation. Design and lead offensive campaigns modeled on known and unknown TTPs to uncover complex attack paths across IT/OT boundaries and within industrial environments.
- Translate hands-on findings into strategic R&D priorities, guiding the development of proprietary tools, behavioral analytics, and detection content by identifying gaps in visibility, response, and prevention in customer environments.
- Evolve internal playbooks, runbooks, and operating procedures, applying field lessons, threat intelligence, and emerging adversary behaviors to improve the efficiency, scalability, and effectiveness of the penetration testing practice.
- Engage executive stakeholders, internally and externally, with strategic cybersecurity guidance, risk prioritization, and remediation recommendations tied to business objectives, delivering clear, authoritative presentations to C-suites, boards, and technical leadership.
- Represent Dragos as an industry thought leader through original research, top-tier conference presentations, whitepapers, and public engagements that advance OT security with unique insights and innovation.
- Mentor engineering, threat intelligence, and consulting teams across functions, cultivating future leaders and a culture of continuous learning, technical curiosity, and mission-driven execution.
Qualifications:
- 8+ years of hands-on cybersecurity experience in vulnerability assessment, penetration testing, or red teaming within the OT space, with in-depth knowledge of OT penetration testing methodologies in white, gray, and black-box contexts.
- Deep understanding of OT-specific architectures and services, including DCS, historians, SCADA networks, transmission/distribution management, AMI, related communication protocols, and other control systems.
- Extensive knowledge of OT cyber threats, attack paths, exploits, and adversary TTPs.
- Hands-on experience with offensive security tooling such as Metasploit, Nmap, Kali Linux, Cobalt Strike, Burp Suite, common LOTL toolsets, and C2 frameworks.
- Advanced experience with networking components (routers, switches, load balancers, firewalls), plus the ability to analyze network traffic and host data in a cybersecurity context.
- Proven experience using large language models (e.g., Claude) to support penetration testing execution and reporting, including reconnaissance, exploit development, and drafting findings, with sound judgment in validating AI-generated output and securely handling client data.
- Strong report-writing and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
- Ability to work independently in a remote environment and coordinate across distributed teams, with willingness to travel up to 30-40% (domestic and international) to support customer engagements.

- Salary: £105,000
- Competitive Equity Package
- Comprehensive Benefits Plan

jobs.title: Solutions Architect – Digital Sovereignty
jobs.description:
FEQ128R99
Location: Germany (remote or from a Databricks office – anywhere in Germany) Languages: Fluent German and business-level English
At Databricks, we build the platform that makes data and AI usable across an entire organization. More and more of our customers in Germany – public sector, critical infrastructure (KRITIS), financial services, healthcare, defence and industry – need to keep control over where their data lives and who can access it. They want the full power of the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform without giving up data residency, jurisdictional control or the option to switch providers.
As a Solutions Architect for Digital Sovereignty, you are the technical lead for this motion in Germany. You design sovereign data and AI architectures with customers, run proofs of concept end to end, and help our sovereign cloud partners and account teams turn a proven pattern into production workloads.
The impact you will have
- Act as the trusted technical advisor on digital sovereignty for strategic and regulated customers across Germany, from the first conversation with the CIO/CISO through to production.
- Design and validate sovereign reference architectures
- Run complex proofs of concept and pilots – performance, scalability, security and network connectivity tests with different data volumes – and translate the results into clear go/no-go recommendations.
- Work hand in hand with sovereign cloud and storage partners: joint solution design, enablement of partner technical teams, co-selling and joint customer workshops.
- Position Databricks clearly in the sovereignty discussion – CLOUD Act, GDPR, NIS2, DORA, BSI C5, EU Data Act, open formats and exit strategies – and articulate how our open architecture reduces lock-in compared with competing approaches.
- Feed field requirements back to Databricks Product and Engineering, and collaborate with Legal, Security and Compliance on customer questions.
- Build repeatable assets: reference architectures, demos, PoC playbooks, Terraform/automation templates and customer-facing collateral in German and English.
- Build Databricks' visibility on sovereignty in the German market through workshops, meetups, webinars and conference talks.
- Turn customer conversations into working prototypes fast, using AI-assisted development to build demos in hours rather than weeks.
What we look for
- Fluent German and business-level English. Both are used daily with customers, partners and internally.
- Substantial experience in technical pre-sales, solution architecture or consulting, including complex enterprise customer interactions across the full sales lifecycle.
- Hands-on experience with data platforms in at least one major public cloud (Azure, AWS or GCP), ideally including Apache Spark and/or Databricks.
- Solid understanding of cloud infrastructure: networking (private connectivity, VPN, private endpoints), identity and access management, encryption and key management (BYOK/HYOK).
- Experience with object storage and open table formats (S3-compatible storage such as MinIO, Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg) and with secure data sharing patterns.
- Good working knowledge of the regulatory and sovereignty landscape in Germany and the EU (e.g. GDPR, CLOUD Act implications, NIS2, DORA, BSI C5, KRITIS) and the ability to discuss it confidently with CISOs, data protection officers and procurement.
- Ability to drive technical and business conversations with C-level executives, orchestrate cross-functional and partner teams, and influence outcomes toward long-term customer success.
- Hands-on coding ability in Python and SQL; infrastructure-as-code experience (e.g. Terraform) is a plus.
- Daily, fluent use of AI tools in your own work. Coding assistants and agents are part of how you operate, not something you try out occasionally.
- Able to vibe-code a demo: assemble a credible, working prototype for a specific customer problem with AI assistance, and recognize where the output still needs your own judgment.
- Experience working with or for European / sovereign cloud providers, public sector or regulated industries is a strong plus.
- Judgment to prioritize the right use cases and investments, and to navigate a competitive landscape.
- Willingness to travel within Germany for customer and partner meetings.
Why this role
- You will shape a new, strategically important motion for Databricks in Germany and EMEA – building on a proof of concept that has already delivered results.
- You will work at the intersection of data and AI, cloud infrastructure, regulation and partnerships.
- You will collaborate closely with Field Engineering leadership, Product, and our partner ecosystem.

jobs.title: Senior Embedded (ARM) Engineer - Quantum Computing (m/w/d)
jobs.description:
eleQtron develops and operates full-stack quantum computers based on trapped-ion technology. Quantum computing is a new computing paradigm rapidly approaching commercial viability. Our unique approach combines laser-cooled trapped ions with microwave control and tailored magnetic fields. Our next-generation computing machines under development will be able to find solutions to problems that are out of reach today, thus enabling new innovative products and services for a brighter future.
We are looking for a Senior Embedded (ARM) Engineer (m/f/d) to join us in Hamburg or Siegen and own the real-time firmware that turns our control electronics into a working quantum computer. You will work on our next-generation system, where the control electronics are being integrated into a single, highly integrated chip. You sit at the heart of the machine, between the hardware that generates the pulses and the higher-level software that describes the experiments. Timing is not a detail here; it is the product. You are the person who makes sure the right signal reaches the ions at the right nanosecond, reliably, run after run.
Responsibilities:
- Own the embedded firmware on our ARM-based control platform, from architecture through implementation to on-hardware debugging
- Develop and maintain the real-time software layer that coordinates pulse sequencing, timing, and data flow across our highly integrated control chip
- Write and maintain the low-level drivers and board support the hardware relies on
- Guarantee deterministic, low-latency behaviour under hard real-time constraints
- Lead firmware bring-up together with our electronics and physics teams, and debug at the boundary where software meets signal
- Define the firmware architecture and engineering practices — build, test, and release processes for the embedded layer as the system matures
- Contribute to the interfaces between the embedded layer and the rest of the stack, so experiments defined in software run correctly on the machine
Required Skills:
- 5+ years of professional embedded software development for real-time or timing-critical systems
- Deep command of C (and ideally C++) on ARM platforms, working close to the hardware
- Experience with bare-metal and/or RTOS environments, and a clear understanding of when each is appropriate
- Comfortable reading schematics and datasheets, and debugging real hardware with oscilloscopes, logic analysers, and JTAG
- Strong grasp of real-time concepts: interrupts, DMA, timing, concurrency, and determinism
- A track record of bringing up firmware on new hardware, not only maintaining existing systems
- Ability to collaborate effectively with experimental physicists and engineers, and to turn imprecise physical requirements into robust firmware
- Strong adaptability and a quick learning mindset
- Good proficiency in English (written and spoken)
Nice to have (Bonus)
- Experience on highly integrated SoCs, particularly ARM+FPGA platforms such as Xilinx Zynq / RFSoC
- Working alongside FPGA/digital-electronics engineers at the software–gateware boundary

jobs.description:
What do we do?
Paddle offers digital product companies a completely different approach to their payment infrastructure. Instead of assembling and maintaining a complex stack of payments-related apps and services, we’re a Merchant of Record for our customers. That means we take away 100% of the pain of payment fragmentation. It’s faster, safer, cheaper, and, above all, way better.
We’re backed by investors including KKR, FTV Capital, Kindred, Notion, and 83North and serve over 10,000 software sellers in 245 territories globally.
The role:
We are looking for a Head of Data Science to build Paddle's data science capability from the ground up. Our Merchant of Record model gives us a data position no PSP or billing provider has: subscription and pricing context alongside granular payment-outcome data, across thousands of software businesses. This role exists to turn that into economic value by putting machine learning and agentic systems into production.
The mandate is deliberately narrow and deliberately ambitious: data science at Paddle owns automated decisioning inside the product — traditional machine learning and agentic systems alike — not decision-support analytics.
We have a long list of candidate opportunities than we can fund, spanning payment performance and revenue recovery, sales and marketing operations, growth and monetisation intelligence, and risk, trust and compliance. We have a working hypothesis about which of these pays back first, and we'll share it — but part of the job in your first quarter is to pressure-test it, size the alternatives yourself, and tell us where to start.
This is a founding role, and for the first few quarters it is a building role more than a managing one. You'll be the only person in the function: doing the analysis, engineering the features, training and evaluating the models or agents, taking the first system live with our engineering teams — and then operating it, answerable for its uptime, its drift and its numbers. Once the first use cases are proving out, you'll hire and lead a hub-and-spoke team of data scientists and machine learning engineers embedded across our highest-value business areas. You'll report into the VP of Data and work in close partnership with Product, Payments, Engineering, Risk and Finance.
What you'll do:
- Prioritise which opportunities have the biggest impact.. Build a value-based use-case backlog across payment performance and revenue recovery, sales and marketing operations, growth and monetisation intelligence, and risk, trust and compliance; size the leading candidates properly; and make the call on sequencing with the relevant Product, Risk, RevOps and Finance stakeholders. This gets refreshed quarterly.
- Personally deliver the first system end to end: the analysis and back-test, the features, the model, policy or agent, the deployment, and the shadow and A/B tests that prove it works. Not a spec handed to someone else to build.
- Operate what you deploy. Own monitoring, retraining, drift response, incident handling and rollback for live decisioning, alongside the engineering teams whose services call it — and set the expectation that the function runs its systems rather than shipping them.
- Work across both traditional ML and agentic systems, and be honest about which a problem actually needs: a propensity or uplift model, a policy of rules, or an agent with tools, evals against golden answer sets and trace-level observability. Several of our strongest candidate use cases point each way.
- Build and lead the team — hire senior data scientists embedded in value areas and machine learning engineers in the hub, and set the professional standards, shared methods and reusable components the function runs on.
- Establish the production stack alongside Data Platform and Engineering: reproducible training data, code and artefacts; a model registry; inference services with real latency, availability and rollback requirements; historically accurate features where decisions need backdated reconstruction; eval harnesses and trace observability for agentic workflows; and monitoring for data quality, drift, model performance and economic outcomes. Start ad hoc where that's sufficient and platformise once the first use cases have shown what's actually needed.
- Own value capture end to end. Shadow-test and A/B test every deployment against the incumbent strategy, translate metric movement into a financial number on a methodology co-signed by Finance, and publish a quarterly report on realised value.
- Set the governance model for automated decisioning — proportionate risk assessment, clear ownership, latency and availability requirements, human escalation and rollback — working with Legal, Privacy, Compliance and Risk on GDPR, EU AI Act and payments obligations, and producing the evidence early enough to shape the design.
- Define the boundaries and the working relationship with Product Science, Analytics Engineering, Data Platform and AI Enablement, so accountability for decision support versus automated decisioning stays unambiguous.
- Deliver cross-functionally: embed in delivery groups with product owners, domain experts and platform engineers rather than handing models over the wall.
We'd love to hear from you if you:
- Experienced leading data science or ML teams that own systems in production, with deployments that moved a commercial metric and kept running afterwards. Proofs of concept and dashboards are not what we're hiring for.
- Hands-on now, not formerly. Your first quarters are spent writing SQL and Python, engineering features, evaluating models and agents, and doing the work that gets a system live — not reviewing someone else's.
- Experienced across both traditional ML and agentic systems, and clear about how they differ in practice: propensity and uplift models, feature pipelines and drift on one side; tool and context design, prompt and retrieval iteration, evals against golden answer sets and trace observability on the other.
- Practised at running live systems rather than just launching them — monitoring, retraining, incident response, rollback, and the on-call reality of a decision the business depends on.
- Pragmatic about method: happy to argue for rules or heuristics where they capture most of the value, and to reserve models and agents for where they genuinely earn their keep.
- Comfortable with an undefined starting point. There's a long list of candidate use cases and a strong internal hypothesis, but no fixed roadmap — you'll be expected to form your own view, back it with numbers, and defend it to an executive audience.
- Strong on measurement — experimentation, uplift modelling, back-testing — and willing to hold your own work to a financial number that Finance will scrutinise.
- Fluent in the engineering side of production ML and agents (training pipelines, model registries, inference services, feature stores, drift detection, trace observability) and able to hold your own with senior engineers on latency, availability, observability and rollback.
- Able to hire, level and develop senior data scientists and ML engineers, and to set standards for a function that doesn't exist yet.
- Credible with executives and commercial stakeholders: you can take a use case from business problem to value estimate to prioritisation decision, and say no to low-value work.
- Experienced in payments, fintech, subscriptions, high-volume commercial operations or another regulated transactional domain — enough to get to a credible value estimate in a new area quickly.
- Comfortable treating regulated ML as a design constraint rather than paperwork — model risk assessment, DPIAs, auditability, traceability of model and policy versions to production decision logic.
Everyone is welcome at Paddle
At Paddle, we’re committed to removing invisible barriers, both for our customers and within our own teams. We recognise and celebrate that every Paddler is unique and we welcome every individual perspective. As an inclusive employer, we don’t care if, or where, you studied, what you look like or where you’re from. We’re more interested in your craft, curiosity, passion for learning and what you’ll add to our culture. We encourage you to apply even if you don’t match every part of the job ad, especially if you’re part of an underrepresented group.
Please let us know if there’s anything we can do to better support you through the application process and in the workplace. We will do everything we can to support any accommodations needed. We’re committed to building a diverse team where everyone feels safe to be their authentic self. Let’s grow together.
Why you’ll love working at Paddle
We’re a diverse, growing group of Paddlers who pride ourselves on our transparent, collaborative and respectful culture.
We live and breathe our values, which are:
- Paddle Together - “None of us, is as smart as all of us”
- Paddle Simply - “Simple can be harder than complex: you have to get your thinking clean to make it simple”
- Paddle for others - “We can realise our wildest dreams, so long as we help enough other people to realise theirs”
We offer a full suite of benefits, including attractive salaries, stock options, unlimited holidays, enhanced parental leave, retirement plans, private healthcare and well-being initiatives.
We invest in learning and will help you with your personal development via constant exposure to new challenges, an annual learning fund, and regular internal and external training.
Connecting at Paddle
We’re a ‘digital-first’ company, which means our Paddlers always have the freedom to choose where, when and how they work within our hub locations.
We recognize that where our Paddlers do their best work is unique to them and we provide trust and autonomy for everyone to work in a way which fits them best. We also value the power of connection and have invested in global hubs which help local communities flourish and bring us together for focused collaboration.
Our Paddle hubs:
- In Europe: UK (London headquarters), Portugal (Lisbon hub), Netherlands and Ireland (Dublin hub)
- In North America: Austin, TX (USA) and Toronto (Canada)
- In APAC: Singapore
Our hub philosophy creates an engaging experience for all Paddlers, wherever, whenever and however we choose to work.
To support this, we focus hiring within our hubs and will always openly share the available locations for each open position on our job description.

jobs.title: Software Engineer (Frontend) - London
jobs.description:
About Us
Teton is redefining the role of healthcare workers through cutting-edge AI technology and a great product experience. As populations get older and staff shortages grow, healthcare systems are under pressure. Our mission is to decrease the cost of healthcare while improving the quality of care.
Our product enables care teams to intervene, prevent and operate more efficiently. Our ambient sensors in resident rooms capture activity, sleep, respiration, gait and more. These signals are used both to react fast to risk events, like falls, and for long-term health analysis that care teams can act on.
Teton is scaling fast, operating in the Nordics, UK, DACH and US. We recently raised a $20M Series A. Expect travel to the US to meet users and team members.
We focus relentlessly on product excellence and user experience, deploying solutions at speed that make a tangible difference for carers. We are an aspiring meritocracy biased towards action, always striving to raise the bar. If you are driven by impact, speed and leveling up, this might be the place for you.
If you are looking for a 9-17 job, perform best with structure and struggle dealing with unknowns, this is not for you. We believe close collaboration between a hard-working, high-agency team enables the fastest and most efficient iteration cycles, helping us build an impactful product that healthcare professionals truly love to use.
The Job
We're looking for an experienced Frontend Engineer to own customer-facing features from the first conversation with a care team to the feature running in production. Care workers rely on our product during every shift and care managers use it to follow up on their residents, on mobile and on the web. This isn't a ticket-taking role. You'll talk to users, cut scope, build the features, and check afterwards whether what you shipped actually made a shift easier. Alongside that, you'll help own the quality of how we build: the tests, pipelines and guardrails that let us ship fast without breaking what care teams depend on.
In this role, you will focus on:
- Feature Development: Own features end-to-end, from design discussions through implementation to production rollout across multiple markets and languages, on the web app, the mobile app and the APIs behind them.
- Customer Insight: Talk to care staff and our customer success team every week, visit care facilities, and turn what you hear into clearly scoped product changes. Come with ideas, sketch the solution, and push it forward.
- Code Quality & Guardrails: Help own code quality across the frontend. Improve our CI/CD pipelines and automated tests, keep the infrastructure scalable, and build the guardrails that let AI coding agents contribute safely.
- Backend & APIs: Work with the APIs, data models and services your features need. You will not just consume APIs, you will help shape, improve and fix the systems behind them.
- Quality, Privacy & Safety: Ship with care for health data: sensible access control, auditability and privacy by default. Use staged rollouts so new features never get in the way of the alerts care teams depend on.
Qualifications
- Several years of experience building production web applications.
- Strong TypeScript skills: this is the language for everything we build.
- Solid production experience with React on the web and/or React Native.
- Experience with CI/CD and automated testing, and a strong sense of what good code quality looks like.
- Great product taste and a keen eye for UX. You work well with designers and can make sensible design decisions yourself when needed.
- Comfortable talking directly with non-technical users and turning messy feedback into concrete decisions.
- Previous startup experience and/or shipping a product where you owned the outcome, from idea to adoption.X
- Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work both independently and in a team.
Nice to Have
- Experience with React Native and Expo in production.
- Experience working with AI coding agents in a real codebase.
- AWS or equivalent cloud platform experience.
- Familiarity with TanStack, real-time systems or push notifications.
- Experience with health data or other regulated, privacy-sensitive domains (e.g. GDPR).
What We Offer
- Participation in our warrant program (stock options).
- A small team where your decisions directly shape the product.
- A Copenhagen-based office with close collaboration, no async-only culture.
- Work on software that healthcare workers depend on every day, the impact is tangible and immediate.
Join Our Team
We're looking for individuals who share our vision and value ownership and entrepreneurship over a conventional job.
At Teton, you'll have the chance to make a real impact with your work.
If you're ready for more than just a job, come aboard and be part of our mission to transform healthcare.

jobs.title: Tech Lead - New Customers Team
jobs.description:
Tech Lead - New Customers Team
Hybrid in London, UK
We’re looking for a Tech Lead
You'll lead the engineering behind how new businesses become iwoca customers – the application they fill in, the checks they go through, and the offer they get.
The company
Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.
That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.
We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.
The team
The New Customers team owns everything from a business's first application to a funded loan: the application flow, the logic that routes each application, the documents we ask customers for, and the models that set loan amounts and pricing. Its measure of success is the customer lifetime value it adds between sign-up and first loan.
The team sets its own goals and direction. It brings together engineers, data scientists, and product and strategy people. It partners closely with credit risk on the trade-offs behind every lending decision. Knowledge sharing is central to how the team works, supported by regular forums to share findings, and dedicated research and development time.
You'll lead two engineers and report to the head of engineering for iwoca's customer journey, from first application to repeat lending.
The role
As the Tech Lead, you'll spend most of your time building. The team is moving its offer logic out of a legacy monolith into a new service. It's the biggest change in a decade to the system behind iwoca's lending decisions. The next phase is yours to lead.
- Autonomy and ownership. You'll shape what the team builds, decide how to build it, and own what goes live. You'll set its engineering roadmap, including what to pull out of the monolith, what to rewrite, and in what order.
- Technical complexity. You'll design the team's part of the new service, which turns models and rules into a lending decision and optimises each offer across amount, duration, fee, and interest rate. You'll keep it reliable in production, easy to change as the models evolve, and able to show how it reached each decision.
- Experimentation and learning. You'll build the systems that let data scientists test new models on live applications. Some experiments run for years, until each loan reaches the end of its term. You'll see the long-term results of the team's lending decisions.
- Influence. You'll get colleagues across iwoca behind technical work that competes with new features for time.
- Leadership and growth. You'll line-manage and coach the team's engineers, setting context and helping them own projects end to end. As the team grows, you'll decide the skills and make-up it needs, and hire the engineers to match.
The requirements
Essential:
- Technical leadership. You've led a team of engineers for at least two years, including line management, while still remaining hands on.
- Backend engineering. You have deep expertise in at least one object-oriented language. You've designed, built, and run customer-facing backend systems in production.
- Commercial or product thinking. You take a business goal, get to the root of what's needed and why, and turn it into a technical plan. You can explain a trade-off in terms of what it means for customers and the business.
- AI leverage. You've built agentic workflows, or used AI to deliver engineering work you couldn't have done alone. You help your team do the same. You judge where it's useful. You check its output before it reaches production.
- Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience.
Bonus:
- Lending or payments experience. You've worked in lending, payments, or another domain where engineering decisions carry financial risk.
- Experimentation. You've built systems that run controlled experiments, especially long-running ones.
- Legacy migration. You've moved business-critical logic out of a complex legacy monolith and kept everything that depends on it working.
- Working with data scientists. You've worked with data scientists from prototype to production, and know their work well enough to challenge it.
- Python stack. You've worked with Python, Django, and PostgreSQL.
- Frontend. You've built frontend features as well as backend services.
The salary
We expect to pay from £100,000 to £130,000 for this role. But, we're open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.
The culture
At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.
We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.
The offices
We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:
- Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.
- Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.
The benefits
- Flexible working hours.
- Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.
- A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.
- 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.
- A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.
- Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.
- 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.
- An employee equity incentive scheme.
- Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.
- Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.
- Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.
And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:
- A learning and development budget for everyone.
- Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.
- Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

Senior Data Scientist - Credit Risk Modelling
Hybrid in London or remote in the UK
We're looking for a Senior Data Scientist to join our Credit Risk Modelling team.
You'll shape how iwoca models credit risk – setting the technical direction on multi-quarter projects, and lifting the bar for the team as you go.
The company
Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.
That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.
The team
The Credit Risk Modelling team owns credit risk and Customer Lifetime Value (CLtV) modelling for iwoca's UK and German lending. That covers the probabilistic machine learning models behind every credit decision, plus the CLtV models that shape pricing and portfolio strategy.
The team is around twelve data scientists. Some work on auto-space models that decide within five minutes from data candidates authorise us to pull. Others work on manual-space models that pick up when a credit analyst adds digital footprint and income data, which lands a decision within 24 hours.
The role
As a Senior Data Scientist in Credit Risk Modelling, you'll own credit risk and CLtV projects end to end – from spotting where the models hold the business back to getting the change live. The work ranges from keeping today's models accurate as conditions change, through incremental improvements, to research that could replace them.
You'll decide which problems to take on and how to solve them. With AI making prototyping cheap, more of the role now goes on research. You'll review other data scientists' modelling choices and coach newer members of the team.
Live examples of the work:
- Causal estimation of offer terms. Estimating the causal effect of amount, duration, and price on customer outcomes.
- Unifying automated and manual models. Finding a principled way to put the two model families, which optimise slightly different objectives, on a common cost function.
- IFRS accounting model. Developing a multi-stage model where recovery predictions feed back to improve the upfront loss estimates that International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) require.
- Generalising credit and CLtV. Exploring whether a single, more general model could replace the separate credit and CLtV models.
The requirements
Essential:
- Applied statistics. You have a background in statistics from a quantitative field – typically a degree or Master's in Statistics, Mathematics, Physics, or similar. You've applied it to commercial problems for several years, and chosen the methods yourself. You know when the data breaks a method's assumptions, and what that does to your answer.
- Probabilistic reasoning. You quantify the uncertainty in each estimate, and treat calibration as a first-order concern.
- Production ML. You've built supervised ML models end to end – exploration, training, deployment, and monitoring.
- Judgement. You critically evaluate model output – yours, a colleague's, or an LLM's – and can explain why a choice is right. You defend your reasoning under challenge, and challenge others' when the evidence points elsewhere.
- Project leadership. You've led modelling projects you spotted yourself, from framing the question to a decision the business acted on. Some of that work changed how a team models a problem.
- AI leverage. You've used AI to produce work you couldn't have delivered without it, and built tools or workflows your colleagues now use. You judge where it helps and where it doesn't.
- Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience.
Bonus:
- Domain experience. You've worked in credit risk, lending, or customer lifetime value modelling.
- Coaching. You've helped other data scientists improve their work, through review or mentoring.
- Non-linear methods. You can think in terms of the cost function and inductive biases of your models.
- Bayesian methods. You've used hierarchical models, MCMC, or Bayesian updating in real work.
- Time series modelling. You've modelled temporal data where autocorrelation, drift, or seasonality mattered.
- Coding. You can write code for analysis. The team works in Python.
The salary
We expect to pay from £90,000 – £130,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.
The culture
At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.
We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.
The offices

- Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

The benefits

Applied AI Engineer - Direct Acquisition
Hybrid in London, UK
We're looking for an Applied AI Engineer to join the Direct Acquisition team.
You'll design and build AI agents that run whole business processes, from planning the work to learning from the results. What you find will steer how far iwoca takes agents across the business.

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don't wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that's as flexible and responsive as they are.

- Delivery. You'll own each agent end to end: connect it to iwoca's predictive models, data pipelines and channel tools, and run it alongside the current process until it has shown it works.

- Agent engineering. You've built systems where LLMs take actions – more than chat or summaries – and you can explain what went wrong and how you fixed it. You know when a problem needs an agent and when it needs a for-loop.

- Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience.

- Languages and data tools. You've worked with Python, Go, Snowflake or dbt.
- Evaluation. You've built evals that measure how an agent performs and where it fails.
- Marketing and growth tech. You've worked with ad platforms, CRMs or direct mail.

Data Scientist - Credit Risk Modelling
Hybrid in London or remote in the UK
We’re looking for a Data Scientist to join our Credit Risk Modelling team.
You'll work on the credit models that sit at the core of iwoca's lending business – the models that decide who we lend to, on what terms, and how far the product can grow.
The company
Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.
That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.
We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.
The team
The Credit Risk Modelling team owns credit risk and customer lifetime value (CLtV) modelling for iwoca's UK and German lending. That covers the probabilistic machine learning models behind every credit decision, plus the CLtV models that shape pricing and portfolio strategy.
The team is around twelve data scientists, who combined create models to efficiently drive fully automated and human-in-the-loop decision making. This forms the core analytical team that interface with and support smaller analytic functions in other parts of the business.
The role
As a Data Scientist in Credit Risk Modelling, you'll use iwoca's lending data to answer credit risk and CLtV questions, and build what you find into the team's production models. The work ranges from keeping today's models accurate as conditions change, through incremental improvements, to research that could replace them.
You'll help choose the team's projects and put forward your own. With AI, prototyping is cheap enough for you to test ideas that once wouldn't have made the priority list. The R&D share of the role is growing as a result. You'll learn credit modelling in depth from several senior data scientists.
Live examples of the work:
- Causal estimation of offer terms. Estimating the causal effect of amount, duration, and price on customer outcomes.
- Unifying automated and manual models. Finding a principled way to put the two model families, which optimise slightly different objectives, on a common cost function.
- IFRS accounting model. Developing a multi-stage model where recovery predictions feed back to improve the upfront loss estimates that International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) require.
- Generalising credit and CLtV. Exploring whether a single, more general model could replace the separate credit and CLtV models.
The requirements
Essential:
- Applied statistics. You have a background in statistics from a quantitative field – typically a degree or Master's in Statistics, Mathematics, Physics, or similar. You've applied it to real-world data, in research or at work. You know when the data breaks a method's assumptions, and what that does to your answer.
- Probabilistic reasoning. You quantify the uncertainty in each estimate, and treat calibration as a first-order concern.
- Research mindset. You've tested new modelling ideas of your own, and judged which were worth taking further.
- Judgement. You critically evaluate model output – yours, a colleague's, or an LLM's – and can explain why a choice is right. You defend your reasoning under challenge, and challenge others' when the evidence points elsewhere.
- Analytical ownership. You've taken ambiguous problems from framing the question to a decision the business acted on. You give an early answer and update it as new evidence comes in.
- AI leverage. You've used AI to produce work you couldn't have delivered without it – a prototype, an automation, or a modelling pipeline others use. You judge where it helps and where it doesn't.
- Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience.
Bonus:
- Domain experience. You've worked in credit risk, lending, or customer lifetime value modelling.
- Production ML. You've built supervised ML models end to end – exploration, training, deployment, and monitoring.
- Non-linear methods. You can think in terms of the cost function and inductive biases of your models.
- Bayesian methods. You've used hierarchical models, MCMC, or Bayesian updating in real work.
- Time series modelling. You've modelled temporal data where autocorrelation, drift, or seasonality mattered.
- Coding. You can write code for analysis. The team works in Python
The salary
We expect to pay from £60,000 – £90,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.
We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We are seeking an experienced Trading Analytics Developer to join our Quant Trading team and play a pivotal role in advancing our data and AI infrastructure. - Design, build, and operate high throughput batch and streaming data pipelines using Kafka, Flink, and ETL technologies
- Design and build unified analytics engine designed for processing large-scale data using Apache Spark and related tools
- Develop and optimize analytical data models for time-series, financial metrics, and trading activity
- Implement and manage analytical databases (ClickHouse, MongoDB, BigQuery, Snowflake, or similar) with cost-aware architecture
- Build idempotent data pipelines with robust backfill and reconciliation capabilities
- Create comprehensive monitoring for data quality, freshness, and pipeline reliability
AI Platform Development

- Strong software engineering fundamentals: system design, data structures, algorithms, data integrity, accuracy and performance optimization
- Expertise in Linux, Github, and modern CI/CD practices
- Proven experience with AWS cloud services and Kubernetes orchestration
- Comfort working with large-scale, complex datasets in financial/trading contexts
Data Platform Expertise
- Advanced SQL with window functions and query optimization, realtime data synchronization together with database design and infrastructure support
- Experience with data workflow and messaging orchestration (Airflow, Jenkins, AMPS etc.)
- Metric design and implementation for trading analytics (PnL, risk, balance and trade reconciliation, backfill and performance tuning)
- Time-series data visualization with Grafana, TradingView, web-based interactive dashboards and BI tools etc.
- Kafka, Flink, and event processing in production environments
AI Platform Capabilities
- Retrieval system evaluation methodologies and quality frameworks
- RAG pipeline architecture and optimization techniques
- LLMOps practices including model lifecycle and prompt management
- Experience with AI agent frameworks in production settings like A2A and MCP
Preferred Qualifications
Financial/Trading Domain
- Experience in trading systems, quantitative finance, or financial technology
- Understanding of market data, data subscription using Rest API / Web Socket
- Knowledge of cryptocurrency markets, defi and related technologies
Professional Attributes
- Excellent problem-solving skills with ability to perform under pressure
- Strong communication skills for cross-team collaboration
- Proactive approach to system reliability and performance optimization
- Continuous learning mindset in rapidly evolving AI/ML landscape
- Balance of practical engineering rigor with innovative solution development

Growth from within. We help to develop new skill-sets that would impact the shaping of your personal and professional growth.

Today we’re a growing team of 700+ across Paris, London, New York, Toronto, San Francisco, and Austin, and we’ve been named a Visionary in the Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Financial Planning Software two years running.
At Pigment, we take smart risks, celebrate bold ideas, and challenge the status quo - all while working as one team. If you’re driven by innovation and ready to make an impact at scale, we’d love to hear from you.
You’ll join Pigment’s Reporting & Collaboration community, working as a senior hands-on Frontend Engineer on some of the most complex parts of the product.
This community is responsible for how users access, configure and interact with their data. That creates significant frontend challenges around large-scale datasets, filtering, visualisation, complex configuration and increasingly AI-powered experiences.
On the engineering part:
- Spend approximately 80% of your time as a hands-on engineer, designing, building and shipping production features.
- Work on complex, data-heavy frontend problems where performance, usability and scale all matter.
- Build sophisticated interfaces for displaying, filtering and interacting with large datasets.
- Work with React, TypeScript and JavaScript, while contributing to the wider technical decisions behind the product.
- Partner closely with Product Managers, Product Designers and Engineers to take features from problem definition through to production.
- Make pragmatic engineering decisions based on the needs of the product and its users, rather than pursuing technical complexity for its own sake.
- Contribute to areas across Reporting & Collaboration depending on business needs and your interests, including data extraction and filtering, visualisation, complex configuration and emerging AI experiences.
- Use modern engineering tooling, with Pigment teams working across GCP, CircleCI and AI development tools such as Claude Code, Cursor and GitHub Copilot.
This is not a traditional Engineering Manager role where you step away from the code. You will remain a senior individual contributor and be expected to ship.
On the people management part, here is what it entails:
At Pigment, people management and technical leadership are deliberately separated.
Tech Leads lead the technical direction of individual teams. Engineering Managers focus on developing engineers as people while remaining hands-on engineers themselves.
- Spend approximately 20% of your time on people management.
- Gradually take on direct reports after establishing yourself as an IC during your probation period.
- Coach engineers across different teams within the Reporting & Collaboration community.
- Support engineers with career progression, development, feedback and performance.
- Run regular 1:1s and help engineers understand what they need to do to progress.
- Set clear expectations and provide actionable feedback.
- Handle difficult performance conversations when necessary and follow through with clear development plans.
- Partner with Tech Leads to understand how your reports are performing technically without taking ownership of the Tech Lead's responsibilities.
- Help create an environment where strong engineers can continue to develop while doing their best work.
Engineering Managers typically support engineers across multiple teams within their community rather than "owning" a single engineering team.
Who you are
We’re looking for someone who is both a strong senior Frontend Engineer and an experienced people manager.
- Significant professional software-engineering experience, with the technical depth expected of a senior engineer.
- Strong recent hands-on frontend engineering experience.
- Production experience with React, TypeScript and/or JavaScript.
- Previous formal people-management experience. Ideally, you have already managed engineers rather than looking for your first management opportunity.
- Experience owning areas such as coaching, career development, feedback and performance management, not simply mentoring engineers or leading projects.
- Experience building complex product interfaces, ideally within B2B SaaS, enterprise software, analytics, data platforms or another sophisticated data-heavy product.
- Experience solving frontend problems involving areas such as large datasets, visualisation, filtering, configuration, performance or complex workflows.
- A strong product mindset. You care about what you're building, who is using it and whether it genuinely solves their problem.
- Strong collaboration skills across Engineering, Product and Design.
- The ability and desire to remain deeply hands-on in the code while managing people.
- The autonomy expected of a senior IC: once you understand the problem, you can work with the team to move it forward without needing constant direction.

jobs.title: Market Data Analyst - Dry Bulk
jobs.description:
At Kpler, we are dedicated to helping our clients navigate complex markets with ease. By simplifying global trade information and providing valuable insights, we empower organisations to make informed decisions in commodities, energy, and maritime sectors.
Since our founding in 2014, we have focused on delivering top-tier intelligence through user-friendly platforms. Our team of over 700 experts from 35+ countries works tirelessly to transform intricate data into actionable strategies, ensuring our clients stay ahead in a dynamic market landscape. Join us to leverage cutting-edge innovation for impactful results and experience unparalleled support on your journey to success.
Your future position:
Kpler’s Dry Bulk business is expanding, and we are looking for a Market Data Analyst – Dry Bulk to take ownership of data quality and operational processes across assigned geographical regions and product groups.
While the position is internally known as Market Data Analyst - Metals & Minerals, its scope extends across a broader range of dry bulk commodities, including ferrous and non-ferrous metals, solid fuels, and industrial minerals.
This is a role for someone who wants to sit close to how global commodity markets actually move. You will combine strong SQL and Python skills with a curiosity about the real-world events shaping those movements - from shifting trade flows and supply chain disruptions to changes in industrial demand, policy, and pricing dynamics.
You won’t just be processing data. You will play a key role in turning complex, high-volume datasets into reliable market intelligence used by clients to understand what is happening in global physical markets. Your work will directly influence how accurately we reflect real-world commodity flows.
Your mission is to:
-
Take charge of specific regions and product groups, ensuring the highest standard of data quality by reviewing internal constraints, validating automated outputs, and ingesting data from diverse external sources.
-
Identify and implement technology and process improvements – including contributions to SQL queries, Python scripts, and pipeline tooling – to increase the efficiency and accuracy of our seaborne flow data.
-
Track news, trade flows, and industry developments across metals and minerals markets. Extract meaningful patterns and ensure they are well reflected in our data product.
-
Lead responses to ad-hoc client requests (email, video call, in-person) with rapid, well-structured analysis. Partner with Sales and Customer Success teams to address client data needs and feed insights back into internal systems.
-
Engage proactively with the broader data architecture; understand how upstream data sources, internal systems, and client-facing solutions interact, and propose improvements that scale across the team.
-
Act as a knowledgeable and self-directed team member capable of picking up complex technical tasks independently and driving them to completion with minimal supervision.
You could be a match if you are or have:
- Experience working with data products and complex datasets. You understand how data is collected, processed, validated, and delivered to end users. You can investigate data inconsistencies, identify root causes, and contribute to improving data quality, reliability, and the overall user experience.
-
Strong proficiency in SQL and Python (PostgreSQL, MSSQL, or similar) is a core requirement. You use both to query databases, analyse data, and automate workflows, building and maintaining scripts to remove manual processes and improve efficiency. Strong Excel skills are required for analysis and commercial reporting.
- A genuine interest in physical commodity markets. You are curious about how global trade works in practice and how commodities move around the world. You want to understand the forces shaping supply and demand, trade flows, production, shipping, and pricing, as well as the economic, political, and industrial developments behind market movements. You actively seek to understand not only what is happening, but why it matters. We are looking for someone who can articulate what interests them about these markets and is motivated to deepen their knowledge over time.
-
Comfortable managing high-frequency datasets, identifying anomalies, and maintaining high standards of data quality under tight deadlines.
-
Strong communicator, able to translate complex technical outputs into clear, actionable insights for both technical and non-technical stakeholders, and build effective relationships across teams.
-
Proactive and self-directed: takes ownership, anticipates issues, and drives work independently to completion.
-
Experience supporting or mentoring junior colleagues, or a clear interest in developing others as the team grows would be highly adventagous.
Desirable:
-
Experience working with seaborne commodity data (e.g. AIS, port or vessel data).
-
Familiarity with data visualisation tools such as Tableau or similar.

jobs.title: Stage: Automatic construction of multi-flow hospital process models by large language models (LLM)
jobs.description:
Project led by: Marwa Trabelsi - IMT Mines Albi Industrial Engineering Centre (CGI)
IMT partners involved:
- Telecom Sud Paris, Electronics and Physics Department, Distributed Services Laboratory, Architectures,
Modeling, Validation, Network Administration (SAMOVAR): Nel Samama - Mines Saint-Etienne : Centre Ingénierie Santé (CIS), Marius Huguet
Proposed subject (5-6 months from February):
Acronym : HOPAL : Hospital Process Automatic Learning
Long title: Automatic construction of multi-flux hospital process models by large language models (LLM)
Project Description:
The study of the emergency management process is essential to understand and resolve the growing problem of overload, which affects many countries. This overload, often linked to an imbalance between demand for care and available resources, has serious consequences: delays in treatment, longer sorting times, and even an increase in mortality. It also reveals systemic challenges, such as difficult access to primary care, which push patients into emergencies.
Optimizing the use of human and material resources not only reduces queues, but also improves the quality of care and overall efficiency of the system. Finally, analysing these processes helps to identify durable solutions, such as better organization or targeted reallocation of resources.
These processes leave digital traces in the hospital information system (HIS), but their modelling remains largely manual, costly and rapidly obsolete.
The mining process allows you to discover process models from these tracks. Traditional discovery techniques, however, reach their limits in the face of heterogeneous, noisy and multiflux logs.
Large language models (LLMs) open up a new path: automatically generate process models (BPMNs, process graphs) directly from organizational tracks, without human intervention, and produce a readable reading by field actors.
In addition, work at CGI has demonstrated the feasibility of LLM predicting patient pathways. The scientific question at the heart of this internship is the articulation of these two bricks: how to link the prediction of journeys with the automatic construction of models, to move from retrospective models (what happened) to forward-looking models (what will happen)?
This project is part of an IMT inter-school dynamic around the explainable AI for public health. The CGI, CIS and SAMOVAR teams are already collaborating through the TRACKING project (Carnot M.I.N.E.S. – CARINGS), with work on indoor geolocation within the emergencies at Le Corbusier Hospital in Firminy. This synergy was extended by an M2 internship in 2025, funded by the Health Seed Fund, dedicated to prototyping a mobile indoor/outdoor patient localization application. An INTERCARNOT thesis was launched in continuity with the validation of the two Carnot institutes (M.I.N.E.S. and TSN) and will start in October 2026.
Purpose of the course
The objective is to design and prototype a pipeline in which the same LLM automatic model construction module is powered by two sources:
- Branch A (retrospective): Actual SIH logs, standardized in event logs, produce as-is models of observed processes;
- Branch B (prospective): In the continuation of the work carried out, the routes predicted by LLM are serialized to the same trace format (activity, timing, resource) via an adapter, and produce to-be models of future processes.
Comparison of the as-is and to-be models allows the detection of deviations, the anticipation of bottlenecks and the support for the explainable decision, until the counterfactual simulation (disturb predictions, reconstruct the model, observe impact).
Profile sought
- Training: M2 or last year of engineering school in computer science, data science, AI or industrial engineering;
- Technical skills: Python essential; an LLM experience (fine-tuning, prompting, API)
- and/or process mining (pm4py) is a strong asset;
- Qualities: scientific rigor, autonomy, taste for work with imperfect real data, interest in the hospital domain.
