jobs.title: Senior Data Platform Engineer, Knowledge Platform & AI Enablement
jobs.description:
About Airwallex
Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.
We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.
We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles to see it in full.
About the team
The Data Platform Engineering team is going to implement various data processing tasks on the newly built next-generation data platform. We aim to further optimize data storage, processing, application, interfaces, and other dimensions. Throughout the continuous iteration process, we will also incorporate new data components and consider new data architectures (such as Lake House) to achieve faster data scheduling, significantly reducing data latency and enabling more efficient operation of data engineering applications.
How you'll make impact
You’ll help build the next generation of Airwallex’s data and knowledge infrastructure, turning structured and unstructured information into trusted context for people and AI systems.
- Own the design, development, and operation of large-scale distributed data systems across batch and streaming workloads, improving data latency, reliability, and engineering productivity.
- Drive foundational technical decisions across data processing, service-layer infrastructure, application-layer systems, third-party data integrations, and performance optimisation.
- Build and automate high-performance distributed data processing systems that support Airwallex’s data and AI capabilities.
- Lead medium- and large-scale engineering projects from system design through delivery, creating impact across the team and wider organisation.
- Raise engineering standards through scalable data architecture, shared tooling, high-quality software practices, and technical guidance for other engineers.
You'll work from our Singapore office five days a week.
What we're looking for
Essentials
- 5+ years of relevant experience as a data engineer.
- A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Systems, or equivalent experience.
- Strong programming skills in one or more of Kotlin, Java, Scala, Python, and SQL.
- Experience designing, building, and operating distributed systems, including establishing overarching data architecture.
- Strong working knowledge of real-time and batch data processing systems.
- Experience working with data at petabyte scale.
- Experience making technical decisions across data processing, service-layer infrastructure, application-layer systems, third-party data integrations, and performance optimisation.
- Experience developing and automating large-scale, high-performance distributed data processing systems.
- A track record of driving medium- and large-scale engineering projects from design through delivery.
- A commitment to high-quality software engineering practices and scalable data infrastructure.
- Experience mentoring or providing technical guidance to other engineers.
Preferred
- Experience with Kafka, data lakes, Spark, Flink, dbt, Spring Boot, Hadoop, BigQuery, or Snowflake.
- Experience contributing to shared data engineering standards, tools, or platforms that improve engineering productivity and output quality.
- Experience with next-generation data architectures such as lakehouse systems.
- Experience working in a high-growth or scaling environment.
You'll thrive here if
- You're comfortable owning the roadmap yourself.
- You own the outcome and you don't wait for permission to fix what's broken.
- You're comfortable with ambiguity. Give you a problem, not a prescription, and you'll run with it.
- You hold yourself to a high standard even when no one is watching. Quality and accountability aren't external expectations, they're internal ones.
- You value in-person collaboration and are happy being in the office five days a week.
- You enjoy working closely with people across multiple countries and time zones as part of one connected, global team, including flexing your hours occasionally to make that connection work.
Learn more about your team
The Knowledge Platform sits at the foundation of Airwallex’s Data and AI strategy. We are evolving traditional data infrastructure into knowledge infrastructure—turning structured and unstructured information into trusted, reusable context that helps people and AI systems make better decisions and take action.
You’ll build the platform end to end, from core technologies such as Databricks, Clickhouse, Spark, and Kafka to real-time analytics, knowledge retrieval and indexing, model infrastructure, agent capabilities, and AI interaction history. You’ll also develop the evaluation, annotation, feedback, governance, permission, and freshness frameworks required to operate AI reliably at global financial scale.
Our mission is making this ecosystem truly agent-ready. That means enabling teams to explore data through natural language, investigate business drivers in real time, and give AI systems secure access to the context and capabilities they need to support decisions and execute workflows.
If you want to build the foundation that turns Airwallex’s data into knowledge, knowledge into intelligence, and intelligence into measurable business impact, this is where that work happens.
Applicant Safety Policy: Fraud and Third-Party Recruiters
To protect you from recruitment scams, please be aware that Airwallex will not ask for bank details, sensitive ID numbers (i.e. passport), or any form of payment during the application or interview process. All official communication will come from an @airwallex.com email address. Please apply only through careers.airwallex.com or our official LinkedIn page.

We don’t regard color, religion, race, national origin, sexual orientation, ancestry, citizenship, sex, marital or family status, disability, gender, or any other legally protected status when making our hiring decisions. How you'll make impact
As a Staff AI Engineer, you’ll define the technical direction for next-generation AI solutions that improve internal efficiency and transform how customers interact with Airwallex. You’ll design and implement robust APIs and system architectures for AI applications, including agentic experiences, language-model-powered workflows, search and data analysis systems. You’ll shape AI application roadmaps, research and apply emerging technologies, and partner with diverse cross-functional teams to turn product goals into reliable systems. You’ll also help resolve application issues and software bugs with prompt, effective solutions while maintaining a high bar for customer experience.
You’ll work from our Singapore office five days a week.
What we're looking for
Essentials
- 10+ years of experience in backend software development, with a passion for AI and language technologies.
- A proven track record of delivering major impact.
- Proficiency in Python, TypeScript or JavaScript.
- Experience designing and developing large-scale distributed systems with high concurrency, high load and high availability.
- Experience working with vector databases.
- A relevant degree in Computer Science, Mathematics or a related field.
Preferred

You'll thrive here if
- You're excited by a category that hasn't been won yet, and want to be early enough to shape it.
- You're comfortable with ambiguity. Give you a problem, not a prescription, and you'll run with it.
- You own the outcome and you don't wait for permission to fix what's broken.
- You say what you mean. You're direct, but you lead with respect.
- You simplify complexity rather than hiding behind it.
Learn more about your team
AI at Airwallex is building the path from financial software to autonomous finance. At the center of this vision is Kai, Airwallex’s AI assistant and the intelligent interface to our global financial platform. Kai connects AI with capabilities across payments, accounts, transfers, cards, expenses, and other financial workflows—enabling customers to describe what they want to achieve while the system handles more of the complexity underneath.
You’ll build intelligent financial products and autonomous agents that understand business context, plan and reason across multi-step workflows, execute actions within clearly defined controls, and learn from outcomes. The work spans agent architecture, orchestration, context and knowledge systems, ontology, evaluation, governance, monitoring, and reliability.
The challenge is uniquely demanding: AI systems are probabilistic, while moving money requires precision, permissions, auditability, deterministic controls, and regulatory compliance. You’ll help define where AI should reason and where financial infrastructure must remain deterministic—turning frontier models into safe, controllable systems that businesses can trust.
Join exceptional engineers advancing Kai from assistance to action and, ultimately, toward autonomous finance—where customers define the outcome they want and intelligent systems securely execute more of the work required to achieve it.

The work is moving up the stack: from analysis to system, from model to harness, and from answering a question once to building something that answers it correctly over time. This isn’t a traditional reporting role. You’ll own the analytical layer of Airwallex’s regulatory data infrastructure, defining what “correct” means and building systems that prove it. You’ll work at the intersection of data engineering, compliance logic and product intelligence to help transform how Airwallex manages regulatory reporting and risk oversight.
- Lead the analytical and data design for priority regulatory reports, translating requirements into data logic, testing and go-live processes.
- Partner with Regulatory Compliance, Financial Crime Compliance, Finance, Data Operations and Data Engineering to standardise common dimensions such as accounts, FX, products and entities across reports.
- Co-design data models and mart-layer logic with Data Engineering, shaping how reporting dimensions are structured, tested and versioned upstream.
- Define automated test suites and manual quality-assurance playbooks that reports must pass before submission to regulators.
- Investigate anomalies, requests for information and audit findings by quantifying impact, identifying root causes across products and entities, and proposing remediation options.
- Shape requirements for a scalable regulatory reporting and risk analytics platform.
- Raise the standard of analytical rigour, documentation and validation across risk and compliance topics, while mentoring analysts and data scientists in adjacent teams.
This is an in-office role — you’ll be in our Singapore office five days a week.
What we’re looking for
Essentials
- A bachelor’s degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Operations Research, Finance, Economics or a related quantitative discipline.
- 5+ years of hands-on experience extracting and manipulating large datasets with SQL, plus scripting experience in Python, Shell or R.
- 5+ years of proven risk management experience or equivalent, including analytics, model implementation and stakeholder management.
- Experience with analytics engineering practices, including writing modular, tested and documented SQL transformations using dbt or an equivalent tool, and thinking in layers across sources, staging and marts.
- Experience building exploratory and production-grade analytics with modern data tools, such as Hex, Evidence or notebook-style environments where SQL, Python and visualisation work together.
- Excellent communication and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to explain technical data topics to non-technical audiences, document assumptions clearly and influence partners across Legal, Risk, Compliance, Finance and Engineering.
Preferred
- Direct experience working on regulatory reporting in risk and compliance domains.
- Hands-on experience with dbt, including models, tests, documentation and macros, and a modern data warehouse such as BigQuery, Databricks or Snowflake.
- Experience owning a data model end to end rather than only querying existing tables.
- Understanding of data pipeline design, including when a problem belongs in the transformation, application or reporting layer, and the ability to discuss these trade-offs with Data Engineering peers.
- Exposure to model risk or AI/ML governance, such as model inventories, validation and monitoring, and an interest in how these frameworks intersect with regulatory reporting and compliance analytics.
- Experience working with cross-functional, geographically distributed teams and managing by influence.

- Drive architectural improvements across distributed, high-concurrency systems by experimenting with new technologies and applying sound engineering judgment.
- Improve the reliability and scalability of payment products, transaction systems and risk-management capabilities.
- Build services that support the detection and mitigation of evolving fraud risks across Airwallex’s products.
- Partner with senior engineers to raise software engineering practices and coding standards.
- Mentor less-experienced engineers and help strengthen the team’s technical capability.
You'll be in our Singapore office five days a week.

Essentials

- More than three years of experience developing risk or payment platforms.

- Strong proficiency in Java, including Java multithreading, high concurrency, I/O, NIO and network communication.
- Experience with common design patterns and the design and development of large-scale, distributed, high-concurrency, high-load and highly available systems.

- Familiarity with Spring, Spring Boot and RESTful services.
- Experience with Gradle, Maven or other build tools.
- Familiarity with JSON and XML.
Preferred
- In-depth knowledge of risk-management strategies and fraud-detection techniques, particularly in financial services or fintech.
- Familiarity with graph databases and their use in pattern and anomaly detection.
- Experience with machine-learning models and frameworks for predictive risk analytics.
- Familiarity with real-time data-streaming technologies such as Apache Kafka or Flink.
- Strong data-analytics skills, with experience using ClickHouse, Spark or NoSQL databases for large-scale data processing and risk analysis.

Risk Platform builds the decisioning infrastructure that sits between Airwallex and every dollar that moves through it, protecting 150,000+ businesses moving over US$260 billion a year across 150+ countries and 60+ currencies, and deciding, often in milliseconds, whether a new signup is real, a payment is safe, or a login is who they claim to be. You’ll shape the architecture, shared libraries, and tooling that help product squads ship faster, more reliably, and with a consistent user experience.
- Define and evolve the shared mobile architecture across navigation, state management, networking, offline strategies, error handling, modularisation, and boundaries between platform foundations and product features.
- Own critical mobile platform capabilities, including design system components, analytics, feature flags, experimentation, authentication, payments, and observability, making them stable, well-documented, and easy for product teams to adopt.
- Improve mobile application security, reliability, performance, and observability through anti-tampering measures, certificate pinning, security best practices, crash reporting, logging, metrics, and tracing.
- Define and track platform-level measures such as crash-free sessions, ANRs, app start-up time, bundle size, and network performance, using data to guide priorities with product teams.
- Own and continuously improve mobile CI/CD pipelines and release workflows across iOS and Android, reducing build times, test flakiness, and friction in shipping new versions.
- Drive cross-squad technical initiatives from problem definition through rollout and adoption, aligning engineering, product, design, and platform stakeholders around technical direction and trade-offs.
- Raise the bar for mobile engineering through hands-on technical leadership, design reviews, mentoring, documentation, automation, best practices, hiring, and community building.

Essentials
- 8–10+ years of experience building native mobile applications on iOS or Android, including at least 3+ years operating at a Senior or Staff level.
- Deep expertise in one native mobile platform: Swift, SwiftUI, Combine, and async/await on iOS, or Kotlin, AndroidX, Jetpack, Coroutines, and Hilt on Android, with commercial knowledge of both platforms.
- A proven track record of leading cross-team technical initiatives and evolving mobile architectures, such as modularisation, design systems, networking, or offline support.
- Strong focus on code quality and reliability, including designing for testability and maintainability and writing high-quality automated tests.
- Experience owning and improving mobile CI/CD pipelines, including build optimisation, test stability, and release workflows using tools such as GitHub Actions or Bitrise.
- Experience driving mobile application security, performance, reliability, observability, or release engineering.
- Demonstrated ability to influence without authority, align engineers, product managers, and designers around technical direction, and make pragmatic trade-offs.
- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Preferred
- Experience defining and driving a mobile platform roadmap while balancing foundational work with product delivery needs.
- Prior ownership of shared mobile libraries or frameworks used by multiple product teams at scale.
- Hands-on experience with mobile design systems and component libraries.
- Experience with mobile analytics, experimentation, and feature flagging.
- Experience with observability tooling such as Crashlytics, Sentry, or logging and metrics platforms.
- Experience in payments, fintech, or B2B SaaS, especially in environments where reliability, security, and regulatory requirements are critical.
- Experience mentoring senior engineers and contributing to hiring and growing mobile engineering teams.
- Contributions to the mobile community through open source, talks, blog posts, or thought leadership in mobile architecture and foundations.

You'll combine hands-on analytical leadership with strategic influence, helping evolve data science into a more scalable, general capability across the business.

- Act as a strategic thought partner to cross-functional teams, using data and technical expertise to inform, influence, and execute strategy and investment decisions.
- Apply quantitative analysis, data mining, forecasting, and clear data storytelling to answer important business questions and guide strategic decisions.
- Define goals, build forecasts, and monitor key business metrics to identify trends and assess performance across the organisation.
- Help evolve data science from individual analyses into scalable systems of decision support, establishing robust analytical approaches that produce reliable insights repeatedly.
You'll work from our London office three days a week.
What we're looking for
Essentials
- 8+ years of industry experience.
- An advanced degree, such as a PhD or MS, in a quantitative field such as Statistics, Engineering, Sciences, Computer Science, or Economics.
- Experience communicating analytical results to leadership and cross-functional teams to influence strategy.
- Experience providing technical mentorship in data science or quantitative analysis in an industry setting.
- Expert-level ability in data-querying languages such as SQL, scripting languages such as Python, and/or statistical or mathematical software such as R.
You'll thrive here if
- You're comfortable owning the roadmap yourself.
- You own the outcome and you don't wait for permission to fix what's broken.
- You're comfortable with ambiguity. Give you a problem, not a prescription, and you'll run with it.
- You connect dots across functions and hold the big picture without losing grip on the details.
- You simplify complexity rather than hiding behind it.
Learn more about your team
Data Science at Airwallex is evolving from individual analyses and standalone models into scalable systems of decision and action. We bring together two complementary capabilities: DS Analytics, which improves decision quality and reduces decision latency, and DS Algorithm, which directly optimizes product and business outcomes in real time.
You’ll build systems of decision that help teams understand what changed, determine what to do next, and learn whether the action worked. This means owning the AI analytics harness around the analysis—including semantic layers, context retrieval, evaluation infrastructure, validation gates, and governance—so decisions remain reliable, contextualized, and trustworthy at scale.
You’ll also build systems of action that use machine learning and AI to shape product behavior, ranking, pricing, risk, allocation, and customer experiences. The work extends beyond training models to designing how intelligent systems reason, use tools, operate within guardrails, execute workflows, and measure their incremental impact.
As AI makes ad hoc analysis increasingly accessible, the remaining advantage is scale, scientific method, and rigor. You’ll structure ambiguous problems, design experiments, identify confounding factors, challenge misleading conclusions, and build production systems that produce reliable outcomes repeatedly—not just one-off answers.
The work is moving up the stack: from analysis to system, from model to harness, and from answering a question once to building something that answers it correctly over time. If you want to create data science systems that compound decision quality and turn intelligence into measurable action, this is where that work happens.

jobs.title: AI Engineer
jobs.description:
About Thunes
Thunes is the Smart Superhighway to move money around the world. Thunes’ proprietary Direct Global Network allows Members to make payments in real-time in over 140 countries and more than 90 currencies. Thunes’ Network connects directly to over 12 billion mobile wallets, stablecoin wallets and bank accounts worldwide, as well as 15 billion cards via more than 220 different payment methods, such as GCash, M-Pesa, Airtel, MTN, Orange, JazzCash, Easypaisa, AliPay, WeChat Pay and many more.
Thunes’ Direct Global Network differentiates itself through its worldwide reach, in-house SmartX Treasury System and Fortress Compliance Platform, ensuring Members of the Network receive unrivaled speed, control, visibility, protection, and cost efficiencies when making real-time payments, globally. Members of Thunes’ Direct Global Network include gig economy giants like Uber and Deliveroo, super-apps like Grab and WeChat, MTOs, fintechs, PSPs and banks.
Headquartered in Singapore, Thunes has offices in 14 locations, including Barcelona, Beijing, Dubai, Hong Kong, Johannesburg, London, Manila, Nairobi, New York, Paris, Riyadh, San Francisco and Shanghai. For more information, visit: https://www.thunes.com/
Context of the role
We are looking for a highly driven, self-motivated, and technically excellent engineer who is truly excited about building the "AI Operating System" of a high-growth Fintech.
You will need to combine a startup mindset with the rigor of a regulated financial institution, moving beyond simple chatbots to build "Stateful" Agentic Systems and Multimodal RAG pipelines that can reason across text, charts, and financial tables. This role is responsible for developing our core generative capabilities and getting them to production in the most efficient, secure, and observable way possible. We architect solutions that bridge our AI tech stack with our enterprise data lake on AWS. We rely on our AI Engineers to possess "Deployment Autonomy", meaning you architect, implement, test, and deploy your own solutions.
Key Responsibilities
- Architect production-grade RAG workflows on cloud resources (e.g. AWS, GCP) using reliable tools (e.g. LangGraph / LlamaIndex). Build agents that can plan multi-step financial tasks
- Implement multimodal reasoning pipelines that ingest and reason over mixed-media financial documents (e.g. Charts, Graphs, Tables)
- Act as the internal adversary (Red Teaming). Design cases to stress-test models against Prompt Injection, Jailbreaking and PII Leakage before they touch sensitive data
- Define and implement the "Definition of Done" for AI using quantitative evaluation. Use evaluation tools (e.g. DeepEval) to score models on Faithfulness and Relevancy. Use these metrics to validate model upgrades and cost-optimisation experiments
- Champion Deployment Autonomy: Containerise your solutions (e.g. Docker), define the infrastructure and deploy to our cloud resources via GitLab CI
- Ensure governance by implementing deterministic guardrails (e.g. NeMo Guardrails, Guardrails AI) to enforce JSON output schemas and block non-compliant financial advice
Professional Experience and Qualifications
- 5+ years of total AI engineering experience, with 2+ years of hands-on experience building and deploying NLP or GenAI solutions in production
- Multi-Cloud Fluency: Expertise in architecting solutions on major cloud platforms (e.g. AWS, GCP). Mastery of cloud native LLM ecosystems (e.g. Bedrock, Vertex AI). Strong operational grasp of cloud services (e.g. IAM, Storage)
- Mastery of GenAI Orchestration: Expert level skills in LangChain or LangGraph (specifically for stateful, multi-turn agents) or LlamaIndex and other equivalent tools/libraries
- Experience in Evaluation & Monitoring: Proficiency with open source tools for testing (e.g. DeepEval). Experience implementing full tracing and observability tools (e.g. LangSmith, Langfuse, Arize Phoenix)
- Passionate about MLOps: Ability to write GitLab CI pipelines (automated testing, linting, scanning) and strong Docker skills (multi-stage builds)
- Holding a Bachelor’s degree in a STEM field (Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Physics)
- Python Expertise: Proficiency with data validation (e.g. Pydantic) and asynchronous REST APIs (e.g. FastAPI)
- Retrieval Engineering: Hands-on experience managing vector databases (e.g. Vertex AI Vector Search, Weaviate, Milvus or pgvector). Understanding of indexing and chunking strategies for hybrid search (Dense + Sparse)
- Experience in Security & Red Teaming: Knowledge of adversarial testing frameworks (e.g. Giskard, PyRIT) to scan for LLM vulnerabilities
- Interest in the Fintech Industry: Prior experience in Payments, Banking or Finance Services is strongly preferred
- Certifications: Google Professional Machine Learning Engineer / AWS Certified Machine Learning - Specialty is highly preferred
Sound like you? Apply now!

Context of the role
Thunes Financial Services is hiring a Security Engineer to be the architect of trust for our fintech platform. We are looking for a hybrid specialist who can bridge the gap between Infrastructure Security and Application Security, ensuring our systems are as resilient as they are compliant. This role will play a critical part in maintaining our regulatory compliance posture while building automated, scalable security guardrails. This role reports to the VP of Engineering.
As a Security Engineer, you will be responsible for security across the full lifecycle of our fintech platform. This hybrid specialist role requires deep engagement with both infrastructure and application security, focusing heavily on automation and regulatory compliance within a high-stakes, regulated environment.
Day-to-day:
- CI/CD Security Integration: Design, build, and maintain automation to integrate security testing (SAST/DAST/SCA) directly into our deployment pipelines. You'll ensure that security is a "paved road" for developers, not a bottleneck.
- Full-Stack Security: Own security across the lifecycle—from securing our cloud infrastructure (AWS/GCP) to performing code reviews and architectural risk assessments.
- Vulnerability Management: Manage our detection stack using modern vulnerability scanning and dependency management tools to identify, prioritize, and track risks across the environment.
- Security Automation: Build and maintain automated workflows for vulnerability reporting, triage, and remediation. We want someone who leverages AI-powered agentic coding tools or similar automation to eliminate manual toil and accelerate response times.
- Compliance Engineering: Monitor our technical security controls to ensure that they are operating effectively throughout the year to meet the rigorous cybersecurity compliance requirements to support regulatory exams as well as SOC-2 and PCI audits.
- Incident Response: Serve as a key member of our security response team, helping to investigate and mitigate potential threats.
Collaborate with:
- Product, data engineering, front-end engineering, tech ops, compliance, and legal
Tech stack:
Cloud (AWS/GCP, K8s), CI/CD tools (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or Jenkins), Python, Go, or Bash, SAST/DAST/SCA, enterprise vulnerability management platforms, automated dependency scanning solutions.
Success in this role means:
- Ensuring systems are resilient and compliant.
- Maintaining our regulatory compliance posture.
- Building automated, scalable security guardrails.
- Having a direct impact on the security strategy.
Travel:
- Some travel required for periodic team offsites.
Knowledge Required
Qualifications
A Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field, but similar professional experience is equally valued.
Experience
A proven track record of deep experience in both Infrastructure Security and Application Security is required.
Technical skills:
- Pipeline Proficiency: Hands-on experience building security guardrails within CI/CD tools (e.g., GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or Jenkins).
- Hybrid Expertise: Deep experience in both Infrastructure Security (Cloud/K8s) and AppSec (OWASP Top 10, Secure SDLC).
- Tooling Experience: Proven proficiency with enterprise vulnerability management platforms and automated dependency scanning solutions.
- Automation Mindset: You don’t just find bugs; you write code (Python, Go, or Bash) to handle them. Experience using AI-driven automation or agentic tools to streamline security workflows is required.
- Fintech Fluency: You understand the high-stakes nature of working in a regulated environment and can translate compliance requirements into technical reality.
Leadership and collaboration:
- Clear, effective communication of trade-offs to non-technical stakeholders
- History of collaboration with engineers and others
Nice to have but in no way required:
- Certifications such as CISSP
- Prior experience in startups, especially Fintech

Headquartered in Singapore, Thunes has offices in 14 locations, including Barcelona, Beijing, Dubai, Hong Kong, Johannesburg, London, Manila, Nairobi, New York, Paris, Riyadh, San Francisco and Shanghai. For more information, visit: https://www.thunes.com/
Context of the role
We are seeking a highly skilled Data Engineer to drive the development and optimization of our data platform. This position is designed for a technical expert who excels at the intersection of data engineering, infrastructure automation, and business logic. The successful candidate will be responsible for building robust data lifecycles, ensuring the scalability of our cloud-native environment, and maintaining the integrity of our streaming and batch processing systems.
1. Job Responsibilities
- Data Platform Engineering: Design, implement, and scale end-to-end data pipelines using Python and SQL-based transformations within a cloud-native data lake environment.
- Infrastructure Orchestration: Manage and scale containerized data workloads and automated workflow orchestration (using tools like Apache Airflow) and Infrastructure as Code (using Terraform) or similar functional equivalents.
- Streaming & Real-time Integration: Maintain and evolve real-time data replication services and stream processing architectures (utilizing Apache Kafka or similar distributed messaging systems) to ensure low-latency data availability.
- Data Quality & Governance: Establish and implement Data Governance frameworks and automated validation protocols to ensure the highest standards of data accuracy, compliance, and platform reliability.
- Business Logic & Data Modeling: Partner with cross-functional stakeholders to interpret complex business requirements and translate them into performant data models for reporting and business intelligence.
- Systems Architecture: Provide technical insights into the continuous improvement of the data platform, ensuring the stack remains resilient and performant as data volumes and complexity increase.
2. Candidate Requirements
- Professional Experience: A proven track record in a Data Engineering capacity, with extensive experience managing and scaling modern, distributed data platforms.
- Cloud Platform Expertise: Deep experience managing cloud-native data ecosystems, with a strong preference for candidates familiar with AWS or GCP environments.
- Workflow & Infrastructure Tools: Proficiency in workflow orchestration and Infrastructure as Code (IaC); specific experience with Apache Airflow and Terraform is highly preferred, though experience with similar tools (e.g., Prefect, Dagster, Pulumi) will be considered.
- Streaming Systems Depth: Demonstrated experience in configuring, maintaining, and troubleshooting distributed messaging and real-time data replication systems such as Apache Kafka or equivalent technologies (e.g., Amazon Kinesis, Google Pub/Sub).
- Data Governance & Quality: Solid understanding of Data Governance principles, including data lineage, metadata management, and automated quality checks.
- Advanced Engineering Skills: Exceptional Python programming capabilities and advanced SQL proficiency, with a focus on writing clean, modular, and highly testable code.
- Business Sense: Strong analytical aptitude with the ability to interface directly with business units, understand underlying data logic, and architect schemas that support complex organizational reporting and data product needs.

What you’d be doing in this role
As Canva scales, change continues to be part of our DNA. But we like to think that's all part of the fun. So this will give you the flavour of the type of things you'll be working on when you start, but this will likely evolve.
At the moment, this role is focused on:
- Partnering with our staff engineer to investigate and resolve complex Chromium issues — including upgrade breakages, rendering race conditions, and incidents caused by upstream changes
- Owning the PDF accessibility post-processing pipeline and implementing features that add proper tagging and compliance (PDF/UA, WCAG) to exported PDFs for Enterprise customers
- Building monitoring and testing infrastructure that catches Chromium changes before they reach production
- Designing accessibility solutions resilient to Chromium's frequent output structure changes, so we're not constantly rebuilding

- Documenting complex Chromium behaviour and architectural decisions to build team knowledge and reduce bus factor

- You're comfortable with C++ when you need to dig into complex third-party codebases

- You've debugged layered systems where the problem spans multiple codebases and languages
- PDF specification knowledge or experience with PDF generation and post-processing
- A background in rendering pipelines, graphics programming, or print production systems
- Experience maintaining systems where upstream dependencies change frequently

The Export team sits within the Editing Platform group and owns one of Canva's most critical workflows — transforming designs into downloadable files that users can share, print, and bring to life. - Demonstrated ability to work across multiple codebases and technology stacks simultaneously
- Hands-on experience using AI/LLM tools in your engineering workflow—you're fluent with AI-assisted development but not dependent on it; you can reason through problems and debug without AI as a crutch
- Strong written and verbal communication skills; you can translate technical decisions for non-technical stakeholders and navigate cross-functional collaboration naturally
- Comfort with ambiguity—you can take a loosely-defined business problem, scope the engineering work, and ship iteratively without waiting for a perfect spec
Preferred Qualifications
- Experience designing systems that non-engineers can build on top of or extend themselves (e.g., platforms, low-code frameworks, template systems)
- Experience in a Solutions Engineering, Sales Engineering, or GTM Engineering role—or a product engineering role where you worked closely with customers or go-to-market teams
- Familiarity with Stripe's products, APIs, or the payments/fintech domain
- Experience integrating with third-party platforms (Salesforce, Gong, etc.)
- Track record of building tools or systems that were adopted beyond your immediate team
- Background in consulting, professional services, or other roles that blend technical depth with business context
Who You Are
Beyond the technical requirements, we're looking for a specific kind of engineer:
- You want to be close to the business. You're energized by seeing your work directly impact how a sales team wins a deal or how a customer succeeds.
- You're a pragmatic builder. You ship working solutions quickly, iterate based on real usage, and know when "good enough now" beats "perfect later." You'd rather show a working prototype today than present a roadmap deck next quarter.
- You're a software engineer by practice. You can architect systems, debug production issues, write clean code, and reason about tradeoffs. AI is a tool in your belt, not a substitute for engineering judgment.
- You're a pattern recognizer. When you build something that works for one person, you immediately see how it generalizes. You think in reusable systems, not one-off scripts.
- You thrive without a traditional product team structure. No PRDs landing in your lap, no dedicated PM, no sprint ceremonies. You identify the highest-leverage problem, scope the work, and ship it. You're comfortable trading on-call rotations and rigid processes for autonomy and impact.
- You're a strong communicator. You can partner with SAs who are domain experts, understand their workflows deeply enough to build great tools, and explain your technical choices to leadership.

Radar helps businesses prevent payments fraud and abuse while enabling legitimate customers to transact with confidence. We combine machine learning and AI with the intelligence of Stripe’s global network to make sophisticated fraud prevention accessible to businesses of all sizes.
Our work spans payments fraud detection, protection against abuse beyond the payment, enterprise APIs that bring Radar’s capabilities into businesses’ own systems and payment flows, and the platform that powers it all. We build everything from reliable, low-latency infrastructure to intuitive tools that help users understand threats and control how they respond.

As a software engineer on Radar, you’ll build products and infrastructure that help businesses understand and stop fraud and abuse. Your work will span backend services, enterprise APIs, and user experiences that put sophisticated prevention capabilities into our customers’ hands.

- An ownership mindset and comfort navigating ambiguity, taking initiative, and following through on user problems

jobs.title: Data Analyst, Intern
jobs.description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a technology company focused on improving the conditions for economic growth and prosperity. We build programmable financial infrastructure, rethinking from first principles how financial services should work, to make it easier and cheaper for any business to start and scale. More than 10 million businesses build on Stripe, spanning the economic frontier—from solo founders to established enterprises—united by a practical focus on growth. The most ambitious companies in the world use Stripe as core infrastructure to grow faster. They process trillions of dollars a year on Stripe, equivalent to around 1.6% of global GDP. While economic growth makes everyone better off, open markets also enable greater variety. When any business can easily serve a global customer base, the quality and diversity of products in the world increase, and craft and creativity are unleashed into the smallest niches. Our own growth is wholly contingent on the success of the businesses building on Stripe. We therefore invest back into our technology at an unusual rate. We make upgrades to our products every single day to deliver compounding gains to our customers. We maintain some of the most reliable APIs on the internet. We build entirely new pieces of financial infrastructure to enable new ideas. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible.
Though people at Stripe don’t tend to take themselves seriously, Stripe is a fairly serious place: our customers are depending on us for their livelihoods. We admire ambition, intensity, curiosity, humility, and rigor. The most effective people become knowledgeable about many domains besides their own. Any company is an applied exercise in understanding some aspect of society or the market. In working with so many (especially the new and innovative ones), we think that Stripe is one of the very best places to learn about how the world works.
About the team
Data Science at Stripe is a vibrant community where data analysts and data scientists learn and grow together. You'll work with some of the most fundamental data at Stripe, and use that data to help drive company-wide initiatives. We have a variety of Data Analytics roles and teams across Stripe and will seek to align you to the most relevant team based on your background.
What you’ll do
As an intern at Stripe you’ll work on projects across our stack that directly impact the way millions of businesses operate. You’ll own problems end to end with the support of your manager and teammates. It’s an opportunity to work alongside some of the most creative and technically rigorous data analysts and scientists in the industry. You'll partner deeply with teams across Stripe to ensure that our users, our products, and our business have the models, data products, and insights needed to make decisions and grow responsibly. You'll work closely with partners to extract insights from the rich and complex data at Stripe. You'll build metrics, scalable data pipelines, dashboards, and reports to inform and run the business. You'll deliver actionable business recommendations through analyses and data storytelling.
Our internship program is competitive and the expectations are high.
Responsibilities
- Analyze data and running experiments to drive impact
- Ensure that our users, our products, and our business have the models, data products, and insights needed to make decisions and grow responsibly
- Create metrics, reports, and dashboards to inform and run the business
- Extend Stripe’s metrics semantic layer
- Build new data assets and improve existing data assets to support decision-making, products, and business processes
- Assess the impact of decisions, product launches, and product improvements using business analytics and A/B testing
- Learn quickly by asking great questions, finding how to work with your mentor and teammates effectively, and communicating the status of your work clearly
- Present your work to the Data Science team, partner teams, and fellow interns
Who you are
- Ambitious builder: You’re energized by building solutions without clear precedent and solving problems with far-reaching consequences. Successful Stripes are deeply curious, and prefer the joy of discovery to the comfort of certainty.
- Rigorous thinker: You appreciate that things worth doing are rarely simple. You enjoy working on problems that have never been tackled before.
- Adaptable problem solver: You adapt quickly and treat obstacles as opportunities. At Stripe we embrace kindness while encouraging Stripes to take measured risks and act boldly, even in the absence of consensus.
Minimum requirements
- Enrolled in a quantitative Bachelor’s or Master's degree program (e.g. Data Analytics, Statistics, Economics, Mathematics, etc.) with the expectation of graduating in December 2027 or spring/summer 2028
- Experience with SQL
- Proficiency with AI tools to accelerate model development, analysis, and coding
- Experience communicating and collaborating with multidisciplinary stakeholders in a team environment
Preferred qualifications
- Experience writing and debugging data pipelines
- Demonstrated ability to evaluate and receive feedback from mentors, peers, and stakeholders via experience from previous internships or other multi-person projects
- Ability to learn new systems and form an understanding of those systems, through independent research and working with a mentor and subject matter experts

• Experience managing and developing individual contributor talent across multiple levels, including coaching, career pathing, and performance management

jobs.title: Financial Data Analyst Intern, Technical Operations
jobs.description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a technology company focused on improving the conditions for economic growth and prosperity. We build programmable financial infrastructure, rethinking from first principles how financial services should work, to make it easier and cheaper for any business to start and scale. More than 10 million businesses build on Stripe, spanning the economic frontier—from solo founders to established enterprises—united by a practical focus on growth. The most ambitious companies in the world use Stripe as core infrastructure to grow faster. They process trillions of dollars a year on Stripe, equivalent to around 1.6% of global GDP. While economic growth makes everyone better off, open markets also enable greater variety. When any business can easily serve a global customer base, the quality and diversity of products in the world increase, and craft and creativity are unleashed into the smallest niches. Our own growth is wholly contingent on the success of the businesses building on Stripe. We therefore invest back into our technology at an unusual rate. We make upgrades to our products every single day to deliver compounding gains to our customers. We maintain some of the most reliable APIs on the internet. We build entirely new pieces of financial infrastructure to enable new ideas. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible.
Though people at Stripe don’t tend to take themselves seriously, Stripe is a fairly serious place: our customers are depending on us for their livelihoods. We admire ambition, intensity, curiosity, humility, and rigor. The most effective people become knowledgeable about many domains besides their own. Any company is an applied exercise in understanding some aspect of society or the market. In working with so many (especially the new and innovative ones), we think that Stripe is one of the very best places to learn about how the world works.
About the team
The APAC Payments TechOps team ensures the accuracy of financial data flowing through Stripe's payment infrastructure, manages aging balances, maintains compliance with partner and regulatory requirements, and builds tooling to detect and resolve data quality issues at scale. Through the internship, you will work with real financial data, gain experience in payments data analysis and operational problem-solving, and have opportunities to present your work to your team and the wider org. Each intern has a dedicated intern manager, and every project is part of the team's roadmap and will directly help Stripe's mission.
What you’ll do
Every internship at Stripe centers around a real, legitimate project that our team urgently needs. We will support you in shipping it. Yes, you will actually ship it. Example projects include building data quality checks for payment flows, creating dashboards to surface aging balance trends, automating compliance reporting, or analyzing cost structures across partner networks. As a Stripe intern, you'll be tackling important projects while working alongside exceptional people who insist on doing their best work. You'll learn from people with high standards who are great at inspiring others to do more and go further. We value technical and personal growth, and see our internship program as a vehicle to foster both.
Responsibilities
- Analyze financial data by writing queries and examining data quality, reconciliation accuracy, or cost structures across Stripe's payment flows
- Write code or build tooling that will be used in production and has meaningful impact to Stripe's payment operations
- Give and receive technical feedback through code reviews, data model discussions, or analysis walkthroughs
- Collaborate with engineers, product managers, and finance stakeholders to seek and incorporate feedback on your work
- Learn quickly by asking great questions, by working with your intern manager and teammates effectively, and by communicating the status of your work clearly
Who you are
- Ambitious builder: You’re energized by building solutions without clear precedent and solving problems with far-reaching consequences. Successful Stripes are deeply curious, and prefer the joy of discovery to the comfort of certainty.
- Rigorous thinker: You appreciate that things worth doing are rarely simple. You enjoy working on problems that have never been tackled before.
- Adaptable problem solver: You adapt quickly and treat obstacles as opportunities. At Stripe we embrace kindness while encouraging Stripes to take measured risks and act boldly, even in the absence of consensus.
Minimum requirements
- A strong fundamental understanding of quantitative analysis through pursuit of a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD degree in computer science, data science, finance, economics, information systems, or a related discipline
- Some experience and familiarity with programming or data analysis, either through side projects or coursework. We work mostly in SQL, Python, and Ruby. We believe new programming languages can be learned if the fundamentals and general knowledge are present
- Experience from previous internships or other multi-person projects, including open source contributions, that demonstrate evaluating and receiving feedback from mentors, peers, and stakeholders
- Ability to learn unfamiliar systems and form an understanding of those systems, through independent research and working with a mentor and subject matter experts
Preferred qualifications
- At least 2 years of university education, or equivalent work experience
- Familiarity with SQL and querying relational databases, either through coursework or personal projects
- Interest in payments, fintech, or financial systems
- Comfort with developer tools (e.g. git) and data visualization
- A strong interest in understanding how financial data flows through complex payment systems and ensuring its accuracy
- Ability to write clearly to explain analytical findings to stakeholders, team members, and other Stripes

Preferred qualifications

The Builder Experience Team makes it easier for Stripe’s product teams to build the right products, ship them with confidence, and help users realize value from them.
In order to build a great product, product teams must develop a deep understanding of users, shape and test ideas, coordinate across functions, navigate launch requirements, identify risks, gather feedback, and manage products after launch. Today, many of these workflows are fragmented, manual, or built around processes and tools that predate recent advances in AI.
We are a small, AI-native team reimagining how Stripe builds, ships, and ramps products. We experiment with new approaches across AI agents, automation, and process—and scale the ones that work. Our initial areas of focus include reinventing launch readiness from gates into guidelines, giving product teams richer and more timely context, and shortening the feedback loops between builders, users, Sales, and Support.
Our users are Stripe’s product managers, engineers, designers, researchers – and we help to simplify the interactions with the cross-functional teams that help bring products to market. We work closely with teams including all of our business unit PMs, Product Operations, and Kai, Stripe’s internal AI platform.

You’ll identify high-friction parts of Stripe’s product-development lifecycle, rapidly prototype new approaches, put them in the hands of real teams, and turn the strongest experiments into scaled solutions used by every product team at Stripe.

- Help define how the team operates, including its technical foundations, product-development practices, and standards for experimentation and quality.

jobs.description:

About the team and the role
The People Systems Operations Administrator supports the day-to-day work that keeps Stripe’s People technology running accurately and reliably. The role sits in the Service Delivery Center and works as part of the wider People Solutions team, with a close dotted-line partnership to People Solutions Systems Management.
You’ll own a defined set of routine tier 1 and tier 2 operational work across Workday and related People Systems. This includes monitoring support channels and system inboxes, triaging requests, completing repeatable administrative tasks, maintaining documentation, and routing complex issues to the right People Systems owner.
This is a hands-on operations role. It creates clearer separation between routine support work and the configuration, architecture, governance, and project delivery owned by the People Systems team.
What you’ll do
Support queue and request triage
- Monitor the Salesforce case management queue and Jira requests for People Systems work.
- Triage incoming requests by urgency, business impact, data sensitivity, and defined support process.
- Resolve standard requests using documented procedures, and route exceptions or higher-complexity work to the appropriate People Systems owner.
Keep request records accurate and complete, including status updates, required approvals, supporting documentation, and clear handoffs.
- Identify recurring request patterns and flag opportunities to improve documentation, self-service, or system processes.
Workday operations
- Monitor the Workday inbox for business process errors, stuck transactions, alerts, and other operational issues.
- Complete routine Workday support tasks, including standard access requests, account maintenance, and operational follow-up.
- Support Salesforce and JIRA run work and respond to common People Systems questions using approved guidance.
- Help with recurring operational tasks such as account monitoring, account resets, and quarterly account reviews.
- Support year-end activity, including schedule extensions, alert configuration, audit requests, and tracking follow-up items.
- Assist with release readiness by reviewing assigned Workday updates, completing test steps, documenting results, and escalating issues found during testing.
- Support recurring People programs, such as performance-cycle launches, using established runbooks and checklists.
Reporting, documentation, and Jira support
- Intake and triage Workday reporting and data requests. Confirm required information, route requests to the right owner, and provide status updates to requesters.
- Complete standard reporting tasks and access-related requests where there is a documented process and appropriate approval.
- Maintain runbooks, Trailhead content, standard operating procedures, and request templates so guidance stays current and easy to find.
- Support data-quality checks and follow established processes to correct or escalate issues.
Partnership with People Systems
- Work closely with People Systems analysts and engineers to understand support priorities, upcoming releases, recurring work, and escalation paths.
- Provide clear handoffs for work that requires configuration changes, advanced reporting, integrations, security decisions, or policy interpretation.
- Participate in regular reviews of queue trends, service levels, documentation gaps, and operational risks.
- Build platform knowledge over time, with opportunities to take on more complex administration and configuration work as skills develop.
Minimum requirements
- Experience in People operations, HR administration, systems support, service delivery, or another operations role involving high-volume, process-driven work.
- Strong attention to detail, particularly where accuracy affects People records, access, payroll, compliance, or reporting.
- Ability to work through a queue independently, prioritize requests, follow defined processes, and escalate issues at the right time.
- Clear written communication and comfort giving requesters concise status updates.
- Experience using Jira, Salesforce, or a similar case-management or ticketing tool.
- Comfort learning enterprise systems and following structured procedures across multiple tools.
- Strong organization skills and a consistent approach to documenting work and following requests through to resolution.
- Good judgment when working with confidential information.
Preferred qualifications
- Experience supporting Workday, including Core HCM, business processes, security administration, reporting, or Workday inbox monitoring.
- Experience handling reporting requests, data access requests, and standard user provisioning.
- Experience supporting cyclical People programs, compliance activities, audit requests, or system-release testing.
What success looks like
Within the first six months, you will:
- Own the defined tier 1 and routine tier 2 People Systems queue work with accurate, timely resolution and clear escalation.
- Establish dependable monitoring for People Systems tickets in Salesforce, JIRA, the Workday inbox, and recurring operational tasks.
- Reduce avoidable handoffs and ensure complex work reaches the right People Systems owner with the context needed to act.
- Keep core runbooks and self-service guidance current based on recurring request patterns.
- Give People Systems analysts and engineers more capacity for configuration, governance, architecture, and strategic delivery work.

- Experience building delightfully simple developer experiences

- An ability to quickly learn new skills and take on new challenges
- Experience at rapidly growing startups and the flexibility it requires

- An understanding of EC2 Nitro Enclaves and ASGs/Kubernetes

The Identity Product Experience team owns Stripe Identity’s mobile SDKs for iOS, Android, and React Native. jobs.title: Offensive Security Engineer
jobs.description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
The Proactive Threat team is responsible for identifying vulnerabilities and security weaknesses across Stripe's systems, applications, networks, and cloud infrastructure — before adversaries do. We operate as a hybrid offensive function: conducting penetration testing, emulating real-world threat actors through red team operations, and partnering closely with our defensive security teams to validate detection capabilities and improve Stripe's overall security posture.
We are builders first. Our team develops custom tooling, automation frameworks, and internal platforms that scale our offensive capabilities and enable repeatable, high-fidelity assessments. We believe the best offensive security engineers are equal parts hacker and engineer.
The team is distributed across the United States, primarily operating in Eastern and Pacific time zones, and collaborates regularly with security, engineering, and product stakeholders across Stripe — including teams in Europe and Asia.
What you'll do
As an Offensive Security Engineer on the Proactive Threat team, you will simulate the tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) of real-world adversaries to uncover security risks across Stripe's products and infrastructure. You'll conduct hands-on penetration testing, lead red team engagements, and collaborate with blue team counterparts to validate and improve detection and response capabilities. Your work will directly influence how Stripe builds, ships, and secures financial infrastructure used by millions of businesses worldwide.
Beyond assessments, you'll design and build offensive tooling and automation that amplifies the team's impact. You'll leverage threat intelligence to prioritize testing efforts, contribute to incident investigations when needed, and act as a subject-matter expert for security initiatives across the company.
Responsibilities
- Conduct comprehensive penetration tests across web applications, APIs, cloud environments (AWS/GCP/Azure), mobile applications, and internal infrastructure
- Plan and execute red team engagements that emulate the TTPs of cyber and criminal threat actors targeting financial services, including initial access, lateral movement, persistence, and data exfiltration scenarios
- Perform assumed-breach and objective-based assessments to test detection and response capabilities in coordination with defensive teams
- Partner with detection engineering, threat intelligence, and incident response teams to validate security controls, identify coverage gaps, and improve detection fidelity
- Contribute adversary tradecraft insights to inform detection rule development, threat hunting hypotheses, and incident response playbooks
- Support incident investigations by providing offensive expertise, log analysis, and root cause analysis when required
- Design, develop, and maintain custom offensive tools, scripts, and automation frameworks to enhance assessment efficiency and coverage
- Build internal platforms and workflows that enable scalable, repeatable offensive operations
- Contribute to internal security tooling repositories and champion engineering best practices within the team
- Automate repetitive testing tasks, payload generation, and reporting workflows using modern development practices
- Produce clear, actionable reports that communicate technical findings, business risk, and remediation guidance to both technical and non-technical stakeholders
- Act as a subject-matter expert and primary point of contact for stakeholder teams engaged in offensive security programs and Stripe-wide security initiatives
- Lead offensive security projects end-to-end, mentor junior team members, and foster a culture of continuous learning and knowledge sharing
- Stay current with emerging threats, vulnerabilities, and attack techniques; share research internally and contribute to the broader security community
Who you are
We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
Minimum requirements
- 5+ years of experience in offensive security, penetration testing, red teaming, or a related field
- Strong programming skills in Python, Go, or similar languages, with demonstrated experience building tools, automation, or custom exploits
- Deep knowledge of web application security, including OWASP Top 10, ASVS, and common vulnerability classes (injection, auth flaws, business logic, etc.)
- Hands-on experience with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP), including cloud-native attack techniques and misconfigurations
- Proficiency with offensive tooling such as Burp Suite, Cobalt Strike, Mythic, Sliver, BloodHound, or similar frameworks
- Familiarity with adversary tradecraft and frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK, including TTPs for initial access, privilege escalation, lateral movement, and exfiltration
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technical findings into clear, risk-based recommendations
- Ability to think like an adversary — creative, persistent, and able to holistically assess risk in complex environments
Preferred qualifications
- Experience conducting offensive security in fintech, financial services, or other highly regulated environments
- Background in vulnerability research, exploit development, or CVE discovery
- Experience collaborating with threat intelligence, detection engineering, or incident response teams (purple team operations)
- Familiarity with big data and log analysis tools (Splunk, Databricks, PySpark, osquery, etc.) for threat hunting or investigative support
- Proficiency with AI/LLM-assisted development tools (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot) and experience applying them to offensive security workflows
- Interest or experience in agentic automation — using LLMs or autonomous agents to augment reconnaissance, vulnerability discovery, or exploitation workflows
- Experience testing AI/ML systems or LLM-based applications for security weaknesses (prompt injection, training data extraction, model manipulation, etc.)
- Contributions to open-source security tools, published research, blog posts, or conference presentations
- Relevant certifications such as OSCP, OSWE, OSEP, OSED, CRTO, CPTS, PNPT, GXPN, or cloud security certifications
Location
This role is remote within the United States. While you are welcome to visit Stripe offices for team meetings, on-sites, and events, our expectation is that you would regularly work from home. The team primarily coordinates across Eastern and Pacific time zones, with regular collaboration with stakeholders in Europe and Asia.
Compensation & Benefits
The annual US base salary range for this role is $170,400 – $255,700. This range may span multiple career levels and will be refined during the interview process based on experience, qualifications, and location.
Additional benefits include:
- Equity participation in Stripe's growth
- 401(k) plan with matching contributions from day one
- Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage
- Wellness stipends
- Annual budget for training, certifications, and conference attendance

jobs.title: PhD Data Scientist, Intern
jobs.description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a technology company focused on improving the conditions for economic growth and prosperity. We build programmable financial infrastructure, rethinking from first principles how financial services should work, to make it easier and cheaper for any business to start and scale. More than 10 million businesses build on Stripe, spanning the economic frontier—from solo founders to established enterprises—united by a practical focus on growth. The most ambitious companies in the world use Stripe as core infrastructure to grow faster. They process trillions of dollars a year on Stripe, equivalent to around 1.6% of global GDP. While economic growth makes everyone better off, open markets also enable greater variety. When any business can easily serve a global customer base, the quality and diversity of products in the world increase, and craft and creativity are unleashed into the smallest niches. Our own growth is wholly contingent on the success of the businesses building on Stripe. We therefore invest back into our technology at an unusual rate. We make upgrades to our products every single day to deliver compounding gains to our customers. We maintain some of the most reliable APIs on the internet. We build entirely new pieces of financial infrastructure to enable new ideas. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible.
Though people at Stripe don’t tend to take themselves seriously, Stripe is a fairly serious place: our customers are depending on us for their livelihoods. We admire ambition, intensity, curiosity, humility, and rigor. The most effective people become knowledgeable about many domains besides their own. Any company is an applied exercise in understanding some aspect of society or the market. In working with so many (especially the new and innovative ones), we think that Stripe is one of the very best places to learn about how the world works.
About the team
Our Data Science team partners deeply with teams across Stripe to ensure that our users, our products, and our business have the models, data products, and insights needed to make decisions and grow responsibly. We're looking for data scientists with a passion for analyzing data, building machine learning and statistical models, and running experiments to drive impact. Our Fraud, Losses, and Financial Crime Data Science team builds the models and data products that protect Stripe and its users from fraud, account takeover, and financial crime. We own the full fraud and loss modeling stack - from account takeover detection and card fraud classification to merchant-level loss estimation, unsupervised anomaly detection, and financial crime risk modeling. We partner with Fraud Engineering, Financial Crimes Engineering, and Risk Operations to bring these systems into production and ensure they have measurable impact on Stripe's financial integrity and user trust.
What you’ll do
As an intern at Stripe you’ll work on projects across our stack that directly impact the way millions of businesses operate. You’ll own problems end to end with the support of your manager and teammates. It’s an opportunity to work alongside some of the most creative and technically rigorous data analysts and scientists in the industry. You'll partner deeply with teams across Stripe to ensure that our users, our products, and our business have the models, data products, and insights needed to make decisions and grow responsibly. You'll work closely with partners to extract insights from the rich and complex data at Stripe. You'll build metrics, scalable data pipelines, dashboards, and reports to inform and run the business. You'll deliver actionable business recommendations through analyses and data storytelling.
Our internship program is competitive and the expectations are high.
Responsibilities
- Applying probability distributions, statistical inference, and hypothesis testing to quantify uncertainty and evaluate business outcomes
- Using Python or R for data analysis, data processing, visualizations, statistical modeling, machine learning, predictive analytics, automation, and implementing causal inference and experimental analyses
- Building, training, and evaluating predictive models across regression and classification tasks for bias-variance trade-offs and model selection
- Modeling temporal dependencies, seasonality, and trend decomposition to generate and evaluate time-series predictions
- Identifying structural patterns, clusters, and outliers in unlabeled data
- Deploying models in production and adjusting model thresholds to improve performance
- Designing, running, and analyzing complex experiments and leveraging causal inference designs
- Using SQL and Spark to create, transform, and analyze large datasets
- Learn quickly by asking great questions, finding how to work with your mentor and teammates effectively, and communicating the status of your work clearly
- Present your work to the Data Science team, partner teams, and fellow interns.
Who you are
- Ambitious builder: You’re energized by building solutions without clear precedent and solving problems with far-reaching consequences. Successful Stripes are deeply curious, and prefer the joy of discovery to the comfort of certainty.
- Rigorous thinker: You appreciate that things worth doing are rarely simple. You enjoy working on problems that have never been tackled before.
- Adaptable problem solver: You adapt quickly and treat obstacles as opportunities. At Stripe we embrace kindness while encouraging Stripes to take measured risks and act boldly, even in the absence of consensus.
Minimum requirements
- Enrolled in a quantitative PhD program (e.g. Data Science, Statistics, Economics, Mathematics, etc.) with the expectation of graduating in December 2027 or spring/summer 2028
- Experience with SQL and a scientific computing language (such as Python, R, etc.)
- Proficiency with AI tools to accelerate model development, analysis, and coding
- Experience communicating and collaborating with multidisciplinary stakeholders in a team environment
Preferred qualifications
- Experience writing and debugging data pipelines
- Demonstrated ability to evaluate and receive feedback from mentors, peers, and stakeholders via experience from previous internships or other multi-person projects
- Ability to learn new systems and form an understanding of those systems, through independent research and working with a mentor and subject matter experts

The Developer Experiences team owns that work: the SDKs, APIs, integration primitives, documentation, and example apps that developers—and, increasingly, AI agents—use to build on Terminal. The Security Incident Response team works to analyze, investigate, and respond to threats before they impact Stripe’s business or users. You will be performing initial triage of potential security incidents through log and data analysis to determine whether or not activity is a substantiated or valid threat, assessing severity and potential impact, taking pre-approved remediation measures to contain a threat, and escalating findings to investigators for further review and analysis. You will use your knowledge of cyber threats and the results of your analysis to coordinate with partner teams to improve threat detection through tuning and creation of new use cases, to improve capabilities through enriching existing data and creation of new data feeds, and to improve triage accuracy, consistency and timeliness through automation. This role plays a critical part in threat detection and response, ultimately reducing the likelihood of security breaches and protecting sensitive company information.
Responsibilities
- Analyze and investigate activity on company devices and cloud infrastructure that could represent a security threat
- Work cross-functionally with the Security teams to develop solutions for analyzing security events at scale and protecting Stripe networks, systems, and data
- Interpret disparate data sources to report on trends and support investigative requests
- Collect requirements for enhancements to detection models and response systems
- Leverage existing systems and data to perform analyses and promote process improvements
- Provide actionable insights to help identify, prevent, detect, and respond to anomalous or potentially malicious user activity
- Collaborate effectively with teammates, lead projects, mentor others, and develop and champion quality operational standards across the team
