About the Role
Cloudflare’s architecture is built on a homogeneous edge: every server in over 330 cities runs every service—from L4/L7 proxies (FL2, Pingora) and DNS to the Workers runtime, cache, and storage. While this design maximizes hardware utilization, it creates a difficult distributed attribution problem. Machine-level telemetry tells us how loaded a server is, but not which product, customer, or upstream service is responsible for that load.
MAPS (Metrics and Analytics for Product Segmentation) is a newly formed team building the core instrumentation, collection, and data platform to solve this from the ground up. We are architecting a system to continuously measure CPU, network bandwidth, memory, and storage utilization across the entire global fleet without sampling—attributing resource consumption both to the underlying system service and to the specific product, account, and zone being served.
The data MAPS produces serves two critical functions at Cloudflare:
- Real-Time Control Plane: MAPS is the primary telemetry input for Cloudflare’s next-generation global load balancer, shifting traffic management from open-loop heuristics to closed-loop routing driven by real-time, per-service resource capacity and consumption (within seconds).
- Fleet Economics & Capacity Planning: MAPS provides the long-term analytical dataset in ClickHouse used to map product demand forecasts to physical hardware requirements, calculate true cost-to-serve per product, and drive multi-year infrastructure investments.
What You’ll Do
You will work across the full lifecycle of a greenfield, high-throughput telemetry system running on every machine at the Cloudflare edge:
- Host-Level Instrumentation ("Outside View"): Build and maintain low-overhead Linux daemons (netacctd, maps_collector) in Rust and C that use eBPF (cgroup_skb) and cgroup v2 accounting to measure per-service resource consumption directly from the kernel.
- High-Performance Client Libraries ("Inside View"): Architect non-blocking, zero-allocation reporting SDKs in Rust and Go used by Cloudflare’s highest-throughput data-plane services to report per-request resource usage and product attribution over local Unix domain sockets.
- Edge Aggregation & Streaming: Build the per-machine collector daemon that ingests millions of events per second, performs bounded in-memory time-window aggregation, serves low-latency gRPC streams to the global load balancer, and flushes batch rollups to ClickHouse.
- Reconciliation & Correctness: Solve complex attribution problems—such as reconciling kernel-level cgroup measurements against application-reported metrics, and attributing resource usage when one multi-tenant service executes work on behalf of another.
- Cross-Team Architecture: Partner directly with the engineering teams behind Cloudflare’s core proxies, runtimes, and storage engines to instrument their critical paths without degrading tail latency.

- Strong systems programming experience in Rust, Go, or C, with a solid grasp of memory layout, concurrency, and performance-critical code paths.
- Experience designing and operating latency- and resource-sensitive server infrastructure or high-throughput data pipelines at scale.
- Strong fundamentals in Linux systems internals—processes, cgroups, sockets, and how the kernel accounts for compute, memory, and I/O.
- Proven ability to work across organizational boundaries: reading unfamiliar codebases, aligning with other infrastructure teams, and driving complex integrations to completion.
- A pragmatic approach to owning outcomes—from kernel-level data collection and wire protocols (protobuf/Cap'n Proto) all the way to the analytical tables consumers query.
Bonus Points
- Hands-on experience writing and verifying eBPF programs, or deep familiarity with the Linux networking stack and scheduler.
- Experience designing schemas and query patterns for distributed columnar databases (particularly ClickHouse) at high ingestion rates.
- Background in profiling, benchmarking, and debugging performance bottlenecks in production Linux environments (perf, PMU counters, flamegraphs).

- Strong customer service orientation and communication skills, both written and verbal.
- Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

- Experience supporting cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP) and SaaS application integrations.

jobs.description:
Developer Engagement Lead
Reports to: Head of Developer Growth · New York, NY
NOTE: This is not a traditional social media or community management role. It’s a developer growth role that sits within the Product org.
Developers are already talking about Datadog - on Reddit, Discord, Hacker News, GitHub, X, LinkedIn, YouTube, forums, and places we probably haven’t found yet.
We’re hiring a Developer Engagement Lead to make sure we’re part of those conversations.
You’ll own how Datadog listens, responds, and participates across developer channels. That means running our existing developer social accounts, building our presence in new communities, creating the monitoring and response systems that help us find relevant conversations quickly, and connecting developers with the right people inside Datadog.
This is a builder role. We’re not looking for someone to manage a content calendar or simply moderate a community. We want someone who can build the operating model for developer engagement at scale.
What you'll own
- Build our developer listening and engagement system. Create the tooling and workflows to monitor conversations about Datadog, our products, our competitors, and the problems developers are trying to solve across Reddit, Hacker News, Discord, GitHub, X, LinkedIn, Stack Overflow, YouTube, and other relevant platforms.
- Turn monitoring into action. Build a process for identifying conversations worth joining, determining when Datadog should respond, and routing questions or feedback to the right engineer, PM, DevRel, support, or product expert.
- Own our developer channels. Run @datadogdevs on X and Datadog Developers on LinkedIn, including publishing, engagement, replies, and experimentation.
- Expand where Datadog participates. Establish and grow our presence in places where developers already spend time. That may include launching Discord, creating a stronger Reddit strategy, building participation models for Hacker News or GitHub, or identifying entirely new channels.
- Make Datadog more responsive. Define response guidelines, escalation paths, ownership models, and expectations so developer conversations don’t disappear into screenshots and Slack threads.
- Participate directly. Know when to respond as Datadog, when to pull in an expert, when an engineer should answer under their own name, and when the best response is simply to listen.
- Create feedback loops into Product. Surface recurring questions, pain points, objections, competitive mentions, product feedback, and emerging developer conversations to Product, Engineering, Developer Growth, and other relevant teams.
- Get more technical voices into the conversation. Make it easy for Datadog engineers, PMs, researchers, and other experts to participate directly in developer conversations instead of relying exclusively on brand accounts.
- Turn shipped work into conversations. Find compelling ways to bring releases, changelogs, technical content, demos, events, and engineering work into the places developers are already talking.
- Build measurement that matters. Define how we measure developer engagement beyond follower counts and impressions. Track things like conversations joined, response coverage, sentiment and recurring themes, participation from technical teams, traffic, product discovery, trials, and signups.
- Run experiments. Test new platforms, formats, tooling, workflows, response models, and engagement programs with a clear hypothesis and readout. Keep what works and move quickly past what doesn’t.
Who you are
You understand how developers behave online.
You’ve built an audience, community, engagement program, developer program, or similar function, and can point to outcomes you changed.
You have strong judgment about when a company should join a conversation and when it shouldn’t.
You are naturally curious. If developers suddenly start discussing something relevant to Datadog, your instinct is to understand why, find the thread, and figure out whether we should participate.
You think in systems. If ten people are manually forwarding Reddit posts into Slack, you want to build something better.
You’re comfortable with tooling, automation, monitoring platforms, APIs, AI, and lightweight workflows. You don’t necessarily need to be an engineer, but you should be comfortable working closely with engineers and technical products.
You can create structure where none exists: monitoring rules, triage processes, response playbooks, escalation paths, reporting, and measurement.
You know how to earn participation from internal experts rather than simply assigning them another marketing task.
You move quickly, have strong judgment, and know what can ship immediately versus what needs another set of eyes.
You have opinions about developer culture, platforms, formats, and internet behavior — and you update those opinions when the evidence changes.
Your background
You may come from Growth,Developer Marketing, Audience Development, Product, Media, Social, Technical Communications, or somewhere entirely different.
What matters most is that you can show us how you’ve built participation around an audience, created systems that scale engagement, and turned what people were saying into action.
Experience working with a technical or enthusiast audience is especially valuable.
Bonus points for:
- Experience building social listening or community-monitoring systems
- Deep familiarity with Reddit, Discord, Hacker News, GitHub, Stack Overflow, X, or similar developer platforms
- Experience launching or operating a Discord or other owned developer space
- Experience creating triage, escalation, or response workflows across large organizations
- Familiarity with developer tools, infrastructure, observability, security, AI, or open source
- Experience using automation or AI to scale monitoring and engagement
- An existing developer audience or active participation in technical communities
- Strong instincts around short-form technical content and video

jobs.title: Engineering Manager I, Commercial Audit
jobs.description:
As the Engineering Manager for Commercial Audit, you will lead a high-performing team responsible for scaling Datadog’s security and compliance posture through automation, tooling, and engineering excellence. Our GRC (Governance, Risk, and Compliance) function is a critical partner to the broader Security and Engineering organizations, ensuring that Datadog not only meets rigorous global regulatory standards but does so in a way that is efficient, scalable, and integrated into our cloud-native infrastructure. You will manage a team of engineers and analysts who are transitioning to a GRC engineering direction to treat compliance as a software problem, leveraging AI, custom tooling, CI/CD pipelines, and cloud-native services to turn complex regulatory requirements into actionable, automated controls.
You will lead the strategy, roadmap, and execution of Datadog’s Commercial Audit initiatives. This is a high-impact leadership role where you will grow a team of engineers and analysts responsible for directly maintaining our compliance programs and related audits (e.g., SOC2, PCI, HIPAA, ISO) while looking to improve efficiency and effectiveness through platforms and tooling. You will act as a bridge between technical engineering, legal, and compliance, enabling the organization to move fast while maintaining a secure and compliant environment. You will champion a culture of "compliance-as-code," identifying opportunities to automate evidence collection, streamline control testing, and reduce manual toil for both your team and our partner engineering teams.
At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds, and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.
What You’ll Do:
- Lead the strategy, roadmap, and execution of Datadog’s commercial security compliance efforts, shifting from manual audit processes to automated, scalable platforms and methodologies.
- Build, mentor, and grow a high-performing team of engineers and analysts, fostering a culture of technical excellence, continuous learning, and cross-functional collaboration.
- Partner within Information Security to operationalize a common control framework that integrates seamlessly into Datadog’s architecture and processes.
- Drive the development of internal tooling to automate evidence collection and dashboarding, reducing operational friction across the organization.
- Define and track program metrics: control coverage, audit efficiency, and automation adoption
- Collaborate with broader internal engineering teams to embed compliance-by-design into our infrastructure, CI/CD pipelines, and cloud-native service adoption.
Who You Are:
- You build strong, trusted relationships across engineering, legal, product, and executive stakeholders. You remain calm under pressure, navigate disagreement with diplomacy, and consistently bring people to alignment without creating unnecessary friction.
- You are a steady, low-ego leader who earns trust through consistency, diplomacy, and sound judgment. You can navigate difficult conversations, resolve conflict constructively, and maintain strong working relationships across diverse teams.
- You have experience leading or managing teams in security engineering, GRC, or risk management with a focus on leveraging AI to build automation and tooling for transitioning to a GRC engineering approach.
- Strong technical background with the ability to review code (Python, Go), interpret architecture diagrams, and understand infrastructure (Kubernetes, AWS/GCP/Azure).
- Deep understanding of the modern compliance landscape (e.g., HIPAA, SOC2, PCI, ISO 27001, FedRAMP) and experience implementing them at scale in cloud-native environments.
- You are a clear communicator who can translate complex technical or regulatory requirements into "plain language" for engineers, leadership, and external auditors alike.
- You possess a systems-thinking mindset—you look for upstream root causes and downstream impacts rather than solving problems in isolation.
- Experience in a SaaS or cloud infrastructure company where security scale and complexity are first-order challenges.
- Experienced people leader with a focus on mentorship, team growth, and inclusion. You know how to build trust and alignment across diverse teams.
- You operate with both rigor and pragmatism. You know when to build a bespoke engineering solution and when to leverage existing platforms or processes.
Nice to Haves:
- Prior experience working as an auditor (e.g., QSA) or directly facilitating audits, with the ability to negotiate scope and timelines effectively.

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineering Manager - Datadog for Startups
jobs.description:
Datadog's Forward Deployed Engineering function is in an active growth phase, and the FDE Manager will play a central role in shaping what comes next. Working in close partnership with the Head of Datadog for Startups and Forward Deployed Engineers, and the existing FDE team, you will help define and expand the FDE framework, build out the structures and processes that allow the team to operate at scale, and extend the program's reach well beyond any single customer segment.
This role sits at the rare intersection of sales, execution, program design, and hands-on engineering leadership. You are part field technical leader, part program architect, and part cross-functional connector. You will help determine what the FDE motion looks like at Datadog, contribute to its playbook, and push the boundaries of what the team can deliver.

jobs.description:

We maintain 11 open source SDKs across Browser, iOS, Android, React Native, Flutter, Kotlin Multiplatform, Unity, and more.

It's a rare chance to own a developer platform that ships in public, at a scale where small decisions reach a lot of customers, and to shape how Datadog builds client-side products in the AI-native era. Both the team and its scope are expanding, so there's plenty of room to grow.

Define release cadences and help customers adopt updates, managing breaking changes in SDKs that can't be rolled back once they're installed in customers' apps

jobs.title: Manager II, Developer Advocacy
jobs.description:
Developer Advocates at Datadog are engineers who share their expertise with technical practitioners, help customers tell their stories, and represent the perspectives of our community inside Datadog.
As a Manager II on the Advocacy team, you will lead our Community Advocacy functions. You will manage a team of Developer Advocates responsible for global programs such as Datadog Ambassadors, Champions, and User Groups, as well as opportunities for customer engineers to share their expertise through technical writing, public speaking, and other community contributions.
Across these interconnected programs, your team will enable customer engineers to contribute technical knowledge, lead communities, and turn their experiences into compelling content and conference talks for Datadog and third-party channels. This role combines people leadership, program strategy, technical judgment, and cross-functional influence to amplify authentic customer voices, deepen understanding of Datadog and its products, and foster a thriving community of practitioners.
What You’ll Do:
- Lead and develop a team of Developer Advocates, setting clear expectations, guiding priorities, coaching performance, supporting career growth, and fostering an inclusive, high-performing culture
- Own the strategy, goals, and roadmap for Community Advocacy, translating broader Advocacy and company priorities into focused programs and measurable outcomes
- Guide the continued development of our Ambassador, Champion, and User Group programs, creating clear contributor journeys, expectations, enablement, recognition, and opportunities for customer engineers to increase their impact
- Build repeatable systems that enable customer engineers to contribute technical knowledge, create content, share best practices, and serve as trusted leaders within their communities
- Develop a strong pipeline of customer stories by identifying compelling practitioners and helping them shape authentic, technically credible narratives
- Oversee the support, co-development, and coaching of conference talks by customer engineers—from identifying an idea and developing an abstract through content review, rehearsal, and delivery—for Datadog events, including our flagship user conference, DASH, as well as third-party industry conferences
- Establish measures of success for Community Advocacy, using qualitative and quantitative insights to evaluate program health, contributor engagement, content quality, audience impact, and customer outcomes
- Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Marketing, Events, Customer Success, and regional teams to align priorities, identify opportunities, and scale customer participation across Datadog initiatives
- Ensure insights from Ambassadors, Champions, User Group participants, speakers, and other community members are shared with the appropriate teams inside Datadog, strengthening the connection between our customers and our products
- Balance strategic leadership with selective hands-on contribution, including coaching speakers, reviewing technical content, participating in community programs, and representing Datadog when appropriate
Who You Are:
- You are an experienced people manager who has led autonomous technical professionals, coached performance, developed talent, and translated complex goals into achievable plans
- You have experience defining and delivering successful developer advocacy, developer relations, technical community, or a related functions
- You have built or meaningfully contributed to programs that enable external practitioners to participate, contribute, create content, or lead communities at scale
- You have experience helping technical practitioners develop and communicate their stories, including coaching conference speakers or co-developing technically credible talks and content
- You are a former software developer, SRE, or other technical practitioner—or have equivalent technical depth—with the judgment needed to assess technical accuracy and coach effective technical narratives

jobs.title: Product Solutions Architect - FinOps
jobs.description:
The Product Solutions Architecture (PSA) team acts as a technical multiplier across Datadog. PSAs are domain experts who partner with Field teams on complex customer use cases across pre- and post-sales engagements and scale their impact by producing reusable collateral, including reference architectures, technical guides, and enablement assets. By feeding real-world customer insights back to Datadog Product teams, PSAs help influence product roadmaps while accelerating adoption, usage, and long-term customer success.
Datadog's Cloud Cost Management (CCM) suite helps Platform, Application Teams, Operations, FinOps, and Finance teams understand, allocate, and reduce cloud spend by putting cost data next to the observability data that explains it. As a Product Solutions Architect, you will partner closely with Datadog customers and the Cloud Cost Management product team to design product use cases, implement best practices, and drive adoption of CCM across customer environments. This includes infrastructure cost allocation, cloud costs, token usage, container costs, budgets, and optimization recommendations.
At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds, and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.
What You'll Do
- Serve as the in-house subject matter expert for Datadog's Cloud Cost Management products, including cost visibility across AWS, Azure, and GCP, Kubernetes and container cost allocation, custom and SaaS cost ingestion, budgets, anomaly detection, and cost optimization recommendations
- Provide architectural guidance on capacity planning, comparing cloud service cost models, and balancing performance vs. cost trade-offs across different cloud environments
- Guide customers on tokenomics and AI cost attribution across providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Google Gemini, Vertex AI, and GitHub Copilot), helping teams map API keys, models, and usage to teams and business units using Tag Pipelines.
- Help enterprise clients track real-time AI spend changes, set up cost anomaly monitoring, and connect token usage back to business outcomes and unit economics (such as cost per user or cost per ticket).
- Partner with Field teams to provide hands-on technical and architectural guidance to enterprise customers adopting CCM, including designing tagging and cost allocation strategies, showback and chargeback models, and cost reporting that connects spend to services, teams, and business units

- Act as a trusted advisor to Product Management by delivering actionable feedback informed by real-world field experience, helping shape the roadmap for cost allocation, multi-cloud cost visibility, token usage, optimization workflows, and FinOps integrations

- You bring a strong engineering foundation, with hands-on experience managing, allocating, or optimizing cloud spend, or building FinOps programs and internal cost tooling in production environments at a large scale, and are comfortable diving deep into billing data and architectural tradeoffs to understand what drives cost
- You are familiar with cloud infrastructure and core observability concepts, such as tracing, metrics, and logging, and understand how compute, storage, networking, and container platforms (including Kubernetes) translate into cloud bills
- Deep understanding of cost models, performance characteristics, and capacity planning across various cloud services and managed platforms
- Experience with languages such as Python and/or SQL, and familiarity with querying and modeling large billing datasets, tagging strategies, and infrastructure-as-code
- Comfortable operating in rapidly evolving, ambiguous technical domains
- You build deep context across teams and translate it into reusable, scalable solutions
- You take ownership from problem definition through implementation and measurable outcomes

jobs.title: Senior AI Research Engineer - LLM Training & Inference Infrastructure
jobs.description:
As a Research Engineer on the Frontier Foundations team, you will partner with Research Scientists to build the systems that run large-scale LLM training, reinforcement learning, and inference at Datadog. You will build and operate an in-house distributed runtime that schedules work across large GPU clusters, and you will own how quickly researchers can iterate and how reliably long training runs complete.
Building on our track record of AI-powered solutions (e.g., Bits AI, Bits Evolve, and our time series foundation model Toto), Datadog AI Research (DAIR) tackles high-risk, high-reward problems grounded in real-world challenges in cloud observability and security.
The Frontier Foundations team builds and maintains the high-performance infrastructure that lets us train and serve large language models at scale. It supports both of our research areas:
Trained Agents for Observability -- Post-training models to operate autonomously across Datadog's domain. SRE incident response is our first target, with a clear path to code repair, security response, and infrastructure optimization. We build the simulation environments, RL training loops, and evaluation infrastructure needed to train agents that match or surpass frontier models at a fraction of the cost.
What You'll Do:
- Design, build, and operate distributed training and inference infrastructure for large language models, including Mixture-of-Experts models
- Scale training with parallelism strategies (data, tensor, pipeline, and expert), memory optimization, checkpointing, and failure recovery
- Build inference and rollout systems that support evaluation, experimentation, and RL without slowing down training
- Build execution environments and sandboxes for online RL and agent post-training
- Own continuous performance validation: regular benchmarks of rollout speed, training throughput, and learning behavior, with dashboards that make regressions visible
- Improve the researcher experience: job submission, scheduling, quotas, GPU utilization, and observability
- Work with platform teams on cluster capacity, networking, and scheduling across GPU providers
- Investigate performance and reliability problems across hardware, software, and distributed systems
Who You Are:
- You have depth in distributed systems and ML infrastructure for training and inference at scale; experience with Ray, Kubernetes, Slurm, or similar frameworks is a plus
- You are proficient in Python and in at least one systems language (e.g., Rust, C++, or Go) ● You have experience operating large-scale training or serving infrastructure, or schedulers and orchestration systems for GPU or other high-performance workloads
- You understand what limits throughput/latency in distributed inference workloads: communication, memory, scheduling, and stragglers
- You have strong debugging, profiling, and incident-diagnosis skills, ideally including on-call experience
- You can explain design and performance trade-offs clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences
- Prior experience training machine learning models is valuable but not essential for engineers with strong distributed systems or HPC backgrounds
Bonus Points (any of the following):
- You are familiar with distributed training frameworks such as Megatron-LM, TorchTitan, or DeepSpeed
- You have experience with LLM inference engines such as vLLM or SGLang, including batching and KV-cache management
- You have experience with RL training systems and rollout infrastructure
- You have experience with collective communication (NCCL), RDMA, or low-latency networking
- You have experience with GPU benchmarking, profiling, and cluster performance monitoring
- You have experience building sandboxed code execution or large-scale evaluation infrastructure
- You have contributed to open-source ML or distributed systems projects

jobs.title: Senior Business Systems Analyst
jobs.description:
Business Systems drives efficiency across Datadog through business process analysis, systems automation and integrations, AI agent and MCP development, and vendor/software review. The team is increasingly embedded in cross-functional initiatives across People, Finance, GTM, Legal, Recruiting, and Technical Solutions — translating ambiguous business problems into scoped, buildable solutions and owning delivery end-to-end.
This is not a generalist BSA role. Each Senior BSA will own a cluster of business functions end-to-end, acting as an internal product manager for their domain rather than processing inbound requests reactively. There are two openings, each covering a different domain:
People, Recruiting, Legal or Finance, GTM, Procurement
As the role evolves alongside AI, Senior BSAs leverage agentic tools for data aggregation and context gathering while remaining the critical human-in-the-loop layer — owning business context and product outlook, validating use cases, managing stakeholder relationships, and making the judgment calls agents can't.
At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships that it builds, the creativity it brings to the table, and the collaboration of being together. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our employees can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.
What You’ll Do:
- Discovery and scoping: Translate ambiguous asks from business stakeholders into well-defined requirements that Business Systems Engineers can build against. Many stakeholders don't know what they want or the cross-functional impact of what they're asking for — you surface both before engineering begins.
- Cross-functional visibility: Identify dependencies, downstream impacts, and integration considerations that requesting teams miss.
- Proactive opportunity identification: Develop deep domain knowledge to identify automation and AI opportunities before they become inbound requests, shifting the team from reactive intake to strategic partnership.
- Stakeholder relationship ownership: Serve as the primary point of contact for your domain, reducing ad hoc consultations that currently land on the team lead and senior ICs.
- Systems and governance: Review system configuration, data integrity, and vendor fit within your domain and make recommendations to stakeholders and BSEs; maintain clear documentation (process diagrams, system flows, user guides); ensure compliance with security and privacy standards (e.g., GDPR, SOX).
Who You Are:
- Prior experience as a Business Systems Analyst or in a similar role, ideally within a high-tech or SaaS environment
- Experience owning a business domain end-to-end; comfortable operating like an internal product manager
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders and manage relationships with senior leadership
- Proven track record using AI/agentic tools for data aggregation and context-gathering, while knowing where human judgment is still required
- Demonstrable experience turning business processes into agentic or automated workflows in a prior role
- Experience in managing projects, particularly those involving multiple stakeholders and complex integrations
- Familiarity with security, privacy, and compliance standards (e.g., SOX, GDPR, SOC, ISO)
- 4+ years as a business system administrator (e.g., NetSuite, Salesforce, Workday, Zendesk) or a business systems analyst leading complex, cross-functional projects or a similar role

jobs.title: Senior Network Engineer, Office Technology
jobs.description:
About the Team
The Office Technology team designs, deploys, and operates the network infrastructure that keeps Datadog’s global offices connected, secure, and reliable. The team owns routing, switching, wireless, office firewalls, connectivity, and the observability and operational practices needed to provide a dependable employee experience at scale.
About the Role
As a Senior Network Engineer on the Office Technology team, you will own major network services and complex multi-site initiatives from problem definition and design through implementation, migration, and stable operations. You will act as a technical anchor for the team, leading design reviews and difficult troubleshooting, improving standards and automation, and helping other engineers deliver high-quality work.
This is a senior level role that combines hands-on engineering with technical leadership. You will shape team roadmap proposals and technical decisions through evidence and clear tradeoffs, while remaining accountable for reliable delivery and day-to-day operability.
What You’ll Do
- Design resilient, scalable solutions across LAN, Wi-Fi, routing, switching, and office firewalls, with explicit failure domains, capacity assumptions, security controls, and migration paths
- Author RFCs and lead design reviews, clearly documenting goals, constraints, alternatives, decisions, risks, validation, rollout, and rollback
- Build production readiness into network changes through meaningful service objectives, monitoring, alerting, runbooks, capacity planning, failure testing, and operational handoff
- Design reusable automation for provisioning, configuration, policy, compliance, telemetry, and change validation, with appropriate testing, peer review, drift detection, staged rollout, and safe rollback
- Own, alongside other senior engineers and leadership, the health and lifecycle of major network services, using data to improve reliability, coverage, performance, security, supportability, and cost
- Lead difficult incidents and root-cause investigations, communicate clearly during high-impact events, and ensure follow-up work addresses systemic causes
- Evaluate technology and vendor options and make pragmatic recommendations grounded in operability, security, scalability, and business impact
- Partner closely with Security, IT Support, Endpoints, AV, Workplace, Construction, Infrastructure teams, and external vendors on cross-functional initiatives
- Mentor other engineers, delegate effectively, improve team standards and documentation, and raise the quality of design and operational practices
- Participate in operational support, incident response, and planned maintenance activities as appropriate for the team
Who You Are
- A deeply experienced, hands-on network engineer with strong knowledge of TCP/IP, routing, switching, VLANs, wireless, DNS, DHCP, firewalls, and enterprise network security
- Experienced designing and operating resilient network infrastructure across distributed offices or campus environments
- Skilled at diagnosing complex issues using packet captures, logs, flow data, dashboards, and vendor telemetry, and at reasoning from protocols and failure modes
- Comfortable building maintainable automation using scripting, APIs, infrastructure-as-code, version control, testing, and CI/CD practices
- Strong in production engineering practices, including observability, service objectives, capacity planning, change safety, incident response, and post-incident improvement
- Able to take ambiguous problems from problem statement to durable solution, balancing reliability, security, user experience, cost, and delivery speed
- A clear, concise communicator who can lead technical discussions, explain tradeoffs, and build alignment with technical and non-technical partners
- A thoughtful mentor who raises the quality of others’ work without becoming a bottleneck or creating unnecessary process
- Responsible in your use of AI-assisted engineering tools: you protect sensitive data, validate outputs, and know when deterministic automation is the safer choice
Datadog values people from all walks of life. We understand not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That's okay. If you're passionate about technology and want to grow your skills, we encourage you to apply.
Bonus Points
- Experience with Datadog or other observability platforms, including network device monitoring, flow analytics, synthetic testing, and service-level reporting
- Experience with Python, Ansible, Terraform, Git-based workflows, or network automation frameworks
- Experience with network access control, RADIUS or 802.1X, segmentation, VPNs, or identity-aware and zero-trust networking
- Experience delivering global office expansions, infrastructure refreshes, or complex migrations in a rapidly scaling organization

jobs.title: Senior Staff Product Designer, Design Lab
jobs.description:
Datadog is entering a new chapter in how our product looks, feels, and operates. Our Design Lab is defining a new visual direction for the platform, and we’re looking for a Senior Staff Visual Product Designer to help turn that direction into a coherent product experience.
Datadog is dense, technical, and used by people working through complex problems—often under real pressure. The challenge is not simply applying a new aesthetic. It is rethinking hierarchy, layout, navigation, interaction, and product patterns so the experience becomes clearer, more cohesive, and more expressive without losing the power our users rely on.
This is a hands-on product design leadership role for someone who combines strong visual judgment with deep product and systems thinking. You’ll work alongside visual designers, motion designers, product designers, Design Systems, and Engineering to ensure the new direction changes how Datadog works—not just how it looks.
What You'll Do
- Co-develop Datadog’s next visual direction by applying and stress-testing it across representative product journeys.
- Translate visual principles into concrete decisions about hierarchy, layout, navigation, information architecture, interaction, and behavior.
- Use visual language to clarify complex, data-dense experiences — hierarchy, density, and attention.
- Hold the visual quality bar across work you don't own, and align teams around it.
- Prototype, test, and refine new patterns before they become systemized.
- Partner deeply with Product Design, Design Systems, and engineering to turn successful concepts into durable system guidance and implementation.
- Create clear artifacts, pilots, and narratives that help teams adopt the direction and raise the product quality bar.
- Influence stakeholders across design, engineering, product, and executive partners.
You will report directly to the Design Director and work as part of a small, focused team defining the future state before it scales across hundreds of designers and engineers.
Who You Are
- You have 12+ years of experience in product and/or visual design.
- Your craft is elevated, and you can execute it yourself at a high bar.
- You're product-native. You understand how visual design and product design act on each other in practice.
- You use visual language to clarify an experience, and you can say why a decision improves it.
- You think in information architecture, hierarchy, and holistic system work.
- You've taken a concept and turned it into patterns that scaled across a real product.
- You're comfortable operating in ambiguity and in large, complex organizations.
- Your portfolio demonstrates shipped product surfaces with exceptional visual quality.
- You are a persuasive collaborator who can make recommendations and align designers, engineers, product partners, and executives.
Why This Role Matters
DRUIDS powers every Datadog experience. The decisions made in this role will shape how millions of interactions feel across web, mobile, and emerging AI-driven surfaces. This is an opportunity to bring a new visual direction into a complex, engineering-forward platform and raise the craft bar across the organization.

jobs.description:
Datadog’s Cloud Networks team designs, builds, and maintains the production network infrastructure that powers everything built on top of our platform across AWS, GCP, Azure, and beyond. In this role, you’ll set technical direction for how we scale our multi-region, multi-cloud network footprint while keeping reliability and performance high. About the Role
We are looking for a Distinguished Engineer to lead technical direction across GitLab's Core DevOps services, the systems the majority of our users touch every day. Distinguished Engineers are recognized experts across multiple technology domains and represent the most senior level of technical leadership within and across divisions at the company.
Core DevOps builds continuous Integration, continuous deployment, planning, and source control experiences. These are among the most mature, highest traffic, and most deeply interconnected systems at GitLab. They carry years of accumulated architectural decisions, they sit in the critical path of our customers' own delivery pipelines, and they are being reshaped by the shift toward AI native development. The job is to raise their quality, converge them onto a coherent go-forward architecture, and retire accumulated risk, all without interrupting the millions of users and Fortune 100 organizations who depend on them.
GitLab is pursuing a set of company-wide engineering goals: large gains in developer productivity, measurably higher quality in what we ship, and engineering practices reshaped around AI and agentic workflows. Core DevOps is where much of that strategy has to land, because these are the services our own engineers and our customers depend on daily. In this role you will bring that strategy into Core DevOps in a form that works for long lived production systems, and carry what you learn here back out to the rest of engineering.
What You'll Do
- Set and continuously refine the go forward technical direction for CI, CD, Plan, and source code experiences, aligned against the horizontal architectural initiatives.
- Work directly with the VP of Engineering as her technical counterpart on planning, technical investment, and where the group's engineering effort should go.
- Translate GitLab's company-wide productivity, quality, and AI native engineering goals into concrete technical direction for Core DevOps, and turn into iterable roadmaps, partnering broadly across the org.
- Define what good means in measurable terms for these services, including availability, latency at p95 and p99, pipeline success rate, test reliability, data correctness, and defect escape rate, then hold designs and implementations to it.
- Maintain a clear and current picture of systemic technical risk across the group, including single points of failure, unowned critical paths, brittle coupling between CI/CD and Plan, scaling limits, and past decisions that now constrain the roadmap. Drive a prioritized plan to retire it.
- Lead the hardest design decisions hands on, writing code, prototypes, and proofs of concept where a design argument needs evidence behind it.
- Drive convergence on shared patterns, libraries, and paved paths, reducing how many different ways the same problem gets solved across the group.
- Design migration paths that let large, long lived systems change underneath users without breaking them, using incremental cutover, dual run, measurable rollback, and deprecation with clear timelines.
- Adopt the platform capabilities coming from GitLab's AI organization and the company's productivity initiatives into Core DevOps, feed this group's requirements back into them, and help prove what works on systems of this scale and maturity.
- Serve as the escalation point for complex or contested technical decisions across the group, including those where no single team owns the outcome.
- Review significant designs and merge requests in the group's critical paths, and use review to teach rather than only to gate.
- Ensure designs hold across GitLab.com, GitLab Dedicated, and Self-Managed deployments, and respect multi-tenant, compliance, and data governance boundaries in each.
- Partner with Infrastructure, Security, and SRE so Core DevOps services are observable and debuggable, and so failure modes degrade gracefully instead of cascading.
- Make architectural constraints and opportunities clear to Product in roadmap terms, so that technical investment and product ambition get planned together instead of traded off late.

- Deep expertise in AI and ML systems, including large language models, agentic frameworks, and autonomous workflow design at production scale.
- Proven track record of leading hands-on technical experimentation, including defining evaluation frameworks, running benchmarks, and translating findings into scalable architecture decisions.
- Strong background in scalable, multi-tenant distributed systems, including service decomposition, fault tolerance, observability, and operational resilience.

- Lead, hire, and grow a team of site reliability engineers and backend engineers, supporting career development, promotions, and onboarding.
- Own reliability for the job processing and caching platforms, including service-level objectives, error budgets, alerting, and weekly operational reviews.

- Experience managing reliability against service-level objectives, including defining service-level indicators, setting up burn-rate alerting, and planning capacity.
- Experience running a 24/7 on-call rotation and coordinating high-severity incidents.
- A track record of balancing operational work and incident follow-ups with roadmap projects, and pushing back on scope when deadlines can't be met.

An overview of this role
As a Software Engineer on GitLab's Authorization team, you'll help build and maintain the system that decides what every user, token, and automated agent can access on GitLab.com, Self-Managed, and Dedicated. You'll work alongside experienced engineers who guide the larger design decisions, delivering well-scoped changes and growing into ownership of larger parts of the system.
Today, that work is Ruby on Rails. Roughly 400 policy classes and a catalog of about 1,900 permissions sit behind every application programming interface (API) request. You'll work on fine-grained token permissions, custom roles, and the GraphQL and representational state transfer (REST) APIs that enforce them. A single request can trigger hundreds of permission checks, so correctness and performance both matter.
You'll also contribute to moving the permission model to a new authorization stack that pairs the Rails monolith with a Rust policy engine. The engine represents access relationships and evaluates permission rules, and can run within the monolith's process or be reached through remote procedure calls using gRPC. You don't need prior Rust experience: several engineers on the team learned it for this work, and we'll support you doing the same.
Some examples of our projects:
- Refactoring GitLab's policy layer so the same permission definitions can be evaluated by the monolith and the new authorization service
- Extending fine-grained token permissions to more resources, with guidance from senior engineers on the design
What you'll do
- Implement authorization changes in GitLab's Ruby on Rails monolith so permission checks allow intended access and deny unauthorized access.
- Deliver well-scoped workstreams from feature-flagged rollout through verifying that the old and new systems produce the same results, with review and guidance from senior engineers.
- Build and extend fine-grained permissions for tokens and roles so additional resources have permission coverage consistent with the established catalog.
- Extend and fix authorization enforcement so GraphQL and the REST API enforce the intended permissions consistently.
- Make incremental refactors to long-lived policy code without changing behavior for existing customers.
- Investigate and fix reliability, performance, and security issues so affected permission checks return the expected results without regressions.
- Work with the authentication, platform, and artificial intelligence (AI) teams to document interface contracts that keep permission checks consistent as authorization moves toward a shared service.
- Contribute to design documents, merge requests, and code reviews so proposed changes have a documented rationale and review feedback is addressed asynchronously.
- Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.
What you'll bring
- Solid experience building and maintaining production Ruby on Rails applications, typically gained over 2 to 4 years or more.
- Hands-on experience with authorization concepts, such as role-based access control or fine-grained permissions, from work or projects.
- A security mindset: you treat a permission bug as a security bug and consider who a change could affect before choosing an implementation.
- Experience making careful changes to existing codebases, including incremental refactors and feature-flagged rollouts that preserve existing behavior.
- Familiarity with GraphQL or API authorization patterns.
- Awareness of performance, including how repeated permission checks can add up on every request.
- Strong written communication and the ability to work effectively when most decisions happen in a document or merge request rather than a meeting.
- Helpful, but not required: hands-on PostgreSQL experience, or experience with Rust, gRPC or Protocol Buffers, Cedar or other policy languages, Zanzibar-style authorization systems, Go, or service-oriented architecture.
We welcome transferable experience from adjacent domains such as identity, policy engines, and platform security.

An overview of this role
As an Intermediate Backend Engineer on GitLab's Security Factory: Code Scanning team, you'll help developers find and fix security issues in their code by contributing to the static analysis engine that finds them.
Your work spans both the engine and the tools we use to evaluate it. You'll extend how the engine models programs, from parsing source code and resolving symbols to building call graphs and tracking tainted data across files and languages. You'll also build and apply tooling to test its findings against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities, measuring both false positives and missed vulnerabilities.
We build the engine with artificial intelligence (AI) agents that write and review code from written specifications, under human direction. You'll implement component specifications within the team's architecture, working with engineers and AI agents. Good judgment about when to trust agent output, and when to bring it to human review, is central to the role.
What you'll do
- Extend the program model, including parsing, symbol resolution, intermediate representations, call graphs, and taint and data-flow analysis, to support new languages and frameworks.
- Build and apply AI-assisted tooling to implement, review, and validate engine changes and findings, in collaboration with the team's technical leadership. Measure detection quality against known vulnerabilities, judging changes primarily on false positive and false negative rates.
- Develop static application security testing (SAST) rules mapped to Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) and the Open Worldwide Application Security Project (OWASP), along with test fixtures that demonstrate they work.
- Implement component specifications with engineers and AI agents through phased plans and small, reviewable changes. Keep specifications and code in sync.
- Improve the harness, agent instructions, and skills that keep agent-written code trustworthy. Use separate coding and reviewing agents, performance checks, application programming interface (API) checks, and dependency checks, and escalate risky changes to human review.
- Solve technical problems of moderate scope and complexity, and identify and address technical debt that slows the team down.
- Write maintainable code that meets our internal standards, and help maintain those standards through code review.
- Participate in on-call rotations to help troubleshoot product operations, security operations, and urgent engineering issues.
- Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.
What you'll bring
- Experience using AI or large language model (LLM) tools to generate or evaluate technical content, with the judgment to assess when their output is trustworthy.
- Solid professional experience writing and testing production code in a systems language, particularly Rust or Go. Our engine is written in Rust, the analyzer wrapper in Go, and the monolith integration in Ruby. You'll be willing to work across them.
- An interest in static analysis and application security, including parsing, intermediate representations, taint and data-flow analysis, and how vulnerabilities arise in code. Deep expertise isn't required; we'll help you grow it.
- Organize and progress your work independently in a remote, largely asynchronous environment.
- The ability to communicate technical problems clearly and concisely and propose iterative solutions.
- Helpful but not required: experience with performance optimization, Docker and continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), web or mobile frameworks, guardrails for agent-written code such as mutation testing and fuzzing, or program analysis and security research through publications or open source contributions. Willingness to learn performance optimization and containerized workflows is also welcome.
About the team
The Security Factory: Code Scanning team develops GitLab's SAST capabilities for customer software repositories. We work closely with the Code Security team on scanning rules and flows, with Composition Analysis on the broader software supply chain, and with other groups across the Sec section. We rely heavily on asynchronous work across time zones.
At GitLab, our mission is simple: to enable everyone to contribute to and co-create the software that powers our world.

- Own day-to-day platform operations: triage and resolve failed pipelines, infrastructure issues, and GitLab team member requests. Use monitoring, service-level agreements (SLAs), data contracts, query and warehouse tuning, and data quality checks to keep the platform reliable and cost-efficient.
- Partner with Analytics Engineers, Data Analysts, Data Scientists, Data Governance, and business partners so data lands in the shape they need for downstream use.
- Use AI coding agents such as Claude Code, OpenCode, GitLab Duo, or similar tools to speed up development, debugging, testing, and documentation without compromising review rigor.
- Apply role-based access control (RBAC) and masking policies to make governed data available to AI tools and agents. Handle data subject to Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) controls, material nonpublic information (MNPI), and personal data safely.
- Ship medium-sized features independently in small, iterative merge requests, and document architecture and runbooks in the handbook.
What You'll Bring
- Professional experience shipping production data pipelines in Python.
- Deep, hands-on SQL skills and experience with a cloud data warehouse; Snowflake is preferred.
- Hands-on experience with ELT or extract, transform, load (ETL) pipelines at scale, including incremental loads, schema changes, backfills, and API ingestion.
- Experience with orchestration tools such as Airflow, familiarity with dbt, and solid data modeling fundamentals, including Kimball dimensional modeling.
- Experience running and troubleshooting data infrastructure, with comfort using Git-based workflows, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), and code review.
- Hands-on experience using AI coding tools in your daily work, with an understanding of where they help and where they fall short.
- Clear written communication, the ability to use GitLab, and comfort working asynchronously in a fully remote organization in line with GitLab's values.
- Preferred, not required: experience with Snowflake; Docker, Kubernetes, Google Cloud Platform (GCP), or Terraform; SaaS application APIs such as Salesforce, Zuora, or Zendesk; data observability tooling; or Snowflake administration.
About the team
The Data Platform team within Enterprise Data is responsible for a scalable, reliable and secure data platform for data analytics at GitLab. That includes managing and maintaining the infrastructure we use, both SaaS and self-managed, and building and maintaining the data pipelines that bring data into it. We make data reliable, secure and ready for analytics, data science and AI tools. About the role
We are looking for a Principal Engineer to help build GitLab Duo Agent Platform, the agentic orchestration layer that runs AI agents and flows across the entire software lifecycle.
Principal Engineers at GitLab are recognized experts across multiple technology domains and represent the senior technical leadership within their organization. In this role you will set technical direction for a significant part of the Agent Platform, working across several teams to turn agentic capabilities into something engineering organizations can actually depend on: predictable, observable, governable, and fast enough to sit in the critical path of real development work.
The Agent Platform is not a single service. It spans agent execution and orchestration, flow definition and event-driven triggering, the AI Catalog through which customers discover and manage agents, model routing and evaluation, and the governance surface that decides which agents may act where and under whose identity. It runs on GitLab.com, GitLab Dedicated, and Self-Managed installations, including deployments that use self-hosted models to meet compliance requirements. You will work on the parts of that system where the hard architectural questions live, and you will do it hands-on.
This role reports into the VP of the AI Engineering organization and works closely with Engineering Managers, Staff Engineers, Product Management, Infrastructure and Security.
What you'll do
- Define the technical direction for a significant area of Duo Agent Platform across several teams, and partner with Engineering Managers and Product to turn it into a roadmap with a six-month horizon.
- Build the orchestration layer that makes agents and flows reliable: session lifecycle, tool invocation, context assembly, concurrency, retries, timeouts, and failure modes that degrade gracefully instead of stalling a developer's workflow.
- Hands on work on driving topics throughout the whole organisation from POC level, architecture to full implementation.
- Participate in Incident Management on-call rotation, to help meet availability goals for GitLab.com.
- Strong product builder and ownership mentality. Understanding of product strategy, technical strategy, delivering customer value and iteration towards a successful product
- Write clear, opinionated design documents, architecture narratives, and decision records that let other teams make aligned decisions. Ensure the architecture holds across multi-tenant GitLab.com, Dedicated, and Self-Managed deployments, including self-hosted model configurations, and respects data governance boundaries in each.
- Use the platform on our own work, find where it falls short of what we claim, and feed that back through improvements into the product.
- Mentor Staff and Senior Engineers, and raise the bar for experimentation rigor and cross-team collaboration.
- Work across the whole platform on different projects, features and teams. This reaches across:
- Design the extensibility surface so customers can build custom agents and flows, connect their own tools and internal systems, and bring external agents such as Claude Code and Codex into GitLab workflows without weakening the platform's guarantees.
- Drive down the cost and latency of agentic requests, and work with Product on how model selection, routing, and credit consumption behave as usage grows.

- Strong Linux systems administration knowledge (LFCE or RHCE equivalent), including performance analysis and low-level debugging tools.
- Practical experience with GitLab and continuous integration / continuous delivery (CI/CD), including how different deployment models and outages affect customers.
- Ability to write and maintain clear, reusable support content such as knowledge articles, runbooks, and troubleshooting guides.
- Proficiency with scripting languages (such as Ruby or Bash) and familiarity with model-view-controller (MVC) frameworks, preferably Ruby on Rails.
- Effective communication skills for explaining complex technical topics to audiences with varying technical backgrounds and for building rapport with customer stakeholders.

An overview of this role
The Trusted Agentic Development team sits within GitLab's Developer Experience group and builds the platforms our engineers rely on every day. GitLab engineers increasingly build software with artificial intelligence agents. Agents can generate code and tests in seconds, but they can also produce passing test suites for software that doesn't work as intended. As a Senior Backend Engineer, Trusted Agentic Development, you'll own the technical thesis for closing that validation gap and build the early proof yourself. You'll rethink what validation means when the author is an agent and make the feedback loop fast, automatic, and trustworthy enough that teams choose to adopt it.
- Validation that confirms agent-generated code does what was intended, so a passing suite means a working feature and not just a satisfied proxy.
- Mid-loop feedback that helps an agent self-correct toward working software instead of green assertions.
- Language-aware approaches under one shared model of what "trusted" means, starting with Rust, Ruby, and Go, while allowing the right technique to differ by language.
- Real measurement of whether engineers trust and adopt the path, fed straight back into the platform.
What you’ll do
- Own the technical thesis for how GitLab validates software when an agent is the author, and turn it into an architecture the team can build against.
- Prototype the hard parts by building early versions of feedback mechanisms that catch the gap between passing tests and working software, proving what works before the team scales it.
- Develop approaches for GitLab's primary stacks, starting with Rust, Ruby, and Go, under one shared definition of "trusted," while allowing the right technique to differ by language.
- Design the mid-loop feedback an agent needs to self-correct toward working software rather than green assertions, and build the systems that deliver it.
- Collaborate with engineering teams to adopt these approaches, measure adoption, engineer trust, and validation quality, and use those findings to improve the platform.
- Set technical direction the team can build on, review designs, and help teammates grow their technical judgment.
- Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.
What you’ll bring
- Deep, current, hands-on experience building real software with artificial intelligence agents, ideally across more than one language, and a clear understanding of why agent output can pass tests yet fail in production.
- A strong point of view on the validation gap and concrete ideas for closing it, backed by approaches you've built or tried.
- Experience designing distributed systems designed to run on Kubernetes first.
- The technical range to design systems rather than tune a single framework, and the judgment to know when a solution should be general or language-specific.
- You prototype to learn, and you ship.
- The ability to influence engineers across an organization without formal authority through working code and sound reasoning.
- Strong written communication in an all-remote, asynchronous environment.
- Alignment with GitLab's values, especially collaboration, iteration, and transparency.
This isn't a quality assurance or test automation role. We aren't looking for depth in a particular testing framework. We're looking for someone who has built with agents, experienced the validation gap firsthand, and wants to solve it.
About the team
The Trusted Agentic Development team is part of GitLab's Developer Experience group. We build platforms and practices that help GitLab engineers validate agent-generated software with confidence. We work across engineering teams and programming languages to understand how people use agents, test new approaches in real workflows, and create a shared model of trusted agentic development that teams choose to adopt.

An overview of this role
As a Senior Backend Engineer on GitLab's Security Factory: Code Security team, you help developers find and fix security issues. Those issues live in the code they write and in the open source components they depend on.
Your work spans complementary parts of a complete security analysis. On the dependency analysis side, you teach the analysis engine what a project depends on. You parse dependency manifests, lockfiles, and SBOMs so the engine knows which libraries and frameworks are in play and how the code uses them. You also extend the service that turns security advisories into automated merge requests that update vulnerable dependencies. On the vulnerability detection side, you grow GitLab's security analysis engine with hybrid analyzers that blend rule-based detection and AI reasoning. You build and apply the tooling that develops, evaluates, and ships those analyzers, and you measure how well they find real problems. That work also expands coverage of the libraries, frameworks, and AI agent tooling that real-world applications are built on.
These threads reinforce each other. What a project depends on, and how its code uses those dependencies, are parts of one picture, and this team works across all of it. We make thoughtful use of AI-assisted development tools in our daily work. We expect you to use them effectively and with good judgment.
What you do
- Act as the directly responsible individual (DRI) for team initiatives from design through delivery, shipping with minimal guidance in partnership with the technical lead
- Bring systems built by one engineer to team ownership through documentation, tests, and shared review
- Design and ship analyzers that pair deterministic analysis capabilities with AI-driven analysis, and build the evaluation harnesses that measure their false positives and missed findings against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities, raising the bar for what counts as a trustworthy result. That includes detection rules mapped to CWE and the test fixtures that prove they work.
- Package those analyzers for every place GitLab runs them, including CI jobs, AI agent workflows, and command-line tools, with findings reported in GitLab's standard security report formats
- Design and ship the manifest, lockfile, and SBOM parsing that tells the static analysis engine what a project depends on, and extend it to new ecosystems and formats
- Ship features across the automated remediation service that turns security advisories into dependency update merge requests, from sandboxed updates to merge request creation
- Solve technical problems of high scope and complexity, actively seek out difficult impediments affecting the whole team, and advocate for improvements to quality, security, and performance with Product Management, Engineering stakeholders such as Frontend and UX, and partner teams such as Code Scanning and Composition Analysis
- Mentor Intermediate engineers through code review and pairing, and maintain our internal standards for style, maintainability, and best practices through review
- Participate in on-call rotations to assist troubleshooting product operations, security operations, and urgent engineering issues
- Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it
What you bring
- Experience building your own LLM tooling, such as a harness, an agent pipeline, or evaluations, with the judgment to know when output is trustworthy and when it isn't
- Substantial professional experience writing and testing production code in a systems language, particularly Go and/or Rust, with depth in at least one. We use both, plus Ruby on the remediation side and Python for some analyzers, and value willingness to work across them.
- Familiarity with package managers and dependency management in one or more language ecosystems, such as npm, Maven, pip, Bundler, or Cargo. Experience building tooling around them is better still.
- Demonstrated application security experience, such as vulnerability research, secure code review, or writing detection rules, and fluency with vulnerability classes (OWASP Top 10, CWE) and the software supply chain
- A track record of taking ownership of ambiguous problems and shipping with minimal guidance, with the self-motivation and organizational skills suited to a remote, largely asynchronous environment
- Demonstrated capacity to communicate clearly and concisely about technical problems, and to write design proposals that bring a team to a decision
Helpful experience
- Experience evaluating AI-driven detection against labeled data, including measuring false positives and missed findings
- Experience with performance optimization at scale
- Hands-on program analysis experience, such as parsing, ASTs, or data-flow analysis
- Familiarity with popular web or mobile application frameworks and how they handle input, data, and configuration
- Experience with containerized workflows and CI/CD (we use Docker heavily)
About the team
The Security Factory: Code Security team builds GitLab's code-level security scanning capabilities, spanning static application security testing and dependency scanning. We help developers find and fix security issues in both the code they write and the open source components they depend on, as early as possible.
We work closely with the Static Analysis team on GitLab's SAST engines, with Composition Analysis on the broader software supply chain, and with other groups across the Sec Section. We rely heavily on asynchronous work across time zones.

An overview of this role
We're looking for an Intermediate Site Reliability Engineer to join the Cells Infrastructure team in GitLab's Scale & Architecture organization. In this role, you'll help build and operate Cells, the architecture that lets GitLab.com scale horizontally. Cells splits GitLab.com into many independent units, each with its own application and data stack, behind a shared routing layer.
This is a build-it-and-run-it role. You'll provision cells, route traffic to them, deploy them safely, and keep them reliable in production. You'll also help move customer organizations onto Cells, one of GitLab's most important scaling initiatives.
What you'll do
- Operate Cells in production: join the on-call rotation, respond to incidents, lead post-incident reviews, and drive corrective actions to completion.
- Define and monitor service level objectives (SLOs) for routing and cell health, and build the dashboards, alerts, and runbooks behind them.
- Provision and operate cell infrastructure on Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Google Cloud Platform (GCP), including Kubernetes, networking, Identity and Access Management (IAM), PostgreSQL, Redis, and object storage.
- Develop infrastructure as code with Terraform, Helm, and GitOps tooling such as Argo CD.
- Operate and extend the global routing layer, built on Cloudflare Workers, Envoy, and a Go service backed by Cloud Spanner, and expand routing to more protocols and services.
- Improve the continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines behind ring-based deployments, covering promotion, database migrations, quality assurance validation, and rollback.
- Support organization migrations by preparing destination cells and helping with dry runs and production cutovers.
- Work with product teams to make their services cell-compatible, and write documentation so others can operate Cells with confidence.
- Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.
What you'll bring
- Professional experience running production infrastructure at scale on AWS, GCP, or both, including Kubernetes, along with strong Terraform and Helm skills.
- Proficiency in Go, or strong experience in another systems language and willingness to work in Go daily.
- Solid grounding in site reliability engineering (SRE) best practices: SLOs and error budgets, blameless post-incident reviews, reducing toil through automation, capacity planning, and designing for graceful degradation.
- Experience owning services in production, including on-call, incident response, and monitoring with tools such as Prometheus and Grafana.
- Practical knowledge of progressive delivery: how to roll changes safely across a fleet and how to roll them back.
- A strong understanding of distributed-systems fundamentals, such as request routing, proxies, consistency, and failure domains.
- Experience working effectively in distributed, all-remote teams: you default to asynchronous, written-first communication, document decisions in issues and merge requests, hand off work cleanly across time zones, and stay transparent about progress and blockers.
- Experience with Cloudflare, Spanner, Argo CD, TypeScript, or operating GitLab at scale is a plus, not a requirement.
About the team
Every team in our organization owns its services end to end, from design through on-call.We own the control plane that tracks cells and decides where each request belongs, and keep the fleet in step with GitLab's release cadence.We work closely with delivery, database, migration, and product teams across GitLab. Feature teams own how their services behave on the platform; we own the underlying infrastructure.We're an all-remote, asynchronous team. We make decisions in GitLab issues, use directly responsible individuals (DRIs) to own technical direction, demo our work weekly, and use AI-assisted workflows every day.
